Chapter Notes

hi everyone! ヾ(≧▽≦*)o i've been teasing this fic for a while now on twitter, but it's finally here! the teacher x teacher au, hehe~

in this fic, mydei is 39 years old and phainon is 26. if that icks you out for whatever reason, don't bother reading lol. it's an age gap romance!!!

anyway, thank you so much to nina for editing, and midnight for cheering me on! couldn't have done this without you both!!!

this fic is almost completely finished being written, so i'll (try to) follow a 1-3 week upload schedule depending on how things go in between chapters.

thank you so much everyone, hope you enjoy! (´▽`ʃ♡ƪ)

Mydei doesn't think much of it when his class is one minute late.

But as the clock on his wall ticks away, signalling that now—after losing himself in deep thought over how to handle today's lesson—it's currently ten past the hour, he finally starts getting suspicious. It's normal for classes to overrun on occasion, gods, even he's even done it before. However, it's an entirely different thing when it's this much time that's gone by without any prior notice. Mydei pushes his glasses back up onto the bridge of his nose, as they've gradually slid down while he was staring at the worksheets on his desk.

He sighs, glancing at the clock once again. Two more minutes, he promises himself, and then he'll go figure out where the hells his class has disappeared off to.

In the meantime, he busies himself with sifting through worksheets. He might as well organise them now for when his class eventually turns up, after all. Mydei is beginning to get worried after this amount of time without hearing anything—he knows that nothing will have happened to them as long as they're on school grounds, but to not even get an apology or explanation email from their current teacher is making him feel slightly annoyed. Mydei checks his email inbox again one more time just to be certain, but no, there's still nothing new in there. Whoever they're with must not be aware of the time, or they're lacking in the competence area. He can't think of any teachers that he knows personally that fit either of those categories, which mystifies him even more to the situation.

The school day starts at 8:45 am, with form room ending at 9:00 am, and then leads immediately onto the first lesson of the morning which lasts an hour. Mydei at least knows that his class is already grouped up together for all their lessons, which can only mean that whatever is holding them up is happening to them all at the same time.

With another glance at the clock on the wall to check how much time has passed, he frowns when he sees that it's gone way past the original two minutes he allotted himself beforehand to wait.

At this rate, by the time the students arrive, the lesson won't even be worth teaching. He'd have no choice but to put on a history documentary of the topic they're studying this month—the Great Okhema War—which, as it turns out, the only copy he has exists in the form of a VHS tape that can only be played on an ancient TV set that's currently collecting dust in the store cupboard at the back of his classroom. Mydei's pretty sure the set is about as old as some of his student's parents now—a fact that pains him to consider—but the department head has constantly and consistently refused to invest in newer versions of the curriculum material, so this is just what he has to work with.

Mydei sighs and runs his hands through his hair, pushing the light greying strands back into place which had come loose during worrying from his high ponytail. It falls right back down into his eye, showing he'd clearly not put enough wax in his hair this morning while styling it. Everything feels like it's going wrong today: his shirt feels too tight, his trousers too short, all despite being sure—no, knowing—he'd washed them on the right settings. He's not hopeless with household chores despite what some people may assume of him, especially his father who still relies on housekeepers to do most of his chores for him. His trousers feel a little tight around his thighs, but he's lucky that the kids are usually too busy staring at the interactive whiteboard or their books to notice how today, they cut a little too high above his ankles to be passed off as fashionable.

He knows he can't sit around doing nothing for much longer, so he sets off towards reception to enquire about his student's whereabouts.

"Mr Kremnos?" Aglaea, the receptionist, says as he approaches her. She stops typing, the quick clack clack clack of her long fingernails coming to a stop. By the looks of the kid sitting in the waiting area sweating bullets, it's probably a late arrival she's noting down.

"Could I get the timetable for 11B? They've not turned up yet and it's been over twenty minutes," Mydei explains.

Aglaea looks concerned hearing that, her face creasing slightly as her eyebrows knit inwards. She nods, and begins clicking around the school's computer software to see what she can find.

"Mr Kremnos, I've found them. They're here in East Block's hall. It seems like they have P.E right now…" She squints slightly at the screen, leaning in closer as if to get a better look at some small print. "Hm, alright. I see. They've got a new teacher it seems, and from what I recall, today is his first day."

Mydei sighs. He feels like he's been doing a lot of that recently. They've all been there on their daunting first day of teaching, disorganised and trying to figure out everything all at once—but he's never heard of something quite like this happening before.

"Thanks, I'll go grab them now," Mydei replies, waving at Aglaea quickly as he leaves.

Aglaea tilts her head in goodbye without another word and goes back to typing, calling the student over so she can finish up the form for being late. Mydei heads off and wanders back down the corridor he's just come through. He's already in East Block, so the hall is only through a set of doors opposite him. He'd walked past it as he came towards reception, but he was so distracted by his own internal frustrations he didn't notice anyone even in there.

This time, as he gets closer, he realises that it is, in fact, in use. He speeds up, already seeing his class through the windows crowding around a large trampoline as someone jumps on it. It's clear as day that they're still in the middle of a lesson, and not even changed out of their P.E kits yet either. Adding that all up in his head can only mean that by the time they've cleared out and are back in their school uniforms, his period will be over and they would've missed the entire thing, all due to this new teacher's infuriating incompetence.

Even worse is that they're nearing exam season too, which is only a few months away at this point, and it's approaching so fast that even Mydei is beginning to feel the pressure of needing to cram in as much as possible to make sure he's covered all he can in order to prepare them. Studying a Great War is no small feat, and it takes a lot of time to unravel everything that happened—every cause, every consequence, every shifting alliance, and every turning point that shaped the course of the conflict. It isn't just memorising some dates or names; it's understanding why events unfolded the way they did, how the reigning leaders made their decisions, and what the outcome meant for the world that followed.

For exams, they'll need to be ready for all of it: the long-term tensions that set the stage for the war, the immediate triggers that pushed nations past the point of return, and the social and economic impacts on the populations involved. And Mydei knows that if they're going to pass—really pass, not just scrape by—they'll need to move beyond surface-level facts that they're currently at and learn to see the war the way the history exam paper markers will expect: as a complex, interconnected web of decisions, mistakes, ambitions and pressures. It's a lot to absorb, he knows, and even for his brightest students, the clock is ticking away for them.

Thinking of all this causes the anger in him to peak as he pushes the doors open, letting them bang against the wall from the force. He's prepared himself as much as possible to yell at the newcomer for not only wasting his time, but the student's time too, and that his irresponsibility is jeopardising their exams, and—

Every ounce of fight that he had leaves him in a single breath as he catches sight of the other teacher.

He's showing the students how to do tricks on the trampoline, from back flips to twists in mid-air that land him on his behind before letting physics do the rest and bounce him back onto his feet again. The grin on his face practically lights up the entire room, joyful laughter echoing in the large space as he clearly continues to enjoy himself. The teacher's soft, unstyled hair swishes and moves in a way that seemingly defies gravity each time he jumps a few feet into the air, two strands on the top of his head bouncing along with him cutely. He looks young, a lot younger than Mydei was expecting, which must mean he's potentially not only fresh on the job, but fresh out of university and teacher training too.

Mydei feels hypnotised at first, just by the way his body moves, practised in every way that shows how talented he is—so much so that it distracts Mydei from taking in the rest of him, too busy watching his performance. His mouth goes dry instantly from how much skin is on show—because he's fairly certain that the uniform the teacher is wearing would be dress coded immediately if he was a student instead. The shorts he's wearing are tiny, barely reaching mid-thigh, while everyone else has to wear knee length pairs. He's even altered his t-shirt as well, rolling the sleeves up to his shoulders and tucking them in so his arms are completely revealed.

Mydei doesn't think much to his build at first, but it's there when he flexes —muscles, so many, in his arms and legs and clearly in his torso when his dark blue shirt lifts up as he jumps around, too many abdominal muscles to count for the split second that they're on show for. Sweat completely covers his whole body, making his pale skin practically glisten silver to match his hair under the bright lights of the hall.

The kids look just as enraptured as Mydei feels as they all watch him finish his routine with a graceful flourish, light catching on him like he's stepped out of some half-remembered dream. His smile is so wide and bright that it steals the breath from Mydei's lungs, and the edges of his vision become softer, blurring, as though the world itself is quietly falling away until the only thing left in focus is the younger teacher—luminous, effortless, and too far away for him to do anything about it.

For a suspended moment, time seems to hold its breath with him. Then the sudden, exuberant applause from the students shatters the spell, pulling Mydei back to the present. The other teacher only makes the moment more surreal by dipping into a playful bow, thanking the children with that brilliant smile—as though he can't help but indulge them even further.

Mydei's earlier ire comes back in full force. Honestly, no matter how hot, charming, or… stunning the new teacher is, it still doesn't excuse how late he's made his students for his lesson. He crosses his arms over his chest, wincing internally at how tight his shirt feels across his biceps and shoulders with the movement. He'll have to check his washing machine's settings again when he gets home, maybe he put them on for too long of a wash…

Mydei clears his throat loudly, both to snap him out of his own thoughts and because no one has noticed him yet, still looming in the doorway. He forces a practised unimpressed look on his face when the teacher's attention finally snaps towards him, and oh—he was not ready for such a blazingly bright look aimed at him. The teacher's eyes are blue, so blue, with a pattern around his irises that he can't quite make out from so far away. It makes him want to get closer, to lean into his space and really see what's going on behind them.

The teacher watches him for a second, eyes wide and mouth gaping, before his mouth slams shut and confusion takes over, as if he's forgotten where he is.

"Oh, sorry! Were we too loud?" He yells, grinning and looking exactly the opposite of sorry.

His words cause the students to look over. "Mr Kremnos!" They all gasp at the same time, and they all look suspiciously sheepish at his sudden presence in the hall. He watches as a few of them glance up at the clock behind him on the wall that hangs above the doors. Ironically enough, it's the biggest clock in the whole school, impossible to miss or not be able to read no matter how bad your eyesight is. He knows his students are at least smart enough to be able to tell the damn time, and going by their guilty reactions, they had just chosen to ignore it and see what they could get away with.

Well, he won't be letting that slide, that's for sure. Mydei narrows his eyes at the other teacher, "Could you please tell me the time, Mr…?"

The teacher looks puzzled by his question and makes his way over, possibly so they don't have to yell across the room anymore. He bounds over the trampoline like an overly excited puppy, those silly two strands of hair still bobbing up and down, and comes to a stop when he's on the edge of the blue padding. He jumps down, landing with another preformative flourish that makes Mydei's lips twitch slightly.

"Just Phainon is fine," The teacher—Phainon—replies.

"So?" Mydei encourages when this Phainon isn't going to answer his other question.

Phainon runs a hand through his hair to tame it back down, and Mydei gets a waft of his scent. The smell of sweat mixed with deodorant should make him cringe and take a step back, but instead he wants to take a step forward. His eyes lock onto a stray droplet of sweat as it makes its way down Phainon's neck, only stopping in its tracks when it's absorbed into the neckline of his t-shirt. It's then that Mydei realises he's got a tattoo on the side of his neck, a blazing sun, and he for some reason wants to trace the outlines of it and see if he can feel them under his fingertips.

Mydei feels as though he's being reeled in hook, line and sinker for this man just from him standing there and looking at him. He tries very hard to claw back the iron will he's famous for around the school grounds, taking a deep breath and letting his eyes flutter closed briefly before he readies himself for another look at Phainon. He needs to ignore all the thoughts of how strong Phainon's thighs look, or how nicely defined his biceps are, or the sultry way his eyes curve up as they watch each other, all in order to continue this conversation.

Mydei clears his throat to distract himself as the silence stretches on.

"So… What?" Phainon finally asks in confusion.

Mydei feels his eyebrows twitch in annoyance. Trust him to find someone that's exactly his type, but is clearly lacking in the common sense department. "So, Phainon, would you like to explain to the year head why my students have missed their entire lesson, or should I?"

The previous bemusement in Phainon's expression completely disappears as his eyes flick up to the clock behind Mydei's head. "Oh shit—I mean, sugar! Oh sugar! Frick, I didn't realise it was that time already!" Phainon garbles, an utter train wreck that Mydei can't seem to look away from. Phainon's skin turns a pretty shade of pink, making him look even more flushed than he was when he was physically exerting himself.

Mydei doesn't even have it in him to be horrified by the language coming from a teacher while still in front of students, too occupied with the feeling of an oncoming headache as his temples twinge painfully.

"I really am sorry, um, Mr Kremnos," Phainon begins, his demeanour now matching his words as he uses the name the students said earlier. "Kids, go get changed now, quickly! I'll deal with putting the equipment away."

The kids all scarper out of the hall without wasting another second, giving Mydei nervous side glances as they run by. He's not a scary teacher by any means—or at least he hopes he isn't—but he's worked extremely hard to earn a healthy level of respect from everyone by using a firm approach to boundaries and methods. Despite this, some of the students still feel overly anxious towards him, and he's pretty sure it's more down to the fact that he rarely smiles or laughs above anything else.

"Phainon, you have to have at least one member of staff in each changing room to supervise them. Are Nikolas and Cipher even in the office right now?"

"Uh…" Phainon looks overwhelmed at his simple question. "I can go find them! I'll hurry the kids up, so you can all head back to your classroom."

Mydei pinches the bridge of his nose before pushing his glasses back into place. "You can't just leave the equipment unattended! I'll stay here while you go check in the office, and then Nikolas and Cipher can come deal with cleaning up instead. I think you and I need to have a little chat." He clicks his tongue in annoyance, feeling like he's lecturing a toddler.

Phainon looks like a wilted flower, drooping around the edges and even those strands of hair that he assumes usually stick up are curled in sadly. He makes a sorry sight overall, one where Mydei almost wants to console him and pat him on the head. Instead, he inhales quickly and surely, as seeing the way Phainon's relaxed aura has disappeared completely doesn't make him feel as righteous as he thought it would.

He leaves Phainon to stare at the floor with his thoughts for a moment, allowing Mydei to look over him again. He feels his heart rate pick up as he takes him in. He knows he shouldn't, but he can't help himself as his eyes rake appreciatively over Phainon's body and face. He has a broad set of shoulders, leading down to slim hips that are only emphasised by how tightly his t-shirt sticks to his skin. Mydei crosses his arms over his chest and shakes his head, demanding himself to remain professional. Tiny pinpricks of embarrassment erupt over his body when he realises that Phainon is staring at his biceps that are practically bulging out of his shirt at this point due to it having shrunk. He knows how ridiculous he must look because of it, but the attention on them makes him subconsciously flex his muscles.

Mydei watches as Phainon's pupils dilate as he swallows, his Adam's apple bobbing with the movement. If Mydei was ten years younger, and they weren't in the middle of a work domestic, he'd probably take that reaction and bask in it with a sly grin. Right now, though, he's only one year away from turning forty, and with his greying hair and crow's feet that are starting to set in despite his ritualistic skin care routine, he hesitates. There's some form of interest in Phainon's eyes, that's for certain, but it's probably nothing more than friendly admiration. He knows Phainon's type—gym obsessed (just like him), loud without much substance (not like him at all), and worst of all, probably straight (definitely not like him).

Mydei exhales, reeling himself back into 'teacher mode' to stop any more damning thoughts from flooding in. He's still on duty after all, and he isn't being paid to check out hot, younger men in his area, no matter how much he wants to appreciate the teacher before him.

"Phainon, you need to go make sure that Nikolas and Cipher are with the kids now. I'll supervise the hall until you're back."

Phainon jumps, his whole body reacting like he's been electrocuted. His ears turn red, and they look so warm they're practically glowing. He nods vigorously, running out of the hall without another word.

Mydei grits his teeth, frustrated at himself. He should've just stayed in his classroom, minded his own business and sent out a few enquiring emails from the safety of his desk chair instead. The kids would've arrived eventually, he assumes, and then he wouldn't have had to meet Phainon who is already turning his brain to mush.

It doesn't take long after Phainon has sorted everything out with Nikolas and Cipher to have all the students safely herded off towards the history department by one of the TA's from the art department upstairs. Mydei waves them off and tells them to sit tight in his classroom until either the bell rings, or until he rejoins them.

Phainon hides behind him like a scared child, somehow completely covered by Mydei's slightly bigger frame. He's acting as if he's quiet enough then maybe Mydei won't notice him and can get away from the incoming lecture. Just as his class disappears out of sight, Mydei rounds on Phainon immediately and pins him to the spot with a glare.

"Office. Now." Mydei demands, storming off towards the P.E office. As much as he'd love to chew him out right then and there, some students are milling about and he doesn't want it to become any more of a spectacle than it already is bound to be with his class being notorious gossips. Even if he doesn't personally report it, word alone will get back to the year head and headteacher, causing them a whole load of trouble either way.

Mydei can't help but feel a little queasy at the thought of the headteacher— his father—calling Phainon in to berate him for his mistake.

"Look, Mr Kremnos, I'm really sorry…" Phainon trails off, unsure, as soon as the office door shuts behind them. Nikolas and Cipher are handling the equipment now, so thankfully they're alone in the room.

Mydei breathes out harshly from his nose, placing his hands on his hips as he turns his back towards Phainon. He needs to try and calm down, and he can't handle this properly if he's angry. He reminds himself that he can make or break Phainon as a new teacher with how he reacts, and he really doesn't want to do anything that'll cause harm in the long run. Mydei remembers how impressionable newbies are, even he was back in the day when he first started with only his father's tutelage behind him—and he doesn't want to knock Phainon's confidence so badly that he's left with nothing to support himself.

Mydei starts slowly: "I understand that you're new. We all make mistakes, I still make them even now and I've been teaching for as long as some of these kids have been alive for. However," Mydei steels himself and turns around to face Phainon again, and the sight of his slumped shoulders makes his heart clench against his will. "However, making students miss a whole lesson without any prior warning, especially this close to exams, cannot be tolerated."

Phainon nods, shoulders caving inwards even more so than before with the weight of his words. The fight in Mydei completely disappears, as if someone blew out a candle. "I'm guessing this was your first class completely unsupervised?" Mydei asks him.

Phainon looks up, his gaze hesitant, but he nods to confirm.

Mydei shakes his head, more at himself than at Phainon. "I'll see what I can do. You won't get fired, if that's what you're worried about."

This time, Phainon's shoulders slump with relief.

Mydei continues, "Thankfully, the kids are safe and they were looked after the whole time. It's not as though you left them unattended for any period of time, correct? We just might need to work on adjusting their timetables for next week to double up on history and no P.E, but I'll liaise with their form tutor to handle that."

Phainon stays quiet, his gaze lingering on Mydei's face as though he's searching for something there. Mydei isn't sure what he's looking for—pity, maybe, or some gentler kindness—but he knows Phainon won't find either. After a long moment, Phainon's expression softens and he offers him a small, sincere smile. The sight of it stirs something in Mydei's chest he thought he'd forgotten how to feel, unfurling quietly inside him like a flower waking to the sun.

"I'll still have to report this, though," Mydei says, stomping down on the feeling inside his chest. "You'll probably be called into the head teacher's office to discuss it, but that's about it."

"Shouldn't I be the one to say something? It was my fuck up, after all," Phainon says.

"Stop swearing on school grounds," Mydei snaps, rolling his eyes behind his glasses. "I said I'd deal with it, so I will."

Mydei hopes Phainon doesn't argue. He's too exhausted after all the emotions he's been going through within the last twenty minutes since meeting the younger teacher. And he still has a full day ahead of him, much to his dismay.

"But—" Phainon begins, but Mydei waves him off.

"You can just buy me a drink as an apology for all this," Mydei says before his brain catches up with him. He feels his cheeks warm at the forced offer, and he can't tell whether he hopes that Phainon will say yes or no to him. Saying yes would only mean one thing—spending time together outside of a school setting. Saying no would save him a lot of trouble, but something deep within Mydei's gut swirls, something small yet no less dangerous: hope.

Phainon's eyes light up at that, "I used to be a bartender, y'know? How about I make you a drink instead?"

Mydei raises an eyebrow, suddenly feeling like he's about to play right into one of Phainon's whims. Hope continues to bubble low and silent inside of him as he answers, "What if you're a shit bartender?"

A shocked laugh leaves Phainon at the curse word, but he doesn't call Mydei out on it. "No way! I was the best in town, people used to flock just to see me mixing," He raises his hands in the air to imitate using a cocktail shaker, but paired with the cheeky grin on his face and the way his hands are circled around an imaginary object, the action just makes something hot pull behind Mydei's navel instead. Repulsed with himself, he shoves that feeling as far down as it can possibly go, never to see the light again if Mydei can help it.

"You're not from here, then?" Mydei questions, genuinely curious. He's not surprised, he supposes—Phainon has small town guy written all over him, having not succumbed to the big city's pressure yet to conform. People like him stick out like a sore thumb when they first move to Okhema, and Phainon is no different.

"Oh, uh, no. I'm from Aedes Elysiae, a small farming village. I only moved here a few weeks ago."

Mydei tilts his head to the side, "Never heard of it."

"I'd be more shocked if you had!" Phainon says, laughing.

"Look, then I'm going to say this to you now for your own good," Mydei begins, seriousness dripping from his words. Phainon's eyes widen and he looks minutely shocked at the tone change, but Mydei continues, uncaring: "Word gets around extremely quickly about people here, but especially if you're new—always assume everyone knows everyone, okay? You need to make sure nothing like this ever happens again."

Phainon rubs the back of his neck sheepishly at the warning. "Why do you make it sound so threatening? It's just a small city."

Mydei sighs, "It's precisely because we live in a small city that it's like this, and I don't want your reputation ruined on your first day over something like this."

"Oh," Is all Phainon says. He looks a little taken aback, but he clearly understands now. "Okay, fine. How about I pinkie promise it won't happen again?" Phainon holds up his hand, sticking his little finger out.

Mydei stares down at it, considering his choices. "I'm not some child that needs placating," He snips.

It's not a no, per se. He could easily reject it and ignore Phainon's offering, but that'd probably lead to him looking sad again, which Mydei doesn't want. Not because it makes him feel bad or anything, of course, but just because that's a lot more of a nuisance than happy Phainon.

"Never said you were, Mr Kremnos," Phainon replies, waggling his finger around. "C'mon, don't leave me hanging."

So, after a few seconds, he indulges Phainon and hooks his own pinkie around the other's.

"What am I going to do with you?" Mydei murmurs under his breath, but it's clear from the grin on Phainon's face that he heard. Phainon tightens his finger around Mydei's and gives it a firm shake before letting go.

"Yeah, yeah. You can go back to your class now. You've got…" Phainon looks at the clock on the wall beside them, "Nine minutes until the bell rings."

Mydei narrows his eyes at him, but there's no real heat behind it. "I wonder whose fault that is."

Phainon doesn't reply, instead he's laughing as Mydei walks past him. He lets their shoulders brush against each other despite there being plenty of space for them not to, and the touch alone sends a zing of pleasure down his spine. He already wants to turn around again, just to get another look at those blue eyes and pale skin, but he keeps walking instead.

Admittedly, their paths will probably never cross again. They're in two completely different departments, and at opposite ends of the school. They won't even see each other during weekly assemblies as neither of them are form tutors, and the P.E department shares the same block as the art rooms upstairs, so they have their own separate staff room to use rather than the general one near West Block. Unless Phainon wants to make the six minute walk across the school grounds to use it, then the chance of them bumping into each other is practically non-existent.

It's probably for the best, Mydei tells himself as he reaches back for the door handle, ready to pull it shut behind him. He's halfway through closing it when, without warning, the door is wrenched open from the other side. The sudden force jerks the handle in his grip and sends him stumbling backwards with a sharp gasp, completely thrown off guard. He flails for balance, but instead collides hard into something behind him—going from the loud oof he hears, he assumes that something is Phainon.

The impact knocks Mydei even more off centre than before, sending a fresh wave of chaos through the moment as the world tilts in an instant of startled, breathless confusion. Phainon exclaims in surprise again, the momentum of Mydei clashing into him making him stagger back too. Phainon reaches up to steady him, grabbing a hold of him by his biceps.

It works, and finally Mydei is stable as his heart races a mile a minute at the shock, stunning him silent. He can't do anything but blink owlishly behind his glasses as he tries to get his brain to stop rattling around inside his head from the flurry of quick movement.

He's somehow back inside the office now, the door wide open from where it was flung back against the wall. Phainon seems equally as shaken as he feels, but instead of silence he begins laughing nervously. Mydei's back is completely flush against Phainon's torso, so much so that he can feel every ridge and bump of muscle and each shaking breath he takes as he calms down. Phainon squeezes his hands around Mydei's biceps in what he thinks is supposed to be his attempt at comforting him, but he still doesn't let go.

Mydei clears his throat, desperate to get out of Phainon's hold and away from his curious hands, but Phainon cuts him off before he can say anything.

"Whoa," Phainon whispers, sounding distracted as the tips of his fingers dig into Mydei's skin through his shirt. "You're seriously ripped, Mr Kremnos." His touch toes the line between pain and pleasure, and it makes something blazing hot churn inside his stomach.

"Phainon," Mydei grinds out, hoping the younger teacher will hear the warning in just his name alone and let him go. He can't tell if Phainon is making fun of him or just being incredibly obtuse to their positioning, and living up to his earlier assumption of him being loud without much substance between his ears.

He doesn't get a reply, but instead feels an appreciative sigh brush past his ear that makes goosebumps ripple across his body. Mydei's eyes widen and his lips part in shock as his cheeks turn red, and he has to leave immediately before he does something stupid. Something stupid like pushing Phainon up against the stupid door and pinning him there, forcing him to keep those stupid wandering hands to himself so Mydei can do something else even more stupid, like lean in and—

Phainon practically throws himself back suddenly, but thankfully Mydei has plenty of core strength to stop himself from falling back again. He stands up straight, brushing invisible lint off his shirt; a motion that he only does to help ground himself after he feels his whole world has been turned on its axis.

He glances over his shoulder to glare at Phainon for his reckless actions, but he's so red in the face it almost looks painful.

"I, um, just wanted to say thanks. For having my back on this."

Mydei grits his teeth and wills his own blush to disappear already, and for his treacherous beating heart to stop. He faces forward so Phainon can't see his face, and they're far away enough now that there's no way he'll be able to hear his heart racing. "Just make sure the drink you make me is extra good."

Phainon laughs, and while he still sounds embarrassed, the tension in the room dissipates. "Alright, deal. You'll have to tell me what stuff you like so I can make it for you."

"Hmph," Mydei says, already beginning to walk out the room. "You'll have to take a guess for yourself. Good luck with your next class." He finishes, not bothering to wait for Phainon to reply as he briskly makes his way back to his classroom.

He makes it back to his classroom within record time, practically skidding through the doorway, and the moment he steps inside, the silence hits him. His students sit frozen, unnervingly well-behaved, and not a single one of them dares to make eye contact. He thanks the TA as they slip out—finally freed now that he's returned—then he turns his attention back to the room.

They're all in their assigned seats for once, which would be impressive if they didn't look like they were waiting for a firing squad. Their backs are so straight it's almost painful to look at, every kid braced for doom as if he's about to announce a mass expulsion of the entire class.

Mydei sighs softly and presses two fingers to his temple, rubbing slow circles in an attempt to chase away the tight band of tension already forming. He can feel the beginnings of a headache lurking—one of those unwelcome ones that seem to appear more and more often these days, triggered by barely anything at all. Getting older, he's learned, means migraines don't need dramatic reasoning anymore; they just show up uninvited at the slightest hint of disorder… and, frankly, he teaches plenty of that.

"Can someone tell me your P.E teacher's surname, please?" Mydei asks once he's standing in front of them all, his hands now settled low on his hips.

The class all look between themselves, a few of them putting up their hands shakily. Mydei points at a random one.

"He's called Mr Khaslana, sir," She says quietly.

Mydei nods in thanks and continues, "I'm guessing you all knew Mr Khaslana's class had run over." He doesn't get a response to that, which he was expecting. "To be clear, none of you are in trouble. It's Mr Khaslana's duty to manage his time better, not yours. So you can all calm down."

It's clear that's what the students were hoping to hear, and their spirits lift immediately. Suddenly, the room is buzzing with activity.

"We were just having fun, Mr Kremnos! We would've felt bad if we had to cut him off," One of the students says, making Mydei's eyebrow twitch. Why do they make it sound like their teacher is an overly energetic dog rather than a fully grown adult?

"And he was hot," One of the girls at the back chimes in, causing her friend group to all begin giggling and talking amongst themselves. The volume in the room suddenly skyrockets with the debate surrounding Phainon's looks, everyone apparently needing to add in their agreements to the statement.

Well, Mydei can't disagree with what they're all saying, but he isn't going to let it slide, either.

"Alright, save that kind of talk for break time!" Mydei says, raising his voice to be heard above the student's chattering. Phainon has caused more of a stir than Mydei originally thought, but looking at their faces it was a good thing instead. They haven't looked this carefree since they were freshly back from the summer holidays, so seeing them all buzzing with something that isn't nervous energy about exams has Mydei's heart softening a little.

The bell rings a few seconds later, signalling the end of his class. The students all begin to stand up to leave, but Mydei holds his hand up.

"I didn't say you could all leave just yet. Sit back down."

The class harmonises in their groans at being kept, but they all sit back down dutifully anyway.

Mydei rolls his eyes at their dramatics, "You'll all have to make up for the lesson you missed today—" An uproar cuts him off, but he shushes them immediately. "Gods, I'm not asking you all to stay after school. I don't want to stick around with any of you either."

That garners a few laughs, of which Mydei is secretly very proud of. Maybe the laid back atmosphere of Phainon's lesson has rubbed off on him as well.

"We're closing in on exams now. Whilst physical activity is important, you don't have any studying for that to do. Next week your timetables will be altered, and instead of P.E you'll be coming straight here for a double lesson. I'll let your tutor know and they'll send out the temporarily amended sheets to you all."

The class remains silent, some bobbing their heads in understanding, but most of them are clearly waiting to see if Mydei has anything else to say.

"Alright, clear off, you lot. I'll see you on Wednesday."

The class bustles with noise and movement, their voices layering on top of each other as they all shout their goodbyes and various farewells until his classroom is empty again. Mydei watches as the last one leaves, the door slamming shut behind her. He flops down into his desk chair, leaning back in it so he can stare up at the ceiling.

He already wants to see Phainon again.

Chapter Summary

His eyes scan over the document a few times, cataloguing every conflicting period or times where they're both free. Maybe he can come up with an excuse? Like suddenly visiting Cipher who he's best friends with (her words, not his) and have an impromptu catch up with her while Phainon is in the P.E office at the same time. Then, they'd get talking, and then—

Ah, who the fuck was he kidding?

A wave of grounding realisation washes over him as it suddenly sets in what exactly he's been doing: sitting in bed before 8pm, going crazy over a timetable of a guy he'd only met once and who is, he assumes, practically half his age.
