"Oh, Mr Kremnos, good morning. You're early today," Aglaea says from behind the receptionist desk.

Mydei nods at her and rubs his cold hands together, wishing he brought his gloves with him. He'd left them at home and hadn't thought about how chilly it was this morning until he was already in the car and starting the engine. He'll live, he supposes, as he can just turn the heating up in his own classroom until he thaws back out again.

"Good morning," He greets, walking over to her to sign in for the day.

"Actually, if I could have a moment of your time, I have something for you," Aglaea says, standing up elegantly from her seat as she turns around to grab something from the printer beside her. Mydei's eyebrows rocket upwards in curiosity—it's not often, if ever, that Aglaea ever stops him for anything more than a quick 'good morning' greeting, and certainly not for anything to give him.

She pushes the glass screen open between them and slips a piece of paper over towards him. Mydei looks at her before looking down at it, and his eyes widen when he sees that it's a timetable. "Oh, is this the new one for my students?" He asks.

"No, I'm afraid not. That's going out later today. This is Mr Khaslana's timetable."

Mydei frowns at her in confusion but picks the timetable up anyway, peering down at it over his glasses to read the bold print. The name at the top reads Phainon Khaslana, confirming it is indeed his timetable. "Has he already lost his?" Mydei asks.

"No," Aglaea replies simply. "I thought you'd might want to have it."

Mydei pauses, glancing up at her curiously. "Why's that?"

"Well," Aglaea begins, sitting down again in her desk chair. "Mr Khaslana has been around here a few times asking after you, so I gave him your timetable. I hope you don't mind—"

Mydei shakes his head, mind racing. Phainon was looking for him? What for? Why? And how does that correlate to Aglaea giving him Phainon's timetable? "I don't mind, I just don't understand."

Aglaea hums, a small smile curling at her lips. She always seems like she knows something he doesn't, and this time it's a lot more obvious than usual. "I think he's looking for a friend, and you're the perfect person to guide him."

"Me?" Mydei says incredulously. He puts down the timetable and slides it back over to Aglaea, "I don't need this. Shred it."

Aglaea pushes it back towards him. "That'd go against the wasteful printing policy. It's already there, so just take it. Maybe you'll be able to sync up on your free periods together."

"You—" Mydei sighs sharply, a twang of pain going through his temples. He lets his shoulders drop, and takes back the piece of paper, handling it like gold. "Fine."

"Thank you, Mr Kremnos. I hope you have a great day," Aglaea says, perfectly pleasantly.

Mydei nods, "You too," And takes his leave, staring down at the timetable in apprehension.

The afternoon following Monday morning's fiasco goes smoothly. Mydei doesn't bump into Phainon at any point—not like he wants to anyway, he has to keep telling himself—but he's starting to get restless. Every time he gets a glimpse of the colour deep blue, the same shade as Phainon's P.E uniform, his heart rate doubles immediately until it falls again when he realises it isn't him.

Currently, he's drafting the email to send to the headteacher and the year head to officially inform them of what happened yesterday. He finds the year head's email quickly, Miss Caenis being relatively near the top of the contact list. He scrolls further down until he reaches K, watching the cursor hovering menacingly over his own father's name next to the 'headteacher' title. Mydei isn't sure if Phainon has an email set up just yet, and can't find him on the staff contact list either. He knows he can just Cc Cipher in instead and ask her to let Phainon know, but as he sits there staring at the blank email, he finds that he just wants to see Phainon even more.

There's technically nothing stopping him from doing that—especially after this morning. He feels the paper timetable like a lead weight in his pocket, burning a hole through his trousers and singeing his skin with shame. He sighs, removing his glasses for a few moments to rest his eyes before he forces himself to finish the email. In the end, he copies Cipher in and leaves a note at the bottom to let her know to pass it onto Phainon whenever she can.

He wants to show his father that he's capable in his role, that he can fix not only his own mistakes but other's too without needing any guidance. He hopes that whatever he's managed to type out in the email lessens the blow for both of them. The risk of being called into the office makes him feel a little off centre, but the thought of Phainon going in there alone makes him feel even worse. He presses send quickly and relaxes back into his chair, and tries to ignore his brain shouting at him to seek the younger teacher out and his impending headache.

He's not going to listen to that little voice no matter how loud it tells him off.

Subject: Late class

To: Eurypon Kremnos, headteacher / Caenis, year head

Cc: Cipher, P.E teacher

—

Hello all, I'm emailing to report an incident which occurred yesterday morning. During first period, Mr Phainon Khaslana accidentally ran over the allotted time and disrupted my lesson so nothing was taught. We are altering the student's timetables next week to rectify this issue by doubling up on history and reducing their P.E lessons temporarily.

Thank you,

Mydei Kremnos

History department @ Chrysos Secondary School

(Cipher, if you could let Phainon know about this email and its contents, I'd much appreciate it.)

Mydei sits in bed, the covers pulled up to his waist as he stares down at the offending piece of paper. He hadn't found the courage to open it up on school grounds, too paranoid that for some reason it would cause Phainon to burst through his doors and interrogate him on why he has a copy of his schedule, despite it not even being his fault that he has it in the first place. Honestly, what was Aglaea thinking?

The lamp on his bedside table is probably too dim for reading now, especially with how bad his eyesight is getting, but he perseveres. At this point in his life, Mydei honestly thought ageing would be the least of his troubles. By now, he'd hoped to have settled down with a husband and a legion of cats and be happy enough with his partner to be distracted from the silver streaks in his hair and his aching bones.

That's all he really wanted, despite how much his father had tried to drive him away from it to focus on his career instead. He always expected Mydei to take over the school as the next headteacher, or at least become a member of the board so the family could remain holding the majority of influence over it like they'd been doing for the past fifty years.

That vision had never suited him, nor interested him, no matter how many times he tried to bend and break himself in order to make it happen—all to satisfy his father. It hadn't interested him when he was a child, being brought up to be a strong leader, and it hadn't interested him when he started teacher training either, too focused on wanting to get his degree for becoming a history teacher instead. That's where his real passion lies—in history, in what it tells the future generations and how it shapes the world. He loves working with his students too, old enough to behave but still young enough to have a chance to change.

In the end, the only thing Mydei is still willing to give his father is to remain in the education sector, but he rescinded his agreement of taking over. Regardless, as Mydei is practically forty and the other doesn't seem to be slowing down well into his sixties, it doesn't look like something is going to happen anyway. His father seems to run on nothing more than spite and greed to keep his title of headteacher, and the oversized and extravagant leather chair he sits on in his office is nothing short of a 'throne'.

Well, it seems that neither of them get what they want in the end. Mydei doesn't have a husband and cats, and his father doesn't have a willing heir. So as far as Mydei's concerned, they're even.

He brings Phainon's timetable closer to his face, squinting at the small font and tilting it more towards the light so the shadows don't completely hide it. Mydei isn't even sure what he's going to do with this knowledge anyway. He could know Phainon's whereabouts by heart and it still wouldn't change a thing—the fact that they'd maybe only have a few chance encounters over the years but nothing more. He's not willing to go out of his way to 'bump' into Phainon or orchestrate anything unnatural, no matter how much he's tempted to.

His eyes scan over the document a few times, cataloguing every conflicting period or times where they're both free. Maybe he can come up with an excuse? Like suddenly visiting Cipher who he's best friends with (her words, not his) and have an impromptu catch up with her while Phainon is in the P.E office at the same time. Then, they'd get talking, and then—

Ah, who the fuck was he kidding?

A wave of grounding realisation washes over him as it suddenly sets in what exactly he's been doing: sitting in bed before 8pm, going crazy over a timetable of a guy he'd only met once and who is, he assumes, practically half his age.

Mydei groans, covering his face as if to block out the shame. He winces at how smudged his glasses are going to be from that, so he tosses them along with the timetable vaguely in the direction of his bedside table before turning the lamp off. He ignores the sound of his glasses hitting the floor as he burrows under his duvet.

Mydei's shame from that night doesn't ease off, and it only gets worse as the days pass until it's finally Friday.

He climbs out of his car, flinging the door shut and locking the door behind him before he realises he's left his satchel in the passenger seat. He sighs, pressure building up behind his eyes from lack of sleep and the sharp spike of anger at his actions. He's already done with the day, wanting to go home and snuggle up under a blanket and read a good book. He's glad he mostly has free periods today so he can ruminate in peace over his woes. Mydei walks around the other side of the car, unlocking it again before snatching his bag up with a little bit too much force than was needed. Mydei finishes it off by slamming the car door shut even harder than before.

"Damn, what did the car do to you?" A voice comes from behind him, making him jump slightly. He turns around quickly on the balls of his feet, heart pounding from the scare until he catches sight of who it is—and then his heart is pounding for an entirely different reason.

"Uh oh, what's that look for? Are you still mad about Monday?" Phainon winces, and all Mydei can think about is the fact that he's in those stupid tiny shorts again, even in the middle of the coldest spring they've had in decades. Phainon's legs are completely bare, and the only thing that can provide him any amount of warmth is the socks that come up to mid-calf and the thin hoodie he's got on, but even that's left undone.

An icy wind whips around them, and Mydei shivers even under a thick winter coat and scarf.

"Uh… Mr Kremnos?" Phainon says hesitantly, adjusting the strap of his backpack that's slung over one shoulder. With his other hand, he waves it in front of Mydei's face. Mydei snaps out of it, but in a knee jerk reaction he glowers at Phainon. "Alright! Sorry, I'll go." Phainon throws his hands up in surrender, taking a few steps back to leave.

Panic instantly sets in within Mydei's stomach, making it feel as though he's standing on the precipice of a ravine with nowhere to go but forward. "No, wait," He pinches the bridge of his nose and scrunches his eyes shut to give himself a few moments to gather his thoughts. "It's just been a rough morning."

Phainon hums as if he understands, but the sound is distant from how far away he is now. He looks unsure if he should approach again. Mydei makes the decision for him and presses the button on his car keys to lock his doors before he takes a step forward, closing the distance spanning between them.

Mydei realises this is it—the chance he's so desperately been waiting for; the one where he finally has Phainon in front of him and hopefully willing to stick around to chat for a bit.

"How have your classes been going?" Mydei asks, figuring this is the safest bet to start a conversation.

Phainon grins, his face brightening as he sheds the previous uncertainty. "Good! No one's been late since, at least. I even have a timer set now so that I don't run over again." He laughs, clearly still embarrassed by what happened.

Mydei raises an eyebrow, slightly impressed. "Very forward thinking of you, Mr Khaslana."

Phainon's cheeks turn rosy at his praise, a small smile forming on his face instead of the beaming one. It's no less blinding though, making Mydei's insides feel like they've been scrambled up and left all out of place.

"Oh, thanks. I made a joke to Cipher about it, but she said it was actually a good idea. The kids make fun of me for it every single time, but I suppose that's how they are at that age!"

Mydei feels every unpleasant feeling in him slip away from being around Phainon—this morning's stress and the hours he spent tossing and turning agonising over what he should do completely washes away in the face of Phainon's sunny smile. It warms him up from the inside out, making his thick coat and scarf feel like too much now that he's here. Sweat pinpricks at his hairline.

"You say that, but you can't be much older than them," Mydei replies.

"Hey, I'm not that fresh out of school. I'm 26, which to them means I'm practically in my grave," Phainon says, chuckling lightly.

Mydei scoffs, "You haven't heard anything yet until they start making fun of you for turning grey."

"Are you going prematurely or something?" Phainon asks, tilting his head slightly to the side. It's clear that delicacy isn't one of his strong suits.

"I'm 39, Phainon. I think I'm well within my rights to start going grey," Mydei replies, shaking his head slightly, his braid swishing to and fro with the action. He prefers to keep his hair up in a bun while he's at work, but today he decided to leave it down and do his tried and true classic braid up for comfort.

Phainon blinks a few times at him, cheeks reddening. "Oh," He says softly, more to himself than Mydei. "I think it suits you, y'know? You've got that whole suave gentleman vibe going on. Plus, I can barely see it, your blonde hair is already so light."

Mydei doesn't want to touch that with a ten foot pole. Phainon is 26—that's 13 years between them, which is how old the majority of his students are.

"Anyway," Mydei begins, trying to change the topic while ignoring the jittery feeling in his stomach. He looks Phainon up and down in continued bafflement. "Aren't you cold? Why are you wearing shorts when it's barely even two degrees out?"

Phainon rolls his eyes as though he's being told off by a parent, and Mydei belatedly realises he's slipped into the tone he uses with naughty students.

"I would ask if you're warm, but considering how terribly you've tied your scarf, I'd be surprised if you said yes."

"Excuse me?" Mydei replies, eyes wide as he reaches up self-consciously to touch his scarf, "What's wrong with it?"

Phainon stares at him dead on, making Mydei bristle at the judgement. He wants to argue, to settle into the challenge that's clearly being presented to him by the younger teacher—but he has to remind himself that he's the older one, that he's supposed to be setting an example and leading the other. Still, he grits his teeth, but his eyes go wide in shock when Phainon makes a grab for his scarf. It catches him off guard when he uses the grip on it to haul him a few steps closer, their shoes nudging each other as their chests bump. It reminds him of Monday when he'd gone falling back into Phainon's chest like some fair maiden swooning, and a frustrated red blooms across his cheeks at the thought.

"HKS!" His mother tongue curse word slips out on accident, and Phainon looks up at him in shock.

"What was that? Hai—" Phainon tries to repeat it, but the intonation is all wrong.

"HKS," Mydei repeats slowly, cutting him off. "It means scoundrel in Kremnoan."

"Oh?" Phainon grins cheekily, giving Mydei's scarf a few playful tugs. "I'm a scoundrel to you?"

"You're definitely something," Mydei responds gruffly, clicking his tongue in annoyance.

Mydei stands stock still, but Phainon shuffles backwards a little to give them both some room. It's too late to do anything, so Mydei stays where he is, staring at Phainon instead as there's not really anything else to look at, not that he's complaining much.

He's usually a lot more precise about his appearance, almost to a concerning degree, but this morning was one thing after another and he'd just chucked the apparent offending item on without thinking too much about it. Mydei definitely hadn't thought he'd bump into anyone this early, let alone bump into Phainon specifically.

Phainon begins fiddling around with the material, unravelling it carefully before redoing it. "Do you still need your mother to dress you or something?" He asks teasingly.

"My mother's dead," Mydei replies flatly.

Phainon's hands pause in their movements for a split second, but he carries on after as if nothing happened. Mydei cringes internally, unsure of why he said it so bluntly and harshly that it inadvertently shut Phainon out. It was going so well, too, well—he thinks it was, anyway; despite cursing at the younger teacher.

"Sometimes Cipher likes to do it for me, though."

Somehow, that's worse than anything he could've said. He should've just stayed quiet and let the moment pass, but now Phainon probably thinks he's a pathetic old man who can't do anything by himself, and—

Phainon's hands are shaking so much that he can't carry on, and Mydei realises he's laughing. At him.

"What a baby! Maybe I swooped in at the right moment to save you from this dreaded scarf then, hm?" Phainon says, and his eyes practically glitter with mischief in the low early morning sun.

"Cipher likes messing around, and that includes disrupting my appearance," Mydei deadpans, ignoring the burning of his cheeks as Phainon continues to crack up.

"She always ruffles my hair," Phainon replies, pouting slightly. "But that's how she shows her love, right?"

"We assume so, yes," Mydei says, a small smile forming on his face as he remembers how she used to do that with Castorice, their literature teacher, before they got together, figuratively and literally pulling on her pigtails to make her notice her.

"Alright, Mr Kremnos, I think your scarf is almost all ready to go," Phainon says, glancing down at it again to do any finishing touches, tidying up the knot so it sits nicer against the base of his throat.

Mydei can't stop looking, eyes trailing slowly all over Phainon's face. From this angle, Mydei can see how long his white eyelashes are as he looks down, fanning delicately across his lash line. He spots a little dip in the skin between his eyebrows, so small that at a distance it wouldn't be noticeable, but from this close he can see the scar clearly. Mydei wonders where it came from—how long he's had it for, what caused it. He also wonders if he traced his fingertips across it, would he be able to feel it under his touch? Or is it so shallow that he wouldn't feel it at all?

He suddenly feels overheated, and he's not sure if it's just because his scarf is done up properly now or because of his wandering thoughts. Mydei had hoped that the next time he saw Phainon, the things he felt during their first meeting was just a fluke—that he was just caught up in a multitude of other emotions and things got horribly crossed along the way. As he watches Phainon, though, with his little furrow between his brows and the slight pout he has on as he concentrates, he feels that pull begin to bubble up again.

Phainon glances up at him, startling Mydei out of his reverie. He's finally finished tying his scarf, giving it a few satisfactory pats before moving backwards, once again broadening the distance between them. Mydei hadn't realised how warm Phainon was pressed up against him until it's gone, causing a chill to set in. Phainon gestures his hand towards the scarf to make Mydei look at it, to which he can only blink down at it in awe at how nicely it's tied. He wasn't expecting that.

"You still owe me a drink," Mydei says instead of thanking him.

"You're welcome," Phainon replies, stressing the words sarcastically. "I'm sure you win all the ladies over with manners like that."

"I don't—" like women, is what he wants to say, but he's cut off by Cipher as she comes barrelling out of the reception doors and runs to them within record speed.

"Phainon!" She yells, skidding to a stop beside them. "What are you doing out here? We have a department meeting in five minutes!"

Phainon's eyes widen in shock, making it clear that he'd obviously forgotten about it.

"Oh no, I thought that was next week. See you later, Mr Kremnos!" Phainon waves a hasty goodbye as Cipher grabs onto his wrist and drags them back into the building.

Mydei stands in the same spot for a few moments longer, letting their interaction settle in. Phainon is the human equivalent of a bull in a china shop—rushing head first through every interaction and leaving a mess of destruction and confusion behind him. At least, that's how it's been for both their meetings, Mydei surmises as he ponders on it. He's starting to feel like being out of his depth while around Phainon is going to become a common thing in the long run, if they ever meet again.

Mydei shakes himself out of it and looks down at his wristwatch, cursing under his breath when he sees the time. His morning routine is completely ruined from the impromptu meeting with Phainon, something that he can't even be mad about as he rushes towards his classroom, giving Aglaea a quick wave as he passes her. He now only has ten minutes instead of thirty to set everything up, which means cutting some corners and hoping for the best. He should be angry, he knows he should. He should be doing a lot of things—like probably holding a festering grudge against Phainon for causing him a slew of unneeded stress, but when he reaches to take his scarf off, he can't bring himself to unravel it.

It stays exactly where it is, firmly and neatly tied around his neck, tucked gently between the lapels of his suit jacket, even as his class comes flooding through the doors.

Done with the first half of the day, Mydei strolls into the staffroom for his lunch break. He gives the room a once over to see who's already in there, and spots Castorice and Cipher sitting at the corner table by the window, huddled up together as they look at something on Cipher's phone.

Mydei makes himself a cup of tea before walking over, taking his time to let the tea leaves steep in the hot water before taking them out. He dumps a few teaspoons of sugar into it and fills the rest of the mug with milk, putting it back in the mini fridge between the counters. He places the mug on the table before sitting down. Castorice and Cipher both look up at him at the same time, scarily in sync as usual. Mydei grimaces at the action before he peers over the phone they're both holding onto to see what they're looking at.

"Tut tut, nosey!" Cipher chastises, putting away her phone before he can see it.

"I don't care anyway," Mydei snaps back. Castorice smiles while Cipher frowns, and he mirrors Castorice's expression towards her immediately. "How are your students doing, Cas? They had mocks today, right?"

Castorice shrugs minutely, "Same old, as usual. They're still arguing over which sonnets they do and don't like, but at least they're passionate about it!" She clasps her hands together enthusiastically. "How about your students?"

"They're fine. Still struggling over some of the concepts which is to be understood—I'm still fighting the department head to try and get a damned DVD player into the classroom rather than that ancient thing we're still using. It's a nightmare." He takes a quick sip of his tea. "I offered to bring one in myself, but they threw a fit over electrical safety and said it had to be one they sourced themselves."

Castorice looks at him with sympathy, while Cipher gives him a Cheshire-like grin. "Are we competing for this now? I asked the office to schedule a bike trip around the local area so the kids could stretch their legs properly, but they said it wasn't relevant. We're having to use the track field instead to ride on."

Castorice and Mydei look at Cipher together before nodding. "I still think I win," Mydei says, to which Cipher sticks her tongue out at Mydei childishly.

"Mydeimos, why are you still wearing your scarf?" Castorice asks, staring at it like it's the most curious thing on the planet.

Mydei feels his ears go a little warm. "I'm cold."

Castorice and Cipher both glance at each other, communicating silently in a way that Mydei has forced himself to stop being jealous of. Despite their clashing personalities sometimes, they stick together like glue, and their way of speaking without any words is a learned skill with almost seven years of them being together.

"Uh huh…" Cipher says, unconvinced. "Did you get laid or something?"

"What?! No!" Mydei exclaims, voice too loud for the quiet room. He looks around, but thankfully no one else is paying them any attention despite his outburst. "Why would you even say that?" Mydei groans, starkly reminded that he hasn't gotten 'laid', as Cipher put it, in a long, long time.

He's clearly given them the wrong reaction because Castorice and Cipher now both look like sharks smelling blood in the water. Castorice squints at him accusingly, her eyes flickering between his steadily warming face and scarf. "It never usually looks that good."

"I dunno, maybe you're hiding hickeys? You usually leave a few buttons of your shirt undone unless you're wearing a tie, so…" Cipher trails off, imitating Castorice and surveys Mydei's appearance. "You're right. Did someone tie it for you?" The words drip with suggestion, much to Mydei's dismay.

Mydei clears his throat and sits up straight, correcting his posture the best he can and pushes his shoulders back. "Is it so unbelievable that I could've just tied it like this myself?"

"Yes," Castorice and Cipher both say at the same time.

"You both are awful," Mydei replies, deflating. "The new P.E teacher did it for me," He admits, giving in under their scrutiny. He knows Cipher especially wouldn't let up without a proper answer, and it's even worse with the addition of Castorice whose natural curiosity will lead her to hunt down the answer until she's satisfied.

Both their eyebrows shoot up their foreheads, clearly not expecting to have an answer so quickly.

"Are you talking about Phainon?" Castorice asks incredulously.

It's his turn to be shocked, "You know him?"

Castorice giggles, which is never a good sign. "I've heard all about Mr Khaslana, yes. My students all adore him and keep telling me about their lessons with him. They're just trying to buy time, but it's amusing nonetheless."

"Oh, I see," Cipher says suddenly, leering at Mydei. "So that's why you two were so cuddled up this morning, hm? He was—" She makes air quotes. "—Tying your scarf."

"That's quite literally all we were doing," Mydei shoots back quickly.

"Mhm, sure," Cipher drawls, winking at him. "You needed to be pressed up against each other for all that?"

Castorice's eyes start to sparkle, which means wherever this conversation is going is a bad turning. "No—"

"Oh, my," Castorice gasps, her hands flying up to her mouth to cover it. "You're blushing!"

"Because you two are embarrassing me!" Mydei says, flopping back in his chair, posture ruined. He sighs, tugging at the scarf to loosen it.

"No, don't take it off! I think it's sweet, don't you, Cipher?" Castorice says, giving her girlfriend a quick nudge with her elbow to encourage her.

"Yep, real sweet," Cipher says, eyes narrowing as her grin spreads. Mydei takes a sip of his drink, lukewarm now, and grumbles about it and Phainon being annoying under his breath. "So when are you gonna let him fuck you?"

Mydei gapes, freezing half-way while trying to put his mug down. "I just said he was annoying."

Cipher laughs as if Mydei had said something really funny, "Then why would you let him anywhere near you? Let alone let him tie your scarf?"

Mydei finishes putting his mug back down onto the table, albeit a little shakily. "He didn't give me a choice! He just did it without asking."

Cipher stretches her hand out suddenly, going straight for his scarf with a manic look on her face, her fangs out. Mydei doesn't think twice before smacking her hand away.

"Right, sure! I'll say again, when are you gonna ask him out?" Cipher asks, pursing her lips to fend off her smile.

"You changed the question," Mydei glares venomously at her. "Why did it go from fucking to dating?"

"I don't know, you tell me, little prince~" Cipher sing-songs vaguely.

Mydei hates his friends. No, really, he does. He swears it, because now even Castorice is laughing at him, quietly chuckling behind her hands as if he can't see and hear her both. He sighs, opening his mouth to defend himself when there's a knock at the door, cutting all the chatter out in the room. Mydei immediately assumes it's a student wanting to speak to one of them, but he doesn't bother moving as he hears one of the other teachers closer to the door get up to answer it instead.

He ignores the quiet sound of pleasantries as he focuses back on his friends, ready to down the rest of his tea before heading out back to his classroom to set up for later today.

"Um, okay. Hang on then. Mr Kremnos?"

Mydei turns around at his name, spotting a TA for the geography department by the door. "Someone's asking for you," She says now that she has his attention.

He nods, surprised that any student from his classes is bothering him during lunch time. He waits for her to move out of the way so he can at least get a glimpse of who it is before he gets up. The TA shifts a little, and Mydei catches sight of a pair of blue shorts that he's been conditioned to desperately seek out.

"Phainon?" He says, a little breathlessly, as he immediately stands up from his chair. Castorice and Cipher jerk backwards in their seats so they can peer around Mydei, and all the sudden attention makes the TA nervously run off back to her table.

Phainon stands there, in his stupidly tight t-shirt and his stupidly short shorts, looking somewhat shy.

"Hey," Phainon says, giving him a short wave before letting his arm drop back down to his sides.

"Is everything okay?" Mydei asks, walking over to the door, his terrible friends and his half-drunk cup of tea forgotten.

Phainon nods, but his face doesn't convince him of that answer.

"Do you need me for something?" Mydei questions when Phainon doesn't say anything else. They're both standing in the doorway now, and Mydei realises he's only an inch or so shorter than Phainon.

Phainon glances at him and then looks away, chewing at his bottom lip. Mydei is progressively getting more and more confused and concerned as time goes on, and it only doubles when Phainon mumbles something that he doesn't quite hear, only catching one word:

"Lost?" Mydei repeats.

"Yes, lost," Phainon replies.

Mydei stares at him, signalling he didn't hear the rest.

"I… got lost," Phainon says, barely loud enough to be heard, but Mydei finally catches it this time.

"You got lost?" Mydei parrots, feeling rather lost himself as to how that explains anything about why he was needed here in the first place.

"Yes, I got lost. How many times should we keep saying it? I've never had to leave East Block before," Phainon huffs, folding his arms.

"Alright. Where did you get lost trying to get to?" Mydei asks, purposely emphasising on the word just so Phainon would shoot him a glare. It works, and Mydei feels a grin curling at the corner of his lips.

"I got called in to see, um… Mr Kremnos… Senior…?" Phainon replies unsurely, stumbling over his words.

Mydei sighs, "You can just call me Mydeimos when it's away from the students. It's easier."

Phainon's whole visage brightens, his shoulders lifting up as his back straightens and a grin plasters itself over his face. "Sure, Mydei-mos!"

"No— no, you're saying it wrong. It's like this—"

Phainon laughs, cutting him off. "Sorry, sorry. You had such a serious look on your face it was funny. Is that why all the students are half-scared of you?"

"They're not scared of me, they respect me."

"They do," Phainon replies, his grin softening. "Hmm, can I just call you Mydei instead, please?"

Mydei sighs, adjusting his glasses on his nose. "Fine. If it stops you butchering my full name, then go ahead."

"Cool, Mydei! Anyway, I need to get to Mr Kremnos's room, and I know it's around here somewhere, and—" Phainon pauses mid-sentence, his expression turning stunned. "—Wait, why are you still wearing your scarf?"

Mydei feels a wave of humiliation go over his body, flustered beyond belief at being called out again over it. He rips it off, bundling it up into his fist before he chucks it onto one of the tables close by. The cold air that washes over his now exposed skin makes him shiver, and he regrets taking it off immediately despite being made fun of for it.

"I forgot," Mydei replies through gritted teeth, ignoring the howling laughter coming from Cipher behind him and tittering giggles from Castorice—he should've known those two would've been listening in.

He adjusts his glasses again when all Phainon does is raise an eyebrow at him.

"I'll show you where his office is. Follow me," Mydei shoulders past Phainon and starts walking down the corridor without waiting. Phainon makes a shocked sound and runs after Mydei, catching up with him quickly. They carry on down the long corridor, walking side by side.

"You were pretty close to it," Mydei says, taking a left when they reach a dead end. As soon as they turn, it opens out into a small waiting area with a large wooden door in the centre of the back wall.

Phainon glances around the space nervously, clear in the way he's worrying at his bottom lip with furrowed eyebrows. The air always feels different in this part of the school, Mydei thinks as his nerves sit on edge. He can practically feel his father through the door and walls, as if his presence over the years has seeped into the concrete and foundation of the building. It's rare now that he willingly comes down this far, so he looks around the area too, taking everything in.

The bustling sounds of the school grounds are completely gone as they're met with dead silence instead. The waiting room air feels stale, cloying and oppressive. Mydei knows it isn't just him who feels it—students and teachers alike always say it feels like they're walking to their death sentence when they're summoned here.

The walls are a dull blue colour, mostly covered up by framed photos and certificates that stretch from each corner from floor to ceiling. Only one wall is spared from it, but in place of the frames there's glass shelving units that are filled up with trophies and medals. Mydei knows that a big portion of everything here is of him, or from his achievements—the golden child until he fell from grace in his father's eyes. There's photos of him in every stage of lower education, on his university's graduation day and then on his first day as a teacher as well. There's even medals and trophies from school competitions he'd entered to make his father happy.

Mydei always aches when he remembers those days now, the memories full of desperation in needing to please his father that he would've—and did— do anything and everything that he was asked of. A heavy feeling settles in his stomach, taking the shape of needing to grab Phainon by his hand and run away as far as they can get from this room. He always thought it was strange how his father kept everything of Mydei here instead of at their family estate, but he'd long forgone the effort of questioning things his father ever did in favour of his own sanity.

He watches as Phainon steps further into the space, looking equally as unsettled as Mydei feels himself. His eyes rake over the walls, taking everything in. Usually schools will have this form of display at reception, or at least somewhere more accessible where everyone could come and admire it, but his father hoards these items like a dragon guarding his treasure.

Phainon wanders over to one of the walls, and Mydei winces at knowing exactly where he's heading. Phainon lights up almost immediately, his previously perturbed expression rolling off him like water on a duck's back. Mydei had hoped that his photos wouldn't have been spotted, their existence so tiny in the vast stretch of identical looking frames with hundreds of other faces in them.

"Look at your hair!" Phainon exclaims joyfully, turning around to Mydei to compare the photo from then to him now. His hair had been cut painfully short in that photo, the strands oddly curling out in all sorts of directions in a way he could never figure out to tame. After that, he vowed never to cut it short and grow it out to where it sits now, on his shoulders, mostly tamed.

Mydei sighs and walks over to where Phainon is standing, finding the photo in question quickly. He really does look small in it, his father standing next to him proudly and towering over him, his late mother on the other side.

"You definitely grew into it," Phainon says, turning his head to grin at Mydei, fluffing up the back of his short hair as if to prove a point. "I like how you have it now, though. Especially the braid. It's cute."

"Cute?" Mydei repeats, eyes slightly widening as the compliment settles deep within him.

"Oh, sorry, should I have said manly instead? You are very manly, Mydei," Phainon chirps, laughing as he nudges Mydei with his shoulder. Mydei glares at him, pursing his lips as he crosses his arms across his chest.

Mydei doesn't bother replying and just watches Phainon go back to looking at the photo until he spots more surrounding it that have Mydei in as well. The one above it seems to catch his eye in particular, it's one of him and Hephaestion gathered together, arm in arm, heads pressed together as they grin into the camera. Mydei had forgotten how young they were back in university compared to now, and his heart aches at the memories that come with it. He hasn't spoken to his friend in a long, long time. Not since…

"Who's that?" Phainon asks, pointing to the photo they're both looking at.

"My friend." Mydei says simply in response, suddenly too tired to go into detail.

Phainon hums, leaning forward to get a better look. "Are you guys still close? This photo looks fairly old."

"Not anymore," Mydei replies, shaking his head, melancholy filling his words.

Phainon seems to take the hint and doesn't ask any further questions, moving onto the more general photos that are littered about without Mydei in them.

"Hm, at least your hair grew out by then. You looked like a little acorn in that other photo."

"First my scarf, now my hair. Anything else you'd like to bring up about me that doesn't suit your tastes?" Mydei questions, eyebrow raising in challenge.

Phainon laughs in reply, waving him off as his eyes curve up sweetly with a grin. Mydei's heart thuds in his chest at the sight, the contrast of warmth radiating from Phainon against the frigid air in the room makes it feel like all his senses are finally waking up. He can't help but stare at Phainon in amazement—any weight that was on his shoulders from being here, thinking of his father and his past friendships, dissipates.

"Let me think on that first," Phainon jokes back.

Mydei lets himself smile, feeling even more hopeless when he notices that Phainon's eyes literally twinkle when he's happy. Mydei's stomach flips, tying itself into knots as a barrage of butterflies explode inside of him.

"Oh," Phainon says, his eyes searching Mydei's face. He sounds as breathless as Mydei feels. "You have a beautiful smile."

Mydei's smile slowly fades from his face as he looks wide eyed at Phainon. He can't remember the last time he smiled wide enough for his cheeks to ache, but now that they are, it's a familiar feeling he thought he'd long lost. Phainon's eyes continue to roam over his face, the gaze feeling like dandelion seeds against his skin as they stand in silence. The quietness cocoons around them, separating them from anything else in the world, the cold suddenly becoming warm as he stays there under Phainon's heated gaze.

It's only broken when the door opens, the sound like a gunshot in the newfound silence of the room. Phainon and Mydei startle, snapping out of their daze as they turn around to face the figure in the doorway.

"I thought I heard your voice, Mydeimos," Eurypon says, his voice stern and eyes set coldly. To anyone else, he looks like a harmless old man, what with his blonde-grey beard growing out and the soft set of his wilting shoulders, but Mydei sees the distant stare in his eyes as they watch each other from across the room.

Mydei clears his throat, straightening his posture subconsciously as he always does when faced with his father.

Don't let anyone see your weakness, his father used to say as he'd take Mydei's queen piece from the chessboard, knocking it down with a finality that was only equal to death. Don't give your opponent anything to work with.

Standing there, a few feet away from his father with Phainon at his side, he feels like he's preparing for battle.

Chapter Summary

"Ah! I forgot to do your scarf!"

"Leave it for today," Mydei says. If they take any longer then they both will be running far behind what they usually do.

Phainon pouts, his bottom lip jutting out slightly as his cheeks puff out, but he concedes quickly when he sees that Mydei isn't going to budge. He kicks the toe of his shoe against the pavement.

"Fine," Phainon says sulkily. It doesn't last for long, as he's shooting up straight and holding his hand out towards Mydei. Mydei stares down at it in shock for a moment—does he want him to hold it? Mydei begins to reach out, his own hand trembling, but then Phainon continues: "Give me your phone. I want to give you my number."

Mydei's hand freezes half way and it falls flat beside him, his cheeks burning with how easily he was about to hold the younger teacher's hand without saying anything or giving it more critical thought. He frowns, "Why?"
