"Father," Mydei says after a tense silence.

Phainon flinches, startling as he looks between the both of them with wide eyes. He must've known that they're related, at least, but perhaps not quite how closely related. Eurypon looks away first to focus on Phainon instead, a placid smile on his wrinkled face.

"You must be Phainon Khaslana?" He asks lightly, his voice giving away nothing.

Phainon gives Mydei one last glance and nods at Eurypon. "Yes, sir. I'm the new P.E teacher." Phainon replies, the politest Mydei has heard from him till now—all his natural, carefree and mischievous attitude has retreated for the time being.

He doesn't want his father to get into Phainon's head like he's done with Mydei over the years. To Eurypon, Phainon is nothing but fresh meat in the business who needs shaping and carving out to become the perfect piece to add to the puzzle. This is just a part of the first test, to see the potential in whether or not he'll succeed or fail. It's a blessing in disguise for his father to have gotten this opportunity so early on, to be able to step in and test the waters with Phainon.

Mydei knows how many of those certificates, medals and trophies come from the sports teams, so it's imperative that any new hire meets the standards his father has set out for them. They're all players in this game, even the students, despite them not realising it.

"Is this to discuss the incident earlier this week?" Mydei asks, playing dumb. He doesn't do it often in general, but sometimes it's easier to be this way when it comes to his father's games. Especially ones that are only just beginning.

Phainon begins to walk towards Eurypon but stops as the tension suddenly skyrockets between the three of them at Mydei inserting himself into the conversation.

"That is correct. I think Phainon and I need to have a little discussion about it, yes?" Eurypon replies, his smile faltering slightly at Mydei's input, a detail that no one else would've noticed but Mydei himself. He's gotten good at reading his father after so long.

"Then I'll join you. I was there too, and we handled it together," Mydei says resolutely. He goes to move towards Phainon, but the look on his father's face makes him hesitate slightly.

"I am aware," Eurypon begins, his eyes as cold as his voice as they pierce through Mydei. "I received your email. I don't think there's any need for you to participate in the meeting, unless Mr Khaslana himself would like you to be present…?" Eurypon trails off, giving the illusion of choice when there's none at all.

Mydei doesn't care. He bulldozes through it, smashing it to pieces as he replies: "I think it's best that Mr Khaslana have another member of staff in there to support him," He says, not giving Phainon any choice in the matter himself.

Mydei walks past Phainon who's still frozen in place, eyes going between the two of them like he's watching a particularly riveting tennis match. Mydei looks at him briefly, giving him a sure singular nod before continuing forward towards his father's office before he's denied entry. Eurypon's gaze feels like the tip of a blade pointed at his throat as he brushes past him.

Phainon follows behind Mydei quickly, sticking so close that he can feel the heat radiating off of him. It sets off the chill that's sticking to his bones, thawing him out slightly. That's right—he's not on his own here. It's not just him to tackle the problem that is his own father, but rather he's here to finally defend someone else for a change. He's gotten so used to looking at his father in the eye and not seeing anything at all—no familiar affection, no hint of kindness or love—that it's almost strange seeing something curious in his eyes instead as he watches them both.

They all settle down quickly around Eurypon's desk, him taking his 'throne' while Mydei and Phainon take the two plain seats opposite. Two cups and saucers are laid out, Eurypon's cup is already full while the other is empty —a clear sign for Phainon to fill his own tea as a source of comfort, all a complete illusion. Out of spite, Mydei reaches over for the pot of tea and fills it up for himself, grumbling internally that there's no milk or sugar present to have with it. He'll live, he supposes, as he takes a brief sip of the hot drink to settle his nerves.

The room is brightly lit by a single overhead lamp, its glow pooling sharply across the polished floor. The walls are painted a muted light grey and feel almost bare, especially compared to the busy waiting room just outside. The only real decoration comes from his father's plants—dozens of them are cluttered along the walls in mismatched pots, their leaves spilling over in an attempt to soften a space that refuses to be warm.

On the opposite side, bookshelves and filing cabinets stand in rigid rows, forming a neat, uncompromising barrier beneath the wide window. The blinds are drawn tightly shut, letting in no trace of the world beyond and giving the room an enclosed, airless quality. It's clean, orderly, and efficient for business—exactly the sort of room his father would choose, and exactly the sort that Mydei has always felt too visible in.

"As we just mentioned, Mydeimos explained everything to me in an email, but I'd like to hear it from you directly, Mr Khaslana. Start from the beginning," Eurypon says, voice flat and demanding.

Phainon clears his throat, setting back his shoulders as he sits ramrod straight in his chair, and goes through everything that happened. He recounts every step of the incident and the aftermath as well.

"I really am sorry, Mr Kremnos. It won't happen again," Phainon finishes, his eyes and words earnest. "Mydei amended the student's timetables immediately and they won't have missed anything in the long run."

Eurypon raises an eyebrow, and the expression sends a ripple of unease through Mydei. His stomach tightens before he can stop it, and for a moment he wonders what exactly triggered that reaction. It's such a small detail, such a small thing, but his father is not one for those types of things. Was it the nickname, the casual address that he almost never allows people to do?

His father certainly never tolerated it. There were rules in that house—rigid ones—and names were to be spoken in full, sharp and formal, never softened. He was never dad or papa, only father. No pet names. No affectionate shortcuts. Nothing that implied warmth. Only his mother had ever broken that rule. She had given him little names in secret, whispered things—variations of her prince, her heart—words that wrapped around him like comfort as he went off to sleep, words he didn't understand the meaning of until he lost it all together. Remembering them now makes something swell painfully in his chest, rising up with a tenderness he's not sure he knows how to hold, let alone show.

Eurypon finally nods, "I truly hope that is the case, Mr Khaslana. Your accolades throughout university and your references were extremely impressive and they are what landed you this job in the first place despite no proper experience. So, forgive me if I'm a tad surprised we're having to have this conversation so early on."

Mydei tenses, knowing that tone of voice very well.

Eurypon continues, an almost serene expression crossing his face now, but his eyes are glinting like daggers in the dark. "How can we, as teachers, set an example to the students if we, ourselves, don't know what we're doing?" Eurypon narrows his gaze at Phainon, contrasting the stagnant smile on his face. "It may have been a small mistake to you, but I assure you that even something like this can lead the students to believe they have power over you in these situations. While they knew when the class should've ended, you did not. Incompetence is a difficult impression to get rid of, don't you think?"

"Father—" Mydei begins, but is quieted by the icy grin on Eurypon's face that shows off all his teeth, as though he's enjoying every moment of this.

"Let Mr Khaslana speak for himself, Mydeimos."

Phainon looks deflated at his father's words, but Eurypon just sits back in his chair, the leather squeaking slightly from the movement. He keeps that thing polished, Mydei is sure of it. Phainon sits there in silence for a moment, clearly digesting everything, mouth opening and closing as he tries to find the words.

"Well, I, uh…" Phainon stutters, unable to find his footing. Mydei can't say anything more without escalating the situation, so he reaches a hand over to place on Phainon's bare knee to give it a reassuring squeeze. He's glad the desk is high enough that the action is well hidden apart from a small shift in position.

Phainon's leg jumps at the contact, but the muscles relax quickly when he realises what it is. Phainon takes a deep breath to centre himself, but now instead of upset and flustered, he looks determined.

"Mr Kremnos, they're just kids.. I don't know what exactly you think they have going on, but they were just having fun and that's why they struggled to tell me that the class had overrun," Phainon says, almost talking through his teeth to keep his tone as polite as possible. Eurypon stares impassively at him, but Phainon holds his gaze, strong and sure.

"I see. So, how will we rectify it if this happens again? Should we punish the students to make it clear that they are also to share part of the blame?"

"What?!" Phainon's volume increases at the question, and Mydei clamps his hand down on his knee even harder to try and keep him in check. There's no use using anger against his father, after all. That'll only fuel him. Unfortunately, he's ignored, and Phainon looks poised to attack. "It was my mistake. If you dare—"

"Phainon," Mydei hisses out, cutting him off before he says something stupid and irreparable. Despite his feelings towards his own father, he's still the damned headteacher of the school they teach at. This is not a time to be throwing around threats, no matter how much Eurypon himself loves to do that.

Phainon's blue eyes are blazing hot as they turn on him, and they only become angrier. "Are you going to agree with him?" He asks.

Mydei falters. He hadn't even realised he'd started slipping into that familiar spiral—the one Eurypon's words always seem to drag him towards, even when they currently aren't meant for him. Apparently, he isn't as immune to them as he once convinced himself he was. But what hits him harder, sharper, is the sting of Phainon possibly believing that he's not on his side. That hurts more than any thought of standing up to his father ever could, more than any backlash he might have to face later on. It settles in his chest like a bruise blooming from the inside, unexpected and far too tender.

Mydei steels himself and straightens his back, turning to face Eurypon head on and sheds any hesitancy about speaking up. "Father, Mr Khaslana has taken responsibility for his mistake and has taken precautions against it happening again. I don't see the benefit in punishing the students when it's already been resolved, nor will I allow it."

Eurypon's eyes turn considering as he watches him, going from looking at Phainon and then back to Mydei. Mydei feels his stomach sink at the look; there's something worse than his father's wrath—it's his father's interest.

"I was just speaking rhetorically, of course. But I understand. I'm pleased to hear you're being proactive about it, Mr Khaslana," Eurypon replies, acting as if they're ganging up on him over nothing as he placates them. "It's always good to know where your strengths and weaknesses lie when you're in a new environment, don't you agree?"

"Yes… Sir," Phainon responds diplomatically, but his face is as bright as thunder clouds as he speaks. It's clear that his former ire hasn't quietened in the slightest, and neither has Mydei's.

Eurypon nods, and the tension in the room slowly and eventually ebbs away, leaving their cups of tea stone cold in its wake. "Very well then. I won't be taking this matter any further. The situation was dealt with quickly and sufficiently, and I assume you've ironically learnt your lesson about this?"

"I have," Phainon replies quickly.

Mydei quickly drops his hand from Phainon's knee, clearly no longer needing it to be there. He misses the warmth of his bare skin instantly though, misses the softness of it beneath his fingertips and the strength he felt in those muscles as they flexed with fury.

"Thank you for your time, Mr Khaslana. I hope you continue enjoying your time here and can achieve great things."

With that clear dismissal, Phainon doesn’t hesitate to stand up to exit. Mydei follows his lead, standing shoulder to shoulder with Phainon, figuratively and literally. He doesn't acknowledge his father any further and trails after Phainon so he can leave this horrible room and the man in it behind him.

He's one foot out the door when his father's voice stops him in his tracks. "Mydeimos, may I have a moment?"

"I'm sorry, father, but I have a lesson to attend to now," Mydei replies, not turning around to face him.

"What a shame. Maybe next time we can have a game of chess, hm?"

"Maybe," Mydei mutters, letting the door slam shut behind him.

Mydei looks up and finds Phainon watching him, worry etched plainly across his face. The sight only twists something tighter inside Mydei. He grits his teeth, fists curling so tightly that his nails bite into his palms. Frustration surges through him—hot, blinding—until he can barely think, let alone see straight. He has to get out. Now.

The waiting room feels like it's shrinking around him, the walls pressing in with their cluttered surfaces and their suffocating reminders of everything he's tried so hard to leave behind. Every shadow, every framed certificate, every photograph feels like an echo of his past he never asked to confront again.

He turns sharply to avoid bumping into Phainon and storms out, long strides carrying him through the waiting room before he can second guess himself. The moment he steps into the corridor, it's like bursting through the surface after being held underwater. Life rushes back to him in a flood—the bright chatter of students, the thud of footsteps, the distant laughter drifting in from the playground.

Mydei quickly inhales, a deep, trembling breath he didn't realise he'd been denying himself for the past half an hour. The air fills his lungs, clearing the fog in his head, grounding him back into a world that feels real and alive— one not ruled by his father's shadows.

"Mydei!" Phainon calls after him. Mydei slows down to a stop as the other teacher jogs up behind him. "Are you okay?" He asks when they're standing next to each other again.

"Shouldn't I be the one asking you that?" Mydei questions sincerely.

Phainon shakes his head. "I'll be okay. Your dad is pretty intense though, huh? Are the students here criminal masterminds or something?"

Mydei scoffs at that, folding his arms over each other as he tries to keep the smile off his face at the silly comment. He feels the fog lift even further now that they're both out of there, and it's just him and Phainon together.

"Intense is one way to put it," Mydei replies.

"Is he…" Phainon pauses, as if considering his words. "I mean, is he always like that? Even with you?"

Mydei sighs and looks away at the grimy carpet instead, not particularly wanting to answer that question. It'll open up a can of worms that he's still trying to shove back into place after that meeting.

"Never mind," Phainon says, and then he pats Mydei on the shoulder comfortingly. The action is startling, making him jump slightly, but the weight and warmth are a welcoming feeling. It makes him loosen up, his muscles unwinding and his shoulders sagging a little.

"Anyway, I totally fucked up in there, right?" Phainon continues, removing his hand to rub it against his forehead. "I just couldn't stand the fact he was using the students against me over it. I shouldn't have yelled like that."

Mydei sighs, not bothering to tell him off for swearing again. He feels every one of his thirty nine years right now after dealing with his father. "You stood your ground, Phainon."

"I know! But… He didn't say anything I didn't already know, and I almost lost it because of that. It felt like he was reading me like a damned book."

"And what exactly does he know about you?" Mydei snaps, unable to help himself. He places his hands on his hips. He can't—he won't—let Phainon leave until he's removed everything negative his father had fed him during the meeting.

Phainon blinks at him in shock, clearly not expecting the sudden venom lacing the words. He shrugs his shoulders anyway, but it's obvious it's just an attempt to appear nonchalant.

"You're not incompetent, Phainon. Mistakes like that happen to us all, and it's about how we deal with them afterwards that shows where we really shine. You handled it fine and fixed the problem so it wouldn't happen again. Does that sound like incompetence to you? Or is there anything else you think you could've done?"

Phainon's eyes turn wide and glassy. He doesn't look like he's going to cry, but instead he looks overwhelmed by Mydei's words.

"Just… Don't let him win, alright? The students love you, and that's all that matters when it comes to things like this. You have their adoration and respect in such a short amount of time—I've never seen anything like it. You've left a lasting impression on them that they'll carry forever—and that's what they won't forget, not the fact that you were late one time."

Phainon carries on staring at him, lips slightly parted and eyebrows knitted. The silence coming from the younger teacher is beginning to unnerve him. Mydei knows he said a lot—probably too much, if he's honest, but he himself has been proven wrong by his own first impressions of Phainon, and damned if he's letting his father's same ones get carried on.

"Do you actually have a class right now?" Phainon asks, the question so sudden it catches him off guard.

"No, I don't. Why?" He asks.

Phainon grins, and the glassiness in his eyes clears up into something much brighter and more beautiful, like the clouds are parting ways to make room for the sun. "Wanna come help me set up the badminton courts?"

Mydei raises an eyebrow. "Is this just you trying to get out of doing them yourself?"

"Maybe…" Phainon replies, grin turning cheeky as he drags out the word conspiratorially.

Mydei scoffs and shakes his head, albeit fondly, and the tension completely leaves his body, his budding headache even easing off.

"Is that a yes then?" Phainon asks excitedly, tilting his body forward so he can catch Mydei's gaze as he peers upwards.

Phainon's eyes are doing that horrible, cute sparkling thing like they did earlier when he was happy, and Mydei knows he doesn't stand a chance against such boyish charm.

"If this is your way of thanking me for having your back again, you need to work on it," Mydei says bluntly, walking off without another word.

"Hey!" Phainon yells indignantly from behind.

"You better show me where the nets are!" Mydei calls back, letting a smile secretly spread across his face while his back is turned. It only gets wider when he hears Phainon cursing and setting off running to catch up to him.

After that, Phainon seems to be everywhere.

Mydei's earlier worries about never crossing paths with Phainon in the general staffroom are unfounded in the end, as every day since their meeting with his father, Phainon is there—either lounging on the worn leather sofa, or sitting on the table in the corner with Castorice and Cipher, laughing and chatting. It's clear that, for some reason, he finds the six minute walk across the school grounds worth it. He can understand Cipher making the trek to see Castorice as they're together, but what exactly does Phainon have here? Mydei supposes they've all become friends now, and he'd do the same, but still. Something deep in his mind nags at him, telling him there could be more.

The image of Phainon with his two best friends (their words, not his) makes Mydei's heart flip, something that is starting to happen far too often to be normal. Even as weeks go by, whenever Phainon smiles or laughs, Mydei feels himself rubbing at his chest as if that'll help ease up the spike in his heart rate.

Phainon is so expressive in everything he does—like the life inside him can't help but burst out, seeping through his pores as radiant sunshine because he has so much of it stored within that it can't possibly all be contained within his body. It seems to be rubbing off on people around him too that even the most stoic of teachers in the school are found cracking a small smile at Phainon's chatter in the staffroom. He's seemingly made friends with everyone as well, teachers and students alike, despite barely two months passing since he first started. Even Mr Anaxa, the most impassive and brusque teacher on the grounds, seems quietly fond of him as they tend to get into the most random of debates.

He enjoys watching Phainon interact with his friends the most though, the both of them having really taken to the younger teacher which doesn't surprise Mydei in the slightest. He always joins them a little late, favouring the first few minutes of his breaks to be making tea instead, but he never feels like he's intruding when all of them get together.

At first, apprehension curls tight in Mydei's chest as he watches it happen in front of him—how effortlessly everyone in the staffroom seems to gravitate towards Phainon, how naturally they gather around him as if drawn by some quiet sun. A part of Mydei, small and shadowed, whispers that he'll never get a moment alone with him again. It's a selfish fear, one he tries to bury before it can surface, but the emotion rises anyway, sharp and unwelcome.

And yet, somehow, despite all the voices and hands tugging for his attention, Phainon always finds him. Mydei barely has time to sink fully into that thought before Phainon's gaze catches his, brightening instantly. He'll excuse himself immediately from the group with gentle, apologetic smiles, slipping free of the crowd as if it were the easiest thing in the world, and cross the space to Mydei's side—like he was never meant to be anywhere else. Mydei wants it to be like that so badly he thinks he's going silly in the head with it sometimes.

Even worse—or better, if Mydei isn't thinking straight—Phainon had even taken to arriving at the same time as Mydei does in the mornings, admitting that the first time they bumped into each other in the car park was because he couldn't sleep so he thought he'd come in early to set up. He grumbles about it being early every single time, but he still jogs over from where he leaves his motorbike to the other side of the car park where Mydei waits for him. So maybe they're both as bad as each other.

They stand in front of Mydei's car, trading small talk as Phainon takes it upon himself to redo Mydei's scarf that he now does badly on purpose He'd originally wanted to wave the younger teacher off at first from doing it again, still holding onto the embarrassment from the first time it happened, but then Phainon had pouted at him…

…So, Phainon pulls his pathetic excuse for a knot completely loose and stares at it in concentrated silence until he's finally happy with the way it looks. Sometimes, if Mydei is lucky, Phainon's fingers will brush against his neck, making him shiver from the goosebumps that ripple out across his skin. He has to focus extra hard on making sure it's not obvious when his breathing begins to speed up when they're this close, and with the added contact. Phainon will always grin in satisfaction when he's done, giving it a few cursory pats to signal to Mydei that he can look down at it now.

Mydei never thanks him, but he always makes a cup of tea ready for Phainon when he comes bundling into the staffroom later on that day.

Phainon is late today.

Mydei checks his wristwatch every few seconds as if that'll explain anything to him, but to his dismay it doesn't change the fact that he's freezing his ass off waiting for Phainon and that he isn't here. If Mydei thinks about it, Phainon could've possibly gotten tired of arriving early, realising that he doesn't need to get here just because Mydei does. Mydei looks down at his poorly tied scarf and feels a little—a lot—abashed that he had kept up with this for so long.

Mydei doesn't need to wait outside. He can easily go about his day, set up at his usual time before it had been changed by their early morning meetings. But he knows, deep down, that if he doesn't see Phainon first thing, he'll feel off for the rest of the day, even if he sees him at lunch time. This is his new routine now, much to his displeasure, and he doesn't want it to change.

He'll give Phainon two more minutes, just like he did when his class was late all those weeks ago. If he's still not arrived by then, he'll go inside and pretend like none of this ever happened.

"Mydei!" A voice calls out, and he looks up from his phone where he was pretending to do something other than just staring blankly at his home screen in order to look busy for the past five minutes. So what if he's a little late too and decided to stay an extra few minutes out in the freezing cold?

There's only one person that calls him that. Phainon's expression is stunned as he runs over, cheeks and the tip of his nose pink from the cold and his hair in complete disarray. "Why are you still out here? Have you been waiting for me?" He asks as he approaches, slowing down to a stop when they're close enough.

Mydei doesn't even think—his hand rises on instinct. He smooths Phainon's hair down gently, fingertips brushing through soft strands that slip easily between them. He lingers a moment too long, pretending to focus on straightening it when he's really memorising the feel of him, the quiet closeness, and the way Phainon tilts just slightly into his touch. Of course, once he's done those two stubborn strands bounce right back into place no matter how carefully he tries to tame them. They're as persistent—and as endearing—as Phainon is himself.

"Is my helmet hair really bad?" Phainon cringes, placing his hand on top of Mydei's to feel where he was sorting out. Mydei swallows, licking his dry lips as his stomach flutters with the contact.

Once he's finished, he drops his hand back down at his side, his hand pleasantly warm in the face of the icy winds whipping around them. "It's fine now," He says, finding it impossible to look away from the way Phainon is gazing at him.

Phainon's face starts turning redder. Mydei curses in his head—he must finally be feeling the cold with how they're just standing around here doing nothing, especially considering he's still in those damn tiny shorts despite the school having a uniform kit with joggers.

Mydei clears his throat before he speaks. "Are you actually starting to feel the cold for once, Mr Khaslana? Your ears are turning red."

Even Phainon's knees begin to colour when Mydei glances down. "Um, yeah. I guess I am a little chilly." He says shakily.

"A little?" Mydei repeats incredulously. Either way, he shakes his head and looks back up at Phainon's face. He still can't understand how the teacher isn't constantly freezing, inside or outside, with how little he wears all the time. Although, Mydei can't complain too much as the view of Phainon's toned legs and thick thighs is still just as enticing as it was the first time they'd met. He can still worry about his well-being, surely? "Let's get you inside."

They start off towards reception and Phainon begins to talk, recounting his morning.

"I'm sorry I was late. I had to break up a fight by the bus stop outside my house. They were still drunk from the night before and they were arguing over nothing, so fuc—freaking annoying!"

Mydei huffs a laugh at the attempt of censoring himself. "How did you get them to stop?"

Phainon grins and lifts his arm up, making a fist with his hand as he flexes his bicep underneath his hoodie. Mydei watches with bright eyes as he sees the material move. "I used my powers, of course!"

"You mean you bodily shoved them apart, yes?" Mydei rolls his eyes. "I'm surprised you didn't get involved in the fight yourself."

"Yeah, yeah, whatever you say, Mr Kremnos," Phainon mutters, then he suddenly stops walking, whirling around to face Mydei. "Ah! I forgot to do your scarf!"

"Leave it for today," Mydei says. If they take any longer then they both will be running far behind what they usually do.

Phainon pouts, his bottom lip jutting out slightly as his cheeks puff out, but he concedes quickly when he sees that Mydei isn't going to budge. He kicks the toe of his shoe against the pavement.

"Fine," Phainon says sulkily. It doesn't last for long, as he's shooting up straight and holding his hand out towards Mydei. Mydei stares down at it in shock for a moment—does he want him to hold it? Mydei begins to reach out, his own hand trembling, but then Phainon continues: "Give me your phone. I want to give you my number."

Mydei's hand freezes half way and it falls flat beside him, his cheeks burning with how easily he was about to hold the younger teacher's hand without saying anything or giving it more critical thought. He frowns, "Why?"

"So I can let you know if I'm going to be late again. I don't want you staying out here in the cold for too long," Phainon replies, making a grabbing gesture with his still-outstretched hand.

Mydei blinks at him from behind his glasses and fishes his phone out to give to him, the device automatically unlocking from Face ID. He hopes his heart isn't beating loud enough that Phainon can hear it. He feels like he's sixteen all over again with his first crush on a boy, although back then he'd be asking for a landline number or their email address instead so they could chat on instant messaging.

Phainon sticks his tongue out through his teeth in concentration as he types furiously into Mydei's phone. "There you go," Phainon says, handing it back, already locked. "Make sure you text me later so I have your number too."

"Will do. You better get a move on now, you need to get the gym set up for your second period."

"Alright, I'm moving!" Phainon says, taking a step forward before abruptly stopping again. He blinks, then frowns. "Wait, how did you know I have a gym session second period?"

Mydei startles, memories of that damned timetable that he swore he wouldn't memorise but ended up doing exactly just that come flooding back to him. He coughs lightly into his fist at his slip up, "Lucky guess."

It's not like Phainon can talk—he has a copy of Mydei's timetable as well! But he doubts that Phainon did anything with it more than a quick glance before chucking it away. Phainon narrows his eyes suspiciously at Mydei, but he thankfully relents quickly—sparing Mydei from any of that interrogation he'd feared when he first was given the timetable.

"Sure," Phainon acquiesces. Then, a small, almost shy smile appears on his face. "I'll… see you later? For lunch?" He asks, voice clearly hopeful.

"Yeah, sure. I'll be there as usual," Mydei responds, mirroring the smile.

Phainon grins at him then, spinning around on the balls of his feet so he's standing in front of Mydei instead of beside him. He clasps his hands behind his back, nodding slowly as he tries to bite back the grin. "Cool, that's cool. Seeya then, Mydei-mos!"

"You still can't say it right!" Mydei calls after him as he's already half way through the double doors of reception, and laughter is all he gets in return.

Mydei huffs a laugh and checks his phone, and if anyone is to ever ask why he's smiling like a fool at his screen when he sees 'Phainon 💙' saved in his contacts, he would vehemently deny doing it in the first place.

By the time lunch rolls around, Mydei is practically vibrating out of his skin. He wants to see Phainon again after this morning. His students are obviously bemused by his restlessness, but thankfully they don't say anything. As soon as the bell rings, Mydei cuts himself off mid-sentence to let them go. They all look like they're being pranked at this point, not making any sudden movements as if waiting for Mydei to have his 'gotcha!' moment and then sentence them to a week in detention. Instead, he waves dismissively at them and encourages them out of the door as quickly as possible before making his way to the staffroom. He barely remembers to turn off the interactive whiteboard before he leaves.

He knows he'll make it there before Phainon, but he still goes as fast as he can without flat out running. Phainon will be dying for a cup of tea like he usually is when lunch comes about, so he's determined to have one ready for him.

When he first offered to make one for Phainon, the other teacher had cringed at the way he took it. Phainon takes his with a tiny splash of milk and nothing else, which Mydei had to get used to quickly as he always goes to put more milk in than hot water at this point. What was worse was when Phainon gulped down his drink in three swallows, wiping the back of his mouth with his hand despite there being paper towels right there on the counter top.

The cheap tea bags they keep in the staffroom are horrible—sour at best but powdery with a damp aftertaste at their worst. He's learnt by now to bring his own tea leaves in with a tiny metal pod to put them in as they steep. Thankfully, none of the other teachers drink tea as they favour coffee instead, minus Castorice who sometimes will help herself to his stash when he's not around. He knows it's her because she's the only one who likes drinking the fancy stuff that he does.

Mydei enjoys the routine of preparing tea for himself, measuring out the correct amount of leaves before leaving them to steep for the perfect amount of time. The current brand he uses says three minutes, which is one minute less than the other one he used before. It's curious, he thinks, how precise you can be to make the perfect cup. He's endured years of heckling from Cipher over it being pretentious, always calling him 'little prince' because of it.

Mydei should find everything about his and Phainon's tea exchange annoying instead of cute, but he just watches him silently each time with a faux grossed out expression as he sips delicately at his own tea. It always gets a laugh out of Phainon either way, so he keeps doing it, making their teas in matching mugs side by side.

He finally makes it to the staffroom in record time, trying to breathe in as much air as possible to slow down his racing heart. He does too much cardio for it to be because he's out of breath from the jog, so it must be because of his excitement at seeing Phainon again. He pushes open the door, the hinges squeaking obnoxiously from age, and frowns when he sees Phainon already there sitting on the sofa.

Phainon's head shoots up from where he was looking down at his phone, and beams when he sees it's Mydei.

"You're early," Mydei comments, having just about caught his breath when his heartbeat races off again at the sight of Phainon. He makes his way over, seeing that there's already two mugs of tea laid out on the table, though one is already half finished.

"Yep, for a change," Phainon glances between Mydei at the mugs that he's currently still staring at and laughs, the sound self-conscious. "I made us both tea since I got here first, but I don't know if it's any good. Mine was fine, at least. I used your little metal tea leaves contraption too!"

Mydei glances at him out of the corner of his eyes. Phainon laughs, "I washed it and put it away in its usual spot, don't worry your pretty little head about it."

Pretty, Mydei mouths, stunned. He walks closer to Phainon and gingerly sits down next to him, already prepared for the heavy lean that would happen when he did. The cushions are so worn that they sink in the middle, making Mydei tilt in sideways closer to Phainon until their shoulders are pressed firmly together. Phainon turns his head when he feels the contact, and Mydei is so close to him that he could potentially count the amount of silver eyelashes he has, or maybe he could begin cataloguing the different shades of blue in his eyes instead. They remind him of forget-me-nots, beautiful and stunning at the same time.

Mydei's lips part as he really does consider doing just that, but Phainon's eyes drop to his mouth as if he heard the silent motion. His gaze lingers on his lips for a moment, too long to not go unnoticed but too short to really mean anything, before he quickly looks away and back down at his phone. He unlocks it, and there's a bunch of photos on a social media app that Mydei doesn't recognise as Phainon continues scrolling. Mydei doesn't use his phone that often outside of texting Castorice and Cipher, and ignoring phone calls from his father's landline.

"Who's that?" Mydei questions when he catches sight of a very muscular, very underdressed man posing in front of a gym mirror with equipment behind him. Something dark and unnamed flares up in this stomach at the sight.

Phainon shrugs and scrolls past, barely giving the guy a proper look. "Dunno. He posts good workout routines though."

Mydei adjusts his glasses so they sit more towards the tip of his nose, allowing him to stare down through them at Phainon's phone, not caring if he comes across as nosey or not. He's intrigued now to say the least.

"So you don't know him, but you have pictures of him on your phone?"

"On my phone—?! I'm on Instagram, I just follow him!"

Mydei points to another guy on Phainon's feed, a video where the guy is doing push ups. "What about him?"

"I don't know him either! I just like his protein shake recipes," Phainon says in confusion. "I don't know these guys personally, alright?"

Mydei nods his head and continues to watch Phainon scroll through, but he's scrolling so fast now that nothing is distinguishable. Mydei narrows his eyes as he sees a lot of skin coloured flashes as he goes by. "Why do they all have to be shirtless?"

Phainon stops scrolling, caught between two posts so that Mydei can't see either one of them fully.

"Because they're hot and they know it?" Phainon raises an eyebrow at Mydei's stormy expression as he hears that. "I don't know! I also take these sorts of photos when I'm at the gym, but mine are purely for tracking progress. Most of the guys on here have to sell their routines for all the electrolyte powders they sell." Phainon laughs and shakes his head.

Meanwhile, Mydei's brain has completely blanked out at the thought of Phainon taking photos of himself like the men he's just seen—sweaty, pouting, and posing in a way that makes their bodies look good and enticing for the viewer. He can picture it all too clearly, Phainon shirtless with nothing but his tiny shorts on, flexing his muscles in the mirror as he takes a few photos for safekeeping. Mydei swallows thickly, something hot pulling behind his navel as his eyes trail down Phainon's chest, ignoring his phone in his hand until his gaze lands on his legs instead. They're so strong, toned and muscular, the hair on them so light it's as if he has none at all.

His brain barely comes back online when he hears Phainon speaking again. "They post some pretty good motivation quotes too. I like them the most," He shrugs one shoulder and starts scrolling again, the same jacked up type of men spanning the next few posts.

They sit in silence, Mydei half paying attention until one post in particular catches his eye when Phainon lingers on it too long. The man is still well built, about the same as Mydei with broad shoulders and a wide back, but he seems a lot older than the rest of the guys that Phainon seems to follow. His hair is black and cropped short, but it's obvious he's going grey from the thick streaks at his temples. He looks expensive, classy and done up in a three-piece dark green suit that compliments his dark skin tone and deep brown eyes. Mydei leans in closer, getting a waft of Phainon's masculine smelling deodorant as he goes, inhaling the scent of sandalwood and pine as he looks appreciatively at the suit the guy has on. It's definitely something he would like to wear, maybe without the waistcoat so he could have a few buttons open at the top to show off his tattoos, but that's the only change he'd make.

"What about him? What does he post?" Mydei asks, curious about the sudden change in content. He hums, contemplative. "His hair reminds me of mine."

Phainon startles and locks his phone immediately afterwards, chucking it onto the coffee table as his face goes red. "I can like these sorts of guys as well!" He says, but he's not looking at Mydei when he speaks.

Mydei's eyebrows fly upwards at the wording.

Phainon continues, almost muttering: "I don't just follow gym rats, alright? He posts like… Fancy photos of him travelling."

Mydei's face falls. So it's not about the looks then that Phainon likes—okay, that's fine—it's just the jet setting aspect that's reeled him in instead. He sighs and pushes his glasses back up his nose, glad he doesn't have to watch Phainon look at other men anymore.

"Why do you look so pissed off? You're even beefier than some of the guys I follow," Phainon says. He begins cooing at Mydei when he sees his expression sour even further, not wanting to talk about this topic now. Phainon lifts his legs up onto the sofa and tucks them beneath him, curling even more into Mydei's side.

Phainon laughs, reaching a hand up to tickle under Mydei's chin once he's settled in his new position, "You're buff too, don't feel bad!"

Mydei glares at Phainon and allows him to fuss over him like a petulant child for a few moments before smacking his hand away from his face. Despite that, he can't stay mad considering he's the one with Phainon's full attention now—not those random men online, nor any of the other teachers in the staffroom. He can hear Castorice and Cipher whispering behind him, but he doesn't pay them any attention as he wants to focus solely on Phainon while he has him to himself.

"Though, I guess for you, your physique is extra impressive, especially since—"

"Since I'm old?" Mydei supplies, peering down at Phainon with a flat look.

Phainon shoots up straight and Mydei instantly misses the weight of the other teacher pressed against him, his side now feeling cold and empty.

"I was gonna say for a history teacher! I promise, you don't look a day over thirty eight, Mr Kremnos," Phainon says, winking at him with a cheeky grin.

"You brat. I'll get you for that one later, so you better watch your back," Mydei replies, pointing at Phainon accusingly as he tries to keep his face as neutral as possible in fear of laughing.

"Is that a warning?" Phainon raises an eyebrow, but the grin is still on his face.

"If you keep saying things like that, it will be," Mydei cautions.

Phainon hums and gives Mydei a thorough once over with his eyes. "Is that a threat or a promise?" He asks, sticking his tongue out through his teeth, his expression pure mischief as they stare each other down.

Mydei feels the air in the staffroom thicken between them, yet again at the mercy of Phainon's taunts. "I can be threatening when I want to be, for a 'history teacher'" Mydei air quotes, a sharp smirk spreading across his face. "But where's the fun if I tell you beforehand?"

"I'm pretty good at hand to hand combat, so you're shit out of luck if you wanna take me off guard," Phainon says, voice sturdy and unwavering.

"Is that so?" Mydei begins, tilting his head to the side. "Aren't you the one threatening me now?"

"If you try anything, I'll have you on your knees before you can even blink."

"I don't think you can handle me," Mydei whispers, leaning in, almost jeering at Phainon. "I'm a bit of a handful."

Phainon's hums again, jaw clenching, muscles jumping in his cheeks. He looks radiant, blazing hot and ready to fight, to take down Mydei with the touch of his hands. Instead, it's the touch of his gaze that flattens Mydei to the sofa, as he looks him up and down again but this time slower. More purposeful. Phainon takes his time with it, propping his elbow up on the back of the sofa cushion and presses his chin onto his knuckles to support his head as his eyes flicker between Mydei's pecs that are obvious even through his shirt, over his biceps and then down to his thighs before making his way back up to Mydei's face.

"Pretty sure I could win against you either way," Phainon says slowly after finishing his evaluation, each word dripping with something Mydei can't quite place.

"I'm not so sure about that, Mr Khaslana," Mydei shifts around, folding one of his legs up onto the sofa so he can face the younger teacher properly. He mirrors him even further by propping his head up on his knuckles using the back of the sofa too so he can look at him the same way Phainon did.

Mydei's eyes dart over him—slowly, deliberately, making sure his gaze is as hot and heavy as he feels—taking in every inch as though he has all the time in the world to commit Phainon to memory. His eyes travel from tousled hair down to the tips of his trainers, lingering far longer on each place than he intends. It's so hard to look away, hard to draw his eyes back up when there's so much to look at before him. The dark blue P.E shirt and matching shorts look almost absurd on the other teachers, he thinks, but on Phainon the colours warm his skin and highlight the silver-white trim and the neat embroidery of the school logo as if it was chosen just for him.

And of course, Phainon has his sleeves rolled all the way up to his shoulders again, exposing smooth skin and the kind of lightly defined muscle that Mydei's eyes trace over without permission. His shorts, already so short to begin with, are hitched up even further with the way he's folded his legs beneath him—leaving his thighs almost entirely bare. The sight sends a quick spark of want through Mydei's chest, sharp enough to steal his breath away.

He forces himself to remain composed, but it's difficult with Phainon sitting there so nicely for him, posed and still as a statue as if he's basking in Mydei's attention. Every detail seems designed to pull him closer, to test the limits of his restraint.

"I think you'd go down first, you look a little too easy," Mydei says finally, having finished taking his fill of Phainon for now.

Phainon's eyes flare dangerously at his words. The leather beneath them squeaks with movement as Phainon leans forward, not backing down from Mydei trying to one up him. The sofa cushions dip even lower in the middle, making them practically fall into each other, their noses almost brushing from the sudden closeness.

"Wouldn't you like to know," Phainon whispers, his words sending puffs of warm air over Mydei's lips.

Mydei's heart is crashing against his ribcage. A cruel smile spreads over his face—it's been so long since he's had his buttons pushed like this, and he doesn't want to disappoint.

"You'd have to do something worth me knowing first," Mydei replies, voice cold. It's a bold-faced lie—Phainon just has to walk into a room and Mydei would be there, wanting, curious and desperate to know everything. The gravitational pull he feels towards Phainon is too strong to deny himself of, and he just wants to be within Phainon's orbit at all times, no matter what.

Phainon bites down on his bottom lip, "Yeah? Like what?" He says, the words so breathy and hitched that Mydei feels his whole body tremble. His eyes zero in on Phainon's lips, watching the action with rapt attention. They look so soft and pretty, just like the rest of him when he isn't running his mouth. The way his bottom lip is slightly swollen from worrying at it means it would be so easy for Mydei to lean forward and capture it with his own mouth.

They're still so close that he hears it when Phainon swallows, the sharp click of his throat making him look back up to meet his gaze. Phainon's pupils are completely blown out, breathing turning rabbity the longer they watch each other. Mydei lets his arm drop down from his face to lie across the back of the sofa, his fingertips brushing against Phainon's elbow that's still propped up. The muscles in Phainon's arms twitch from the touch—the action so subtle he wonders if he imagined it.

Mydei's whole body is ablaze, the pit of his stomach swirling and tugging dangerously. There's only a few inches between them, the space so small and so vast at the same time. He can imagine them sparring at the gym— heavy handed, grappling and pawing, shoving one another down onto the mat before being pushed back, neither one of them quite winning against the other. It'd be so fun, the challenge, the fight, the dire need to prove himself an equal against someone as strong as him.

"Phainon…" Mydei murmurs, the name heavy in his mouth with how desperate he feels. Phainon's lips part open, showing Mydei a glimpse of his tongue. His hands are itching to touch him, to press his thumb against his swollen bottom lip and see if Phainon opens up sweetly for him—he wants to see how far Phainon will let him go, see how much he can take in his mouth until it's too much, see who will back down first.

He wishes Phainon would touch him too, wishes that his hands were as curious and busy as his eyes that are roaming all over him, lingering on his clavicle between open buttons and the way his thighs are spread across the sofa, practically inviting him in. He wants and wants and wants, but it's too much, too little, too soon that it almost pains him.

The sound of a stack of papers being slammed down on a table makes them both jump out of their skin, leaping away from each other in fright. Phainon blinks rapidly, his skin rosy, and his chest heaving like he's just been fished out from being submerged underwater for too long. Mydei knows he's not faring any better, his hearing going in and out with how much blood is rushing through his veins.

"I, uh—" Phainon's voice breaks, which makes his cheeks glow an even brighter red. "Class. My class. It's time!" He stutters. Mydei barely understands what he's saying but nods along anyway.

"I'll see you later," Mydei says, words thick and cloying in his mouth. He clears his throat and halfheartedly gives Phainon a wave goodbye as he sprints out of the room.

As soon as Phainon has left, Mydei glances around the room without really seeing. He catches Castorice's gaze—which is glowing and glittery—and then he looks at Cipher who is scowling like she's just seen something revolting.

"Gods, the fucking stench in here after that," Cipher snipes, waving the papers in the air like she's wafting away a bad smell. Castorice nods sympathetically, and Mydei just stares at the door Phainon had left through forlornly.

Chapter End Notes

Chapter Summary

His thoughts are cut off when there's a knock at his driver's side window, making him jump. He quickly hits pause on the music before it can get going again and he looks to his right, spotting Phainon there. Phainon's leaning over, peering through the car window at him as he waves a hand and a handsome smile appears over his face. Mydei's lips curdle at first, nerves still hitting him slightly, but then they flatten out into a tense smile of his own.

Phainon laughs, the sound muffled through the window, then he pulls back slightly to breathe fog onto it. Mydei's eyebrows raise as he watches on in confusion until Phainon draws a little smiley face into the condensation, quickly disappearing as soon as it comes. But nonetheless it existed, and before Mydei knows it he's smiling properly again, all tenseness and bundling nerves gone.

"You're looking extra pretty today, Mr Kremnos," Phainon says through the window, gesturing with his hand the line of his smile.
