Mydei's phone buzzes on the counter just as he's dropping a ladleful of pancake batter into the pan. The sound has become familiar—expected, even—ever since he and Phainon exchanged numbers. Yet it still makes him pause in that same soft, startled way every time, a quiet flutter in his chest as if he hasn't quite adjusted to the fact that someone like Phainon keeps choosing to reach out to him.

He puts down his ladle and spatula and picks up his phone, grimacing when he realises he's still got a bit of flour on his hands. Mydei dusts it off quickly, taking a moment to smile at the blue heart which is still there. He's not entirely sure why Phainon added it—maybe he's gotten used to adding emojis next to his own contacts—but it makes a small smile appear on Mydei's face either way, a tiny, private one he'd never show anyone else or tell them the cause of it. It weirdly means a lot to him to have a bit of Phainon's personality show, even here, and especially now when the notification lights up his dim kitchen like a personal sunrise.

Their conversations have slowly taken on a rhythm of their own, woven into the fabric of his days: Phainon sending blurry photos of the moon at ungodly early hours, or voice notes where he rambles about lesson plans, or half-sarcastic texts complaining about staff briefings he still forgets to attend half the time if it wasn't for Cipher reminding him about them. And Mydei… Well, he's surprised by how easily he replies. He doesn't send any voice notes back—he has no idea how that part of his phone works, and he's too prideful to ask at this point—so he just reacts to the messages with a thumbs up and types his reply instead.

He especially likes the voice notes, where he gets to hear Phainon's voice through his tinny speaks and hear his laugh—always ha ha ha, each one separate, but it always sounds so genuine and full bodied that he figured out how to replay the notes so he can listen to it again and again in the privacy of his own home.

The pan sizzles beside him, a reminder that it shouldn't be left alone for too long—but surely he has a moment. Just one moment, he tells himself as he finally unlocks his phone, and it opens right up into their text messages.

Phainon 💙 [06:36 am]

i'm hungryyyyy

Mydei huffs a laugh and gives a quick glance over to the pan on the stove, and subtly turns down the heat just a little, just in case. He turns back to his phone and begins typing:

Mydei [06:37 am]

Then eat.

Phainon 💙 [06:37 am]

dont have anything in lol i forgot to pick smth up last night :-(

Mydei's brow creases. How is a P.E teacher supposed to work a full day of exercising without eating? That's completely ridiculous.

Mydei [06:38 am]

Do you have anything for lunch at least?

Phainon 💙 [06:38 am]

granola bar :-D

Mydei [06:38 am]

????

Is that it?

Phainon 💙 [06:39 am]

it'll be fineee i'm just complaining lol

He sighs, then looks between the pan and his phone, and an idea begins to form.

Mydei [06:41 am]

I'll make you something.

Phainon 💙 [06:42 am]

[Voice note]

Mydei lifts a hand up to his face to lightly cough behind, but also so he can hide the small smile on his face that's appeared, despite the fact that no one else is here. He presses play on the voice note, already preparing himself to hear Phainon's loud voice destroy the quiet in his kitchen.

"Mydei! Will you really?! I didn't know you could cook!"

Mydei scoffs at the incredulous tone.

Mydei [06:43 am]

Don't sound too surprised. I love cooking.

Phainon 💙 [06:43 am]

i'm sonxcicited

so excited**

Mydei's small smile blooms into a full, helpless grin—but it shatters the moment he inhales and catches the acrid scent of something burning. His heart lurches, and he drops his phone onto the counter with a dull clatter and scrambles for the spatula, flipping the pancake just in time. He breathes out in relief when he sees it's only a shade darker than he'd prefer… Tolerable, maybe, for himself. But for Phainon? Absolutely not. He can't give Phainon anything less than perfect—not when it's coming from him.

He lets the other side cook as he mentally rearranges his own breakfast plans. He has enough batter for four pancakes total, which is fine because he can split the amount in half and they can have two each. They're fairly large ones, anyway. So, a couple of pancakes with syrup on the side to avoid them getting soggy during transit and then also some berries should be sweet and warm enough to start the day off without being too sickly.

But lunch—that's a whole matter entirely. Something comforting? Something fresh? Something that will make Phainon smile the way he does over text? Mydei scratches the back of his head in thought, being careful not to pull out any hairs from his half up half down style. He then slides the slightly overcooked pancake onto a separate plate—the plate reserved for himself. His phone buzzes again, bright and insistent, but he refuses to look. Not until he gets these right.

The pan sizzles softly as he pours in more batter, the smell turning warm and buttery almost immediately. He watches closely, eyes narrowed in focus and spatula at the ready, waiting for the tiny air bubbles to rise and burst— his signal to flip. Each pancake after the first one turns out perfectly golden brown, pillowy in the centre and with crisped edges that flake off if you dare touch them.

Only once he's finished plating the two sets of pancakes does he finally let himself breathe. The kitchen is warm with the sweet scent of sugar and soft, rising batter, the air thick as he breathes it in. But he can't linger too long— he needs to get moving if he wants any chance of making it to school on time. He grabs a tupperware box from the cupboard and carefully tucks in two perfectly fluffy pancakes into the larger compartment, treating them with far more reverence than any breakfast should probably warrant.

Next, he fills a small pot with golden syrup, watching it pour like honeyed sunlight before sealing the lid tightly. Then come the berries—raspberries, blueberries, strawberries and blackberries—scattered all over the pancakes in a handful of bright colours. Hopefully Phainon likes them all, or they're both shit out of luck with this one. Still, Mydei smooths a thumb along the edge of the container once it's all packed away and sealed, and something warm and fluttery emerges in his chest as he imagines the younger teacher opening it later.

Mydei shakes his head, snapping himself out of it quickly. He doesn't have time to be standing here daydreaming, he needs to get a move on and get cooking so he can be out of his front door on time.

He steels himself and begins the walk over to his fridge, opening the door to peer into. He spots a few ingredients that could work… And then an idea hits him.

Mydei isn't entirely sure how he managed to cook two sets of breakfasts and prep two lunches—all while still squeezing in enough time to scarf down his own—but somehow he pulls it off. By the time he's locking the front door behind him, he's still miraculously on schedule. If he keeps this pace, he'll reach the school grounds right around the same time Phainon does. The thought alone gives him a tiny little anticipatory bubbling in his chest.

The drive helps settle him. Titan's Mercy—one of the heavier metal bands he secretly adores—blasts through the speakers as he pulls into the car park, the deep thrumming of bass vibrating the steering wheel. He bobs his head in time with the beat, fingers tapping out a rhythm against the leather as he eases the car into his usual space. The distortion-heavy guitar riff cuts through the morning quiet, steadying his beating heart and grounding him.

For a moment he sits there, letting the last few chords fade into the hum of the engine. He glances at the passenger seat where the neatly packed boxes rest in a carrier bag, and something warm and nervous coils low in his stomach. He hopes the pancakes didn't cool too much. He hopes Phainon likes the berries. He hopes—

His thoughts are cut off when there's a knock at his driver's side window, making him jump. He quickly hits pause on the music before it can get going again and he looks to his right, spotting Phainon there. Phainon's leaning over, peering through the car window at him as he waves a hand and a handsome smile appears over his face. Mydei's lips curdle at first, nerves still hitting him slightly, but then they flatten out into a tense smile of his own.

Phainon laughs, the sound muffled through the window, then he pulls back slightly to breathe fog onto it. Mydei's eyebrows raise as he watches on in confusion until Phainon draws a little smiley face into the condensation, quickly disappearing as soon as it comes. But nonetheless it existed, and before Mydei knows it he's smiling properly again, all tenseness and bundling nerves gone.

"You're looking extra pretty today, Mr Kremnos," Phainon says through the window, gesturing with his hand the line of his smile.

Mydei's smile drops and forms into a scowl immediately, which only makes Phainon laugh harder. Mydei cuts the engine and grabs his satchel and carrier bag with the food in and opens the door, not caring that he slams it straight into Phainon's knees. Phainon jumps back, mumbling curses, but he never raises his voice at Mydei for it.

"Flatterer," Mydei mutters as he gets out of the car, shutting the door behind him and locking it swiftly.

"What was that?" Phainon asks, rubbing his knees and wincing. "That really hurt!"

"Stop being dramatic," Mydei replies and holds out the carrier bag. His own lunch is stored safely within his satchel. "Here."

Phainon stops messing around and stands up straight, eyes wide and curious as he gently takes the bag Mydei is offering him. He peers into it, not quite opening it up fully, to see what's in there. "Is this…?" He trails off, sounding slightly awed.

"It's your breakfast," Mydei says. "And lunch."

"You seriously made me food? I thought you were kidding since you never replied to me!" Phainon exclaims, blinking a few times in shock. "Thank you!"

"It's not much," Mydei feels the need to say. "But it'll keep you full for the day and full of energy—"

"Like I need more of that, right?" Phainon cuts him off, winking and poking Mydei in the shoulder playfully. "But no, seriously, thank you. I really appreciate this."

"…You're welcome," Mydei says eventually, the words making a light flush settle on his cheeks that he can easily blame on the cold weather if asked.

"What did you make me?" Phainon asks, shifting his weight from foot to foot, clearly excited.

"You'll have to wait and see," Mydei replies vaguely, and holds back a chuckle when Phainon frowns at him. "You should head in early so you can eat your breakfast and let it settle before your first period."

"Let me do your scarf first then," Phainon says, shuffling the bag up to catch on his inner elbow as he holds it out of the way.

"No need," Mydei waves him off. "I'll only be taking it off in a few minutes anyway."

"I know," Phainon says, but his hands are reaching up to undo Mydei's scarf. "But let me do this for you."

"You've already said thank you for the food," Mydei points out, holding his chin higher so Phainon can tie the knot easier.

Phainon is efficient at redoing his scarf now. His fingers work quickly, undoing it and smoothing it out before flipping it over itself and tying it around in a thick knot that doesn't easily come undone.

"There, done!" Phainon says, eyes narrowing in concentration as he finishes up. He pats over it like he always does before pulling away, dropping the carrier bag from his elbow down into his hand.

They head towards the reception doors together, their footsteps crunching softly over the thin layer of frost still clinging to the ground in the early morning's dew. Mydei steps ahead just enough to pull one of the glass doors open, holding it for Phainon. The younger teacher slips past him with a quiet, grateful bow of his head, his shoulder brushing lightly against Mydei's arm as he goes through.

The moment they step inside, a gentle wave of warmth greets them, a welcome contrast to the sharp, whistling wind behind them. The air inside carries the faint smell of polished floors and morning coffee drifting from behind the receptionist's desk. Mydei lets the door swing shut behind them and watches Phainon exhale, a soft puff of lingering cold dissolving into the heated air.

"I'll see you at lunch time?" Phainon asks, turning to face Mydei.

"Yeah, you will," Mydei replies softly, nodding at him.

Phainon grins at him, holding the carrier bag up between them. "I shall report back swiftly about any critiques or comments I have." He says in a faux-posh accent, ending it with a laugh.

"Oh, Mr Kremnos, Mr Khaslana," Aglaea says from behind the desk. She waves at them briefly.

"Good morning," They both say at the same time, their voices accidentally harmonising.

Aglaea looks up at them from her computer screen, a small, almost secret smile blossoming on her face. "It's good to see you took my advice, Mr Kremnos." She says.

Mydei bristles, remembering her telling him that Phainon needed a friend, or someone to guide him, and it's clear as they stand next to each other that they've become just that within a short amount of time.

"Advice? What advice?" Phainon asks, looking between them curiously.

"Doesn't matter," Mydei mumbles, grabbing onto the arm of Phainon's hoodie and encouraging him to start walking again. "Now get to work."

"Hey! I need to eat my delicious, homemade breakfast first," Phainon says, puffing out his chest and giving Mydei a confident smirk. "Made by the famous Mr Kremnos himself, did you know, Miss Aglaea?"

She hums, those eyes of her all too knowing as they pierce through Mydei as though they're seeing all his secrets and reading through them all. "Stop bragging and go eat then." Mydei says, his pull on Phainon becoming stronger until he's practically dragging him across the floors further into the building.

"I can brag all I want!" Phainon says, his smile so wide his eyes are almost shut, mooning closed sweetly. "Seeya later, Miss Aglaea!" He shouts as Mydei hauls him away from reception.

Mydei rarely brings his own lunch to work, preferring a large breakfast to carry him through the day and relying on a rotation of healthy snacks to bridge the gap in between—munching on them during breaks or sneaking a bite between classes while students shuffle in and out. So by the time lunchtime rolls around and he wanders into the staffroom, he isn't particularly hungry. The room smells faintly of coffee and someone's reheated pasta, the usual midday hum of exhausted teachers filling the space.

Beside him, Phainon is perched on the edge of his chair, eating the pomegranate seed salad Mydei packed for him this morning like it's the best meal he's ever had. He's been muttering to himself words that Mydei can't quite catch, and making indecent sounds as well as taking huge bites. He's already asked several times, but yet again he lifts his fork expectantly.

"Are you sure you don't want any?" Phainon asks for what has to be the millionth time at this point, voice muffled around a generous bite.

"I am very sure," Mydei replies with a huff of amusement, raising both hands in surrender to ward off the incoming forkful.

Phainon frowns like it's a personal tragedy and pointedly scoops up more lettuce, more feta, more pomegranate seeds until his fork can't carry any more, and then he shoves it in his mouth without an inch of decorum. He moans around the utensil, his eyelashes fluttering slightly as he chews, his blue eyes going in and out of focus as they turn hazy with delight. It's… Well, it's enough to set off something dark swirling around in Mydei's stomach, yet also something light tugging at his chest that sets it fluttering. Mydei continues watching him, trying (and failing) to stop the warm feelings rising at how earnestly Phainon is enjoying something he made for him.

He leans back in his chair, arms crossed loosely as he lets himself indulge in the moment—a quiet lunch, the soft clinking of cutlery, the way Phainon's knee keeps bumping lightly against his under the table like he's forgotten how close they're sitting.

So no, he's not hungry. He's plenty full just watching Phainon, his expressions changing like the Okhema weather as he finishes off his lunch, sitting back with a huff of contentment.

"I think that was the best thing I've ever eaten," Phainon says, rubbing his stomach happily. "Wait, no, maybe it was the pancakes you made me for breakfast… Ugh, they're both so good!" He turns to Mydei, eyes blinking at him imploringly. "How do I get you to make me dinner, too?"

"Ask nicely," Mydei replies, but then he rolls his eyes behind his glasses when Phainon perks up far too much.

"I can beg, I can totally do that," Phainon says far too quickly and earnestly, putting his hands up like a dog's paws as his eyes round out and turn dewy. "Please, Mydei? Mr Kremnos? Can you make me dinner?"

Mydei smacks him upside his head.

"Ouch!" Phainon exclaims, hands going straight to the back of his head where the sting should still be. Mydei made sure it wasn't too hard to hurt, but definitely enough to make him wince. "So cruel to me, Mydei!"

"Stop shouting," Mydei says, then he breathes in deeply, steeling himself. "I actually have a question for you."

"Oh?" Phainon's arms drop onto the table, any pain in his head suddenly forgotten. "What is it?"

"I was wondering…" Mydei trails off, shifting in his seat. "If you'd like to accompany me and my class to the National War Museum next week?"

"Was the food a ploy of buttering me up into saying yes?" Phainon asks, laughing. He shakes his head, "Playing chauffeur? Sure, that's fine by me."

"More like a chaperone," Mydei corrects. "We need another teacher to even out the student:teacher ratio, so I thought if you'd be up for it then you can come along."

Phainon blinks at him. "If I don't go, will you not be around for the whole day?"

Mydei tilts his head to the side, "Yes. I'll be gone for the full day."

Phainon sniffs and crosses his arms, sitting back in his chair again. "I'll definitely go then. Who would I hang out with at lunchtime?"

"Cipher or Castorice?" Mydei supplies, eyebrows raising.

"But I like hanging out with you the most," Phainon says so quietly that Mydei almost misses it, then he sits up again, packing away his tupperware.

Mydei's mouth parts slightly, but no words come. Phainon's honesty knocks the breath out of him, leaving him feeling strangely exposed—like he'd peeled back a little too much of himself just by asking the question. Because he thinks the same too, he likes spending time with Phainon the most, more than he ever expected after his first impressions of him. But they're long gone, long proven wrong, and he feels silly for having ever thought them in the first place.

Phainon is more than just an exercise obsessed young man. He's excitable, genuine, funny and silly all rolled into one, and although those qualities usually rub Mydei the wrong way and cause a clash in personalities, this time he's merely endeared towards it instead. Phainon knows when to be serious, when the situation calls for it and Mydei can tell he's adjusting, but then there's also times where he can openly be himself—loud, bright and endlessly charming.

The realisation warms his cheeks, a slow, blooming heat that he wishes he could stop. Still, he's grateful that Phainon agreed to come along. It means more moments together, more chances to fall into easy conversation and get to know him past being a P.E teacher. Even if most of their time will actually be spent corralling students and keeping chaos at bay, at least they'll be doing it side by side. Well, and Professor Anaxa will be there too, plus a few teaching assistants that volunteered as well…

Mydei sighs and pushes his glasses up the bridge of his nose, settling them higher up. "I'll forward the itinerary to your school email so you can have a read through it."

"I think I have it set up now… I went down to the I.T department the other week and got them to put it on my laptop."

Mydei nods his head, taking a sip of his tea. It's still slightly too hot, but it feels perfect as the heat slides down his throat, warming him up. "That's good. Makes it easier than sending it to Cipher, at least."

"Talking about me, are we?" Cipher's voice echoes from behind them, making them both jump.

Her and Castorice walk up to them, taking a seat opposite them at the table. Cipher's smirk is spelling out so many bad things for Mydei—full of mischief and havoc. "What are we discussing?" She asks.

"Nothing," Mydei says at the exact same time that Phainon says: "A museum trip!"

Mydei suddenly feels a headache coming on, a twang of tension going through his temples.

"Oh, a trip, hm? Just you two, or…?" Cipher trails off.

"It's with Mydei's class," Phainon explains, "I've never been to a war museum before…"

"Hah! You always invite me to come with you, now I'm being replaced?" Cipher says dramatically, although any ire in her voice is completely void with the fact that she's grinning, her fangs pointing outwards.

"I don't always invite you," Mydei says, but Cipher bulldozes straight over him:

"As soon as the new pretty boy is in town, I'm suddenly forgotten about, hm?" Cipher cajoles.

"You think I'm pretty?" Phainon asks, batting his eyelashes sweetly at Cipher while wiggling his fingers under his chin.

"Why don't we ask Mr Kremnos?" Cipher replies, then all eyes are on him, zeroing in. "Do you think our resident pretty boy lives up to the hype, Mydeimos?"

"I—" Mydei begins, looking between Cipher and Castorice while not daring to look at Phainon while put on the spot. He feels a blush warming his cheeks, turning them crimson. He sighs, the fight leaving him almost immediately. "Yes, I think you're pretty, Mr Khaslana." But it comes out too soft to be stern, too honest to be a lie, too everything that it feels like he's exposing his still developing feelings right then and there.

He braves it then, turning around to face Phainon, who's looking at him with round eyes and a gaping mouth. He's red up to the roots of his hair, turning his skin a dusty rose colour instead of the pale tone it usually is. Phainon laughs, a stilted ha ha ha, and scratches the back of his head as he looks down at the table top.

"Thanks, Mydei," Phainon says, although he sounds rather shy. "You'll all let it go to my head if you carry on."

Cipher coos at him and reaches across the table to pinch his cheeks, yanking his poor face around left and right before letting go. "You didn't blush when I called you pretty! What's with this favouritism that's going on lately? I'll start feeling left out if you're not careful."

"Sorry, Cipher," Phainon says, not sounding sorry at all as he rubs his swollen cheek. "But I really wanna go to the museum, so I'm not swapping places this time."

Cipher rolls her eyes, then nudges Castorice with her elbow. "You seeing this shit, Cas?" She asks.

Castorice nods enthusiastically, her hands clasped together underneath her chin as her eyes sparkle, bright and wide. "I think it's lovely."

"We've lost her," Cipher mutters. "Anyway, are you going to the National War Museum again?"

"Yes," Mydei replies. "I think this is the ninth year in a row we've gone now, but it's always a hit with the kids."

"How do you not get bored of it?" Phainon asks, pushing off from the table to rock back on his chair. Mydei sighs and grabs the backrest and shoves him back down so all four legs touch the ground.

"Don't make me tell you off like you're one of my students," Mydei grouses. Phainon laughs, but doesn't do it again. Instead, his leg starts bobbing up and down, restless. "I'm not saying it isn't boring, but the museum is pretty good at switching up exhibitions and such. They're doing a display on the Great Okhema War this time around, which is what we're studying."

"Oh! Cool, that sounds interesting," Phainon replies.

They don't get a chance to chat anymore as the warning bell rings, signalling there's five minutes left until classes end and that it's the end of lunch. They all stand up, gathering their stuff as they begin to shuffle out towards the door.

"Phainon," Mydei calls, and the younger teacher stops, turning around to face him. "Make sure you check your emails later, okay? I'll send you all the details, so I don't want any excuses if you're late."

"I won't be late! C'mon, Mr Kremnos, have some faith in me," Phainon says sulkily, kicking the toe of his shoe into the carpet.

"Even if we leave at seven in the morning?"

"Even if— Wait, seven?! That's so early, are you serious?" Phainon asks, mouth open in shock.

Mydei chuckles lightly and pats Phainon on the shoulder, "I suppose you'll have to wait and find out." And then he walks away, leaving Phainon standing in the staffroom for a few moments longer.

The day of the museum trip dawns in soft watercolour hues, the early morning sky stretching open in delicate pastels as the lazy sun is barely in the sky. Mydei arrives while the morning is still tender, the air cool against his skin and carrying the faint scent of dew on grass. Sunlight gathers slowly at the edges of the school roof, warming the bricks in a washed out pale, golden glow.

The school grounds feel almost enchanted at this hour—hallways hushed, floors gleaming without any scuff marks on, every sound amplified by the quiet. The coach is already there waiting for them, and as Mydei stands outside the doors for it, he sees students arriving in groups as it gets closer to the departure time. They all seem a little sleepy still, their smiles hazy as they greet him and clamber onto the vehicle, their excited murmurs muted. Mydei lets it surround him, the gentle chaos, but his eyes keep flickering towards the front gate, waiting for a familiar figure to arrive.

He checks his wristwatch—there are still twenty more minutes before they have to leave, but his nerves won't settle. He rocks his weight from one foot to the other, rubbing his hands together to chase away the cold that clings stubbornly to the morning air. The kids are all bundled up in thick winter coats and scarves, the sight of them dressing sensibly for once pleasing him. Every few seconds after checking his watch again Mydei pushes his hair behind his ear, only for the strands to slip loose again in a restless little loop that betrays just how impatient he's getting.

Mydei tells himself he's being ridiculous—there's no reason to feel this keyed up—but that doesn't stop his pulse from jumping at every set of approaching footsteps. Mydei glances up when he sees Professor Anaxa and the teaching assistants approaching, all gathered around each other as they're clearly in the middle of a heated debate.

"Good morning, Professor," Mydei says when they're close enough, and nods in greeting towards the TAs.

They all chime a good morning back and get onto the bus, taking their seats near the front away from the students. Mydei looks at his wristwatch one last time—ten minutes to go. All the students and teachers seem to be here, they're just waiting for a certain someone to appear and then they can finally set off. The noise inside the coach is steadily getting louder as the students wake up, gossiping and chatting amongst themselves with excited giggles accompanying them.

"Mr Kremnos!" A voice shouts, and Mydei perks up immediately, the frown creasing his features suddenly disappearing as he spots Phainon up ahead entering the gates, a few students surrounding him.

"Mr Khaslana, you made it," Mydei says, his happiness radiating through his words at seeing Phainon.

Phainon's dressed differently today. No shorts this time, but a pair of dark blue joggers that cling to his thighs before loosening around his calves. The change shouldn't affect Mydei as much as it does, yet he still gives Phainon a slow, appreciative once-over, quietly cataloguing the new look in the private archive of his mind. He looks good—unfairly good—in the school's winter P.E kit, the deep blue making his eyes seem even brighter.

Still… Mydei can't help the faint tug of longing for those tiny shorts Phainon usually wears, the ones that show off his legs so shamelessly. The joggers make more sense in this weather, and for once it seems like Phainon is starting to feel the cold like the rest of them. He's even got his hoodie zipped up to the top, his backpack firmly set on his back rather than loosely held over one shoulder.

"Kids, get on the coach. We're leaving in a few minutes," Mydei says, but he doesn't look away from Phainon who's watching him too, gesturing to the open doors for them to glide past him, clambering up the steps and into the vehicle.

"I see you're finally dressed for the weather," Mydei comments once the students are out of ear shot.

Phainon laughs brightly, scratching the back of his neck. "Yeah, well, I wasn't sure how much time we'd be spending outside today."

Mydei hums, "Not too long, probably just for a wander around the museum grounds and to eat lunch."

"Lunch—! Shoot, I forgot about that. Do they have a café there?"

Mydei purses his lips and sighs, "Don't worry, I packed extra. I had a hunch you'd forget."

"No way! You're seriously a life saver, Mr Kremnos," Phainon says, awed.

Mydei sighs and then notices that Phainon's hair is a bit of a mess, with what he assumes is a mixture of the wind playing around with it and also helmet hair. He reaches up to sort it out, wanting to feel those soft strands again, but he's stopped by a voice:

"Are you two done?" Anaxa says from the top of the coach's stairs, his one eye peering down at them with disdain as his arms are folded across his chest.

"We're coming," Mydei says back, dropping his hand before it ever had a chance to land and glancing at Phainon quickly before he climbs the steps and onto the coach, the sound of Phainon's footsteps behind him.

Mydei pauses at the front of the coach, letting his eyes sweep over the rows of seats. Most of them are already filled—clusters of students talking loudly, swapping snacks, or dozing against the windows. The back is a packed sea of chatter, but now that Anaxa has sat back down, there's one open space beside him. Mydei heads towards it, grateful for the safe, neutral option.

But before he can reach the seat, one of the students pops up like she's been waiting for her moment. Her friends behind her push and shove her into place until she slides neatly into the spot beside Anaxa, and flashes Mydei an apologetic, almost guilty smile.

"I have something I want to discuss with Professor Anaxa," She announces, as if that settles everything. "There's a free spot next to Mr Khaslana, though!" Her friend group bursts into giggles.

"Alright, settle down," Mydei says, eyes narrowed at them in suspicion. He's slightly baffled by their odd behaviour, but nods anyway at them. What else can he do?

He turns back to assess the aisle again—and that's when he realises she was telling the truth: the only open seat left is the one beside Phainon. The younger teacher sits by the window just behind the driver, the morning light spilling over him in a soft glow as he fiddles absently with the strap of his bag.

Mydei exhales slowly. It's not that he doesn't want to sit next to him. It's that he's not entirely convinced he can handle being that close for an entire coach ride—shoulder to shoulder, knees brushing with every bump in the road, surrounded by the soft warmth and the scent of his masculine deodorant that he smells of that always seems to unravel him a little too easily.

Still, there's no avoiding it now. Mydei squares his shoulders, steels himself, and starts down the aisle towards Phainon. He hesitates for a heartbeat when he gets there, fingers tightening around the strap of his satchel as he stands, waiting to be noticed. He can feel the warmth creeping up his neck already, anticipation and dread tying themselves into tight, fluttering knots in his stomach. Of all the spare seats that could've been left, of course it had to be this one. It's not even like he's not used to sitting next to Phainon—he is, he does it all the time during lunch breaks now, but something about this feels closer, more personal.

Phainon looks up barely a split second later, and his face brightens instantly. That gentle, earnest smile spreading across his lips in a way that makes Mydei's heart falter in his chest. The sunlight streaming in through the window illuminates his hair, turning it a glowing silver, almost pure white, and for a ridiculous second, Mydei forgets how to breathe.

"Oh, looks like you're stuck with me!" Phainon says, scooting his bag onto the floor to make room. The teasing lilt in his voice is gentle, almost shy, but his eyes linger a moment too long on Mydei. "Hope that's okay."

Mydei forces himself to move, lowering into the seat with stiff, careful motions as if the smallest misstep might give him away. The space between them isn't much—barely a few inches—and he's acutely aware of the warmth radiating from Phainon, the faint scent of clean laundry and something spiced rising every time the younger teacher shifts, which is a lot. He's fidgeting.

"It's fine," Mydei murmurs, clearing his throat. "More than fine."

Phainon's knee brushes his, perhaps on accident, but he doesn't pull away, not immediately. His gaze flicks down, then up again, searching Mydei's face with something unreadable. The coach lurches into motion then and the student's chatter gets to an all time high, to which Anaxa yells at them all to be quiet. It doesn't quite work, but the sound gauge does drastically lower after that.

"Good," Phainon says quietly, as though afraid to be overheard despite everyone else in their own little worlds. "I like sitting next to you. I thought you'd abandoned me then for Prof Nax."

Mydei raises an eyebrow, "Do you call him that to his face?"

"Of course I do… not," Phainon chuckles. "I overheard the kids calling him that and he went ballistic at them, so I don't care. It's just less of a mouthful than his full name."

"You seem to struggle with full names, don't you? You still can't even say mine," Mydei replies, dropping his satchel on the floor between his feet.

"I can! I've been practising," Phainon says, and then he sits up straight and turns his shoulders towards Mydei, coughing lightly into his fist. "Mydeimos."

Phainon's voice goes all low and almost… sultry, as the younger teacher waggles his eyebrows at Mydei once he's said it. It's still not quite perfect, his slight farmer accent getting in the way of saying it right, but it still makes something fuzzy and static go through Mydei's spine.

"Wrong," Mydei says, just to spite him. His stomach swirls dangerously, and he fears if he hears it again, he might need to lie down for a moment.

Phainon harrumphs and mirrors Mydei's posture, folding his arms across his chest. "I'll get it one day, just you wait."

"I don't doubt that," Mydei says, chuckling lightly as he can't help it.

"Are you excited for the trip?" Phainon asks, changing the topic.

Mydei nods, relaxing back into the seat a little. "More than I thought I'd be. I'm looking forward to seeing the refurbishments that they've been working on since last year."

Phainon perks up at that, shifting towards him with genuine interest. Their knees brush again, but neither of them flinch away. "What kind of refurbishments?"

"Well…" Mydei begins. "They've redesigned the Great War wing. Expanded the trench reconstruction, updated all the interactive panels, and added new primary-source stations. Supposedly, the lighting and sound design are more immersive now too. Less outdated diorama, more walking into a memory."

Phainon's lips part in awe. "That sounds incredible. I've never been to a museum with that kind of setup before." His shoulder bumps Mydei's lightly as the coach turns a corner. "You'll have to tell me what's new and what's not. You know more about this than I do, I'm just here for fun."

"No, you'll be here to learn, too," Mydei assures. "It's hard not to when you're completely surrounded by it all. It's fascinating stuff, and I'm especially excited to see how the students react when we go into the interactive exhibits."

"Is there any stuff on antiques?" Phainon asks, tilting his head to the side. He looks like a curious puppy.

The coach hums along happily, joining onto the motorway after winding through smaller residential streets. The trip to the museum is about forty minutes on a good day, but with early morning traffic they could be looking at some delays. Mydei hopes that isn't the case, but that only means he gets to sit next to Phainon for longer. Now that he's calmed down and thought about it, it's actually a good thing. They're friends now—at least, he hopes so—after spending lunchtimes together, so their chatting is familiar by now.

"Antiques? I… I think so," Mydei scrunches his face up in contemplation. "I'll have to check the leaflets when we get there to see. Why do you ask?"

"I love antiques," Phainon answers honestly, and his whole body brightens up, his eyes glistening. "I have a small collection of my own at home, little trinkets and such that I've picked up over the years. You never know what you can find in those tiny eclectic shops on the high street and markets!"

Mydei blinks at him in shock, having not expected this little hobby at all. "Well then, I definitely hope that they have some you can look at when we're there. I know they have plenty of things that were found on the battle ground—such as broken pots, machinery, and jewellery. Does that interest you?"

"Yes, definitely!" Phainon holds his hands in front of him, and they're clenched into fists like he can't contain himself. "Oh, I really can't wait now." He says, his leg bouncing up and down.

Mydei sighs fondly and places his hand over Phainon's knee to stop it from moving. Phainon looks down at it and then back up at Mydei, a sheepish smile coming over his face. "Sorry, I'll try not to do that."

"I don't want you exhausting yourself before we've even gotten there," Mydei explains and removes his hand, the warmth from Phainon's leg radiating through his thick joggers and onto Mydei's palm.

Phainon huffs a laugh, "Sure thing, Mr Kremnos," He says lightly, and then pulls out his phone from his pocket and starts typing.

Mydei takes that as the end of the conversation, and he settles back into his seat, adjusting his glasses slightly before he relaxes fully and watches the outside world from the front window.

The museum doors glide open with a low hum, and the group filters through into the grand entrance hall—its ceiling stretching high above them like the open sky, banners of faded regimental colours hanging in long, solemn rows. Dust motes swirl in the shafts of light spilling in through the skylights, the air warm with the scent of polished wood and old parchment. Mydei inhales deeply; this place always feels like stepping into history itself, as though the walls still remember the echoes of the stories they protect.

"Alright, everyone," Mydei calls, his voice carrying easily in the vaulted space. The students gather, forming a loose semicircle around him. Even the teachers drift closer—Phainon included, standing just slightly behind his shoulder, listening with visible curiosity as his eyes wander around the museum's entry hall. "Stay with the group and keep the noise to a minimum. This isn't like last term's field trip—you're standing in a national archive of our past. Treat it with respect."

They nod, and Mydei leads them towards the first exhibition hall. The doors open into a dimmer room, lit by soft golden lights that cast a warm glow over the displays. The walls are lined with murals depicting sweeping landscapes—mountains cracked by artillery fire, plains scorched into mosaics, and cities swallowed by toxic fogs. Beneath them, glass cases display relics: dented breastplates, shattered blades, handwritten letters, and ration tokens worn smooth by touch.

"This," Mydei begins, his voice lowering reverently. "Is the Hall of Origins —the beginning of the Great War of Okhema." He gestures to the panoramic mural stretching across the left wall where two armies are painted mid-charge, weapons raised. "Most people think it started with the assassination of High Regent Cerydra, but that was only the spark. The tensions had been simmering for decades between Oleinus Highlands and Okhema City."

The students edge closer, whispering amongst themselves. Mydei lets them off, they're clearly digesting everything they're hearing—it's stuff they already know, but he's more so doing it for the Phainon so he can learn about what he's teaching too.

Mydei continues, "Trade disputes, border conflicts, political sabotage… Oleinus and Okhema had been playing a dangerous game for years. Cerydra's death was just the moment the world finally flipped."

Phainon listens with wide eyes, his shoulder brushing Mydei's whenever the group shuffles forward. Mydei pretends not to notice the warmth radiating from him, or the steady presence by his side, but he can't help but look at him through his peripheral vision. He can't afford to get distracted— especially not in front of the students and other teachers.

Mydei leads them to the next display: a massive, circular projection table. With a soft hum and a quiet click, it lights up, displaying a three-dimensional map of the world as it was a century ago—fractured into colour-coded alliances.

"This map shows you the alliances at the start of the war," Mydei says, tapping a small panel. The hologram shifts, highlighting borders in flashing lights. "The Pact of Twelve—here—banded together in response to the Oleinus advance. But as the war dragged on, loyalties… Shifted." He presses another button, and the borders scramble again. Some of the students gasp, their eyes as wide as Phainon's.

"Whoa," Phainon whispers under his breath, just loud enough for Mydei to hear. Mydei turns his head towards him and grins, sharp and pleased.

"Interesting stuff, huh?" Mydei says. "The Great War wasn't just battles like most lead you to believe. It was mostly political unravelling. Families divided, and decades of treaties undone in months."

They move deeper into the hall. Mydei guides them to a towering display: a full skeletal depiction of a Dromas. Mydei goes to open his mouth to explain what it is and how they were used during the war, but Anaxa beats him to it.

Everyone turns to him when he begins to speak, his index finger pointing upwards as he explains: "The dromases were a peaceful species. They were created by Georios, the 'Titan of Earth'—one of the Twelve—who helped during the Great War battle against Oleinus. Warriors rode on the backs of dromases, who were said to have such a powerful stomp it could take out thirty to fifty enemy warriors in one go."

Phainon whistles, looking up at the Dromas that towers above them. "I've seen pictures of them, but it's something else in person! They're huge!"

"They really are," Mydei agrees, standing next to Phainon while Anaxa rambles on. He's got the attention of the kids at least, so that's all that really matters. "They were breathtaking. Terrifying, but breathtaking. Thankfully though, they had very mild natures outside of battle."

"No way, seriously? Like… A pet?"

"Exactly like a pet, they were domesticated, after all," Mydei says.

As they chat, the students wander closer, carefully studying the bones. Mydei catches a few of them sketching it for later notes. Pride swells subtly in his chest—this is the part of teaching he lives for: the spark of genuine interest.

They continue through the galleries—past preserved uniforms, war-time poetry etched into metal sheets, and diaries sealed behind thick glass. Mydei's voice softens when he reads aloud from one:

"If morning comes and we still stand here, then I shall write home. If dusk comes instead, tell them I didn't run."

A hush falls over the group, even the teachers stopping their chattering in the back. Phainon steps closer again, eyes wide and dewy as he peers over the display, his eyes scanning the scribbled words laid bare in the diary.

"Fascinating," He says quietly, to himself more than anyone else, Mydei assumes. "This is stunningly preserved. And the words…"

"Hm, has it caught your eye?" Mydei asks, leaning into Phainon's space so they can both look at it together.

"I'm trained in looking out for treasures, Mr Kremnos," Phainon says, drawing back slightly so he can turn his head and look at Mydei. They're suddenly close, closer than before, their noses almost brushing from the lack of space between them. Mydei's breath hitches, and he implores himself to not look down at Phainon's lips. He instead stares into his blue eyes, and sees a slight reflection of himself in them. "And I think I've found one." Phainon finishes, looking directly at Mydei still, never taking his eyes off of him.

Mydei feels a flush building on his cheeks, warming them. He clears his throat and breaks their eye contact first, staring down at the open diary. "It is a rather beautifully bound book."

"Who knows," Phainon replies vaguely, humming as he smiles softly at Mydei before he rocks back onto the balls of his feet and turns around to the rest of the class. "Where to next?" He asks, and the spell between them is broken.

"Alright," Mydei begins, clearing his throat as he wills his cheeks to cool down. "Let's head to the next hall. There's still the Reconstruction Wing and the Hall of Fallen Cities to go through before lunch."

The students eagerly follow, their phones all out as they take photos of the displays for later, their notepads full of facts and tid-bits they've picked up along the way.

Lunchtime rolls around quicker than expected, and as students and teachers alike scatter across the outdoor benches, Mydei somehow ends up sharing a table with Phainon. They sit opposite each other beneath a pale spring sun that offers more light than heat, and Mydei silently curses himself for not bringing a flask of hot tea to enjoy with his sandwiches. Instead, he has to make do with a lukewarm bottle of water he grabbed from the café earlier, turning it between his palms as if friction alone might warm him.

Across from him, Phainon is happily demolishing the sandwiches Mydei prepared that morning, his enthusiasm almost comically earnest. The quiet chirping of birds fills the silence between them, blending with the distant chatter of students. Mydei keeps his gaze on his own lunch, pretending not to notice how Phainon stuffs his cheeks full until he looks more like a startled chipmunk than a grown man. But every few moments, despite himself, Mydei glances up—just to make sure Phainon's enjoying his food, of course. No other reason.

"Gods, you're a messy eater," Mydei comments as he takes a gulp of water. He winces at it and quickly puts the cap back on. He whips out a handkerchief from his jacket pocket and leans over the bench, wiping away crumbs that are dusted around his mouth. Mydei clicks his tongue and gives his napkin a few flicks to get rid of the debris.

"It's because you make such good food," Phainon replies, a big silly grin on his face. His eyes shine in the sunlight prettily.

"They're just ham sandwiches," Mydei remarks, taking a bite of his own. He filled it with plenty of ham, mayonnaise, lettuce and tomatoes because he thought it might be more filling than a plain sandwich would've been.

"Mmm, but I only usually get the cheap stuff from the supermarket. You probably get thick cuts from a deli counter, right?" Phainon says, polishing off the last bite of his sandwich. He sighs happily, wiping his mouth with the back of his hand.

Mydei cringes and offers his handkerchief out to Phainon again, who happily takes it and rubs it over his mouth until it looks sore. He really is like a child sometimes, Mydei thinks, albeit strangely fondly. It's kind of cute, he admits against his will.

"I do," Mydei says, a little embarrassed at being so easily seen through with his shopping habits. "Good ingredients don't always make a dish, but it's nice to go all out sometimes."

"Agreed," Phainon nods, "Although I don't know much about cooking outside of making salads… I still think about the one you made me the other week."

"I can send you the recipe if you'd like?" Mydei asks, already getting his phone out to text Phainon the full thing.

"Sure! Thanks, Myd— Mr Kremnos," Phainon replies, stumbling on his name.

Mydei doesn't say anything and doesn't call him out on the almost slip up, and graciously accepts his handkerchief back from Phainon. "It's almost time to get going again," Mydei says after he's sent Phainon the text with the recipe in for the pomegranate seed salad he'd made him.

"Aw, but it feels like lunch only just started…" Phainon replies, pouting slightly.

"It's free time for the students, so you're welcome to stay here for the next hour or so while we all go back inside," Mydei says flatly, already knowing that Phainon will protest.

"No, no! I'll come back in, I wanna take a look at the relics," Phainon says, shaking his head. "I saw some cool ones in the entrance, so I'll probably go straight there first."

"I'll join you, then," Mydei says, then pauses. "If you don't mind…?"

Phainon laughs, waving his hand. "Of course I don't mind! Maybe you'll know all about them and can teach me." He says, resting his elbows on the edge of the table as he places his chin in his palm. Phainon looks up at Mydei through his lashes, "You're really cool when you're in the zone."

"You mean when I'm blathering on about history?" Mydei asks, raising an eyebrow.

"No! I'm serious, that passion is super cool. I like it," Phainon says. "I like passionate people."

Mydei clears his throat and shifts in his seat slightly at the praise, not really knowing what to say or do. "It's just how I've always been." He finally settles on saying.

"I can tell," Phainon replies, and his smile is small but no less genuine or bright. "So teach me more, Mr Kremnos."

The way he says his name… Mydei shivers slightly, a tingle going down his spine. "Sure," He replies simply, clearing his throat. He gathers their rubbish in his hand and gets up from the bench, jogging over to the trash can further away on the field. He dumps it in and takes a moment to steady himself, breathing in and out deeply before he turns back around and makes his way over to Phainon again.

"It's time to get moving," Mydei says, packing away the tupperware he brought with him back into his satchel, dumping his water bottle in there. He'll pop it in the fridge once he gets home so it's actually drinkable for him.

"Class!" He shouts, and everyone turns their heads towards him. "It's time to get back into the museum. It's free time, so you're allowed to wander around for an hour before heading back onto the coach. Behave, don't get lost, stay on the museum grounds and don't be late, okay?" He warns.

Everyone nods and starts getting up from the benches, packing away their lunch stuff swiftly until they're all following Mydei back into the building like little ducklings. He huffs a silent laugh at that thought, and Phainon looks at him quizzically. He shakes his head and they continue onwards until they're standing in the entrance hall again.

They form a loose semicircle around Mydei again, waiting for further instructions. "Like I said, behave and remain respectful. I'll see you all back here in an hour. Go enjoy yourself, the gift shop is still open so if any of you brought any change, go have a look!"

The students and other teachers all dispatch, wandering off immediately all in different directions. Mydei sighs and hopes there will be no trouble when it comes to gathering everyone back up again in time for the coach home. He doesn't want to be stuck here after closing time looking for rogue students who lost track of time.

"Coming?" Phainon asks him, smiling.

"Lead the way, Mr Khaslana," Mydei says, gesturing out into the hall.

Phainon laughs—bright and boyish—and starts walking ahead, hands tucked into the pockets of his joggers as he leads them deeper into the gallery. Mydei follows a step behind, watching the way Phainon's head turns left and right, his hair swishing with the movement and those two silly strands on top bobbing along. He's clearly drinking everything in with curious, eager eyes. It's endearing, painfully so, and Mydei lets himself admire him for just a moment longer before refocusing on the displays.

They stop in front of a row of tall glass cases—three of them to be exact, each lit from above so that the relics inside glow faintly in the warm museum light.

"Ah, these are interesting," Mydei comments as soon as he recognises them.

Phainon steps closer too, leaning forward slightly, palms braced on the railing as he peers inside. "What are they?" He asks, voice hushed as if the artefacts might wake if he's too noisy.

Mydei joins him at the railing, their shoulders nearly brushing as he places his hands on top of the cool metal, their pinkie fingers touching. "These," He begins, trying to keep his voice neutral as their contact makes his heart begin to beat faster. "Are personal effects recovered from the Battle of The Black Tide. They belonged to soldiers from both sides."

The first case holds a battered metal canteen, dented and scorched, rusted around the rim. Its straps are frayed, one side torn off completely. Beneath it lies a set of dog tags—two fused together by fire, the writing on them no longer legible. The next one holds a broken pocket watch, the glass surface shined and bright, glinting in the overhead light as if it still works. The third case displays a letter, opened and undelivered.

"Some hard hitting stuff," Phainon remarks, lifting his other hand to point at the letter so their pinkies are still touching. "I still can't believe how long that's survived. How long ago was the battle, like, almost two hundred years ago, right?"

"Correct," Mydei says, nodding firmly. "But there's much older stuff in this museum, on the top floors. Then you're going into ancient times. Would you like to see?"

"Sure!" Phainon says excitedly, and then he's pulling away, the warmth from his shoulder and hand disappearing along with him as he begins to briskly walk off, almost breaking into a run towards the stairs.

"Mr Khaslana!" Mydei calls after him, refusing to run within the museum. "No running!"

"Oh, shoot, yeah," Phainon says, skidding to a stop. He turns around and waits for Mydei to catch up, rubbing his neck sheepishly.

"Do I need to hold your hand like a child so you don't go running off again, Mr Khaslana?" Mydei reprimands, voice stern and eyebrows furrowed.

Phainon giggles—giggles—and holds his hand out towards Mydei, palm up. "You can hold my hand if you'd like, Mr Kremnos."

Mydei pauses, looking down at Phainon's large hand being offered to him. His eyes trace over the lines on his palm, the smooth skin not giving away any secrets. He wants to take it, wants to reach out and entwine their fingers together, wants to feel their skin brushing against one another without having to be squirrelled away subtly. Without thinking, he lifts up his hand until their palms are hovering over each other, his fingertips brushing against Phainon's. Then, suddenly, he comes back to himself and snatches his hand away, accidentally clipping Phainon's palm with his fingernails.

"Ow!" Phainon exclaims, looking down at his palm with a frown before he lets his arm drop down back beside him.

"I'm sorry," Mydei says quickly but honestly, his hands hovering outwards as though to grab Phainon's hand and inspect it himself for damage. He doesn't, though, and lets his arms down, his shoulders sagging.

"It's fine, it didn't hurt," Phainon says, offering him a placating smile. "Although I can't say I'm in a rush to offer my hand to you again, Mr Kremnos." He laughs.

Mydei rolls his eyes and begins the walk up the stairs, listening to Phainon cackling behind him.

By the time the museum trip winds down, darkness has descended upon the sky. It's even colder than before, as each breath Mydei takes, a puff of clouded air comes out in return. The students are still somehow buzzing with chatter, but their energy is starting to fray around the edges as he catches a few of them yawning after such a busy day. Mydei watches them pile onto the coach in waves, their laughter and shouts mingling with the occasional groan of tired limbs. Phainon helps shepherd the last few stragglers, giving gentle reminders about hurrying up and some playful nudges as he goes.

Once everyone is settled, Mydei takes a seat near the front, and Phainon slides in easily next to him. The sun is completely gone now, but there's still some streaks of gold in the sky, lingering. The warmth of the coach is welcome as he settles down. The hum of the engine mixed with the quiet murmurs of exhausted students all creates a lullaby of some sorts, and he's not surprised when he looks over to face Phainon that the younger teacher's eyes are drooping sleepily, his head nodding back and forth as he tries to fend off sleep.

"Have a nap," Mydei whispers, startling Phainon slightly. He looks over at him, half-lidded but no less bright.

"I think I'm gonna have to," Phainon slurs out, rubbing one of his eyes with his fist. He leans back into the plush coach chair and closes his eyes, but almost immediately his head lolls to the side, landing on Mydei's shoulder.

Mydei tenses, nearly jumping out of his skin, but he tries to keep any outward reaction to a minimum as he feels the steady rise and fall of Phainon's breath. He can't believe he's out cold already, just like that? He's almost jealous, having to spend most nights tossing and turning until sleep claims him. Maybe Phainon just has nothing to worry about, or maybe he feels safe right now, curled up into Mydei's side. Mydei feels his own eyes begin to droop with fatigue, but he stares ahead instead of at the top of Phainon's head even as the strands tickle his cheek. He doesn't want to fall asleep, he wants to continue feeling the warmth and weight of Phainon resting on him, watch his eyelashes flutter slightly as he dreams and his lips part and close again.

Before he knows it, Mydei's head rests atop Phainon's, and he's fast asleep.

…

"—lana, Mr Kremnos!"

Mydei grumbles, face scrunching up as voices infiltrate his sleep. He adjusts himself in his spot, settling down again.

"Mr Kremnos? Whoa, they're seriously flat out right now."

Then there's a click of a camera and a flash going off behind his eyelids.

"Stupid! You forgot to turn it off!"

Mydei's eyes instantly open, and he realises he's surrounded by a gaggle of students, all of them peering at him and Phainon—who is still snuggled into his side, and Mydei's cheek pressed on top of his head. He sits up straight, jarring Phainon awake with his sudden movement. He adjusts his glasses frantically, eyes blinking and wide as everything sets in.

The coach isn't moving anymore.

"Are we back at the school?" Phainon asks from beside him, his voice droning from just having woken up. It's deeper than usual, Mydei notices, but he shakes himself out of it as the bunch of students are still there, watching them.

"Whoever took a photo, delete it immediately or you're all going in for a week's detention," Mydei declares, raising his voice so the entire coach can hear him.

The students all spring into action, laughing loudly and running out of the coach, sprinting away without giving Mydei a chance to reprimand them again for their shenanigans.

"Those kids…" Mydei grouses, more to himself than to anyone else, but Phainon still laughs.

"Sorry about sleeping on you, Mr Kremnos," Phainon says as he gets up, shuffling out of his seat and into the aisle.

Mydei sighs and picks up his satchel from the floor, joining Phainon in the aisle. It's a tight squeeze, their fronts pressed together, but neither of them move as they're now alone on the coach except for the driver who's on his phone.

"No problem," Mydei says gruffly, then he slides over and past Phainon, trying not to think too much about the contact until he's safely off the coach. He turns around to Phainon who's climbing down the steps and jumps the last one, landing on the pavement with a slap of his trainers.

"I'll see you tomorrow, Mydei," Phainon says, waving at Mydei.

"Mhm, tomorrow," Mydei says and watches as Phainon begins to walk off towards his bike. He breathes in the night air, cold and soothing, and calls after the younger teacher: "Get home safely!"

Phainon turns around and walks backwards, giving Mydei another big wave with his whole arm this time. "You too!" And then he's running through the car park, leaving Mydei on his own.

Mydei scratches his cheek, still feeling the phantom tickle of Phainon's hair against it.

Chapter Summary

He prowls back over to where Mydei is still standing by the doors, making Mydei feel like he's being hunted down by a wild animal. Once Phainon is close enough to do so, he reaches a hand up to place on his shoulder. The touch is so light Mydei can barely feel it through his suit jacket, but it still sends shivers down his arm regardless. Phainon hums to himself, eyes contemplative as he drags the fingertip of his index finger down from his shoulder, stopping when he reaches the middle of Mydei's bicep.

"What if I want to see these in action?" Phainon asks coyly, wrapping his fingers around his arm, but they barely begin to cover any of the circumference.
