"Oh, hells!" Mydei yells into his empty classroom, scooting back his desk chair so he can survey the damage he's just caused. He glances down at his now ruined white shirt that's been completely soaked in coffee, and the only emotions at seeing such a mess are defeat and exhaustion. Thankfully, he'd been lounging back in his chair so it just missed the paperwork on his desk. It would've been a literal nightmare to explain to his students about how their work was ruined because of his own carelessness.

Because that's what this was—carelessness. No one had bumped into him, no one had knocked it over on accident, no—he'd just completely missed his mouth because he was thinking of a certain white haired teacher. Mydei's brain won't stop replaying what happened the other week in the staffroom, images going around and around over and over again. It haunts him in bed at night and well into the daylight hours, too. He can't get it out of his head how willing he was to kiss Phainon in the middle of the room, right in front of his co-workers that he'd forgotten were even there in the first place. It was like everything had narrowed down into a pinpoint on just them, the rest of the world falling away from focus as he watched Phainon watching him.

If Phainon had asked him to do anything in that moment, or had pushed a little harder, Mydei would've done it—and that scares him, but even worse he would've wanted to as well. He would've kissed Phainon if he'd asked nicely, or rudely, or just plainly demanded. He would've thrown away his dignity (however little is left after all this) and would've kissed that damned mouth to get him to shut up.

"Gods damn it," Mydei curses, realising he's zoned out again thinking of Phainon. The coffee on his shirt is still there, unfortunately, and has now cooled down so that it just feels uncomfortably sticky against his skin. It then occurs to him that the only place in the school that stores spare clothes is the P.E department—which means if he wants to be stain-free for the rest of the day, that's the only option he has.

Mydei goes through Phainon's timetable in his head as he tries to confirm where he could be right now. If he remembers correctly, Phainon should be in a lesson, so thankfully he won't have to worry about bumping into him while in this sorry state. He's not sure he could look the younger teacher in the eye if that was the case. Mydei sighs, long and suffering, and puts his suit jacket on to try and hide the majority of the stain as he begins the walk over to East Block.

He's practically shivering once he reaches the office, the wind completely cutting through him due to the wet material making it feel like ice against his skin. Mydei knocks on the door and waits.

"Come in!" A voice says, and Mydei pushes the door open to the office, not sparing the other person a glance as he turns around to shut the door behind him.

"Do you have any spare shirts?" Mydei asks, beginning to turn around.

"Mydei?" The voice that let him in earlier says, and Mydei feels a flood of dread run through him when he realises who it is.

He turns around fully to Phainon, facing him head on, who's sitting at a desk looking at Mydei with wide eyes and concern plastered across his face.

"What happened?" Phainon questions, staring at directly at the wet patch that his suit jacket couldn't quite cover.

"…I spilled my coffee," Mydei says, trying to push back on feeling any shame as he's face to face with the cause of the accident.

"Did you burn yourself?" Phainon asks, shooting up from his seat to rush over to Mydei. He raises his hands up as if he wants to touch and check, but very thankfully he keeps those wandering hands to himself for once. Mydei isn't sure he can handle Phainon touching all over him right now, even if it is out of concern.

"No, it was lukewarm. I just came here to ask if you had something I could change into."

Phainon tears his eyes away from Mydei's chest to look at his face instead. "We should do. Miss Aglaea had a clear out of the lost and found the other week and donated a few pieces to us. I think it's mostly all kids sizes, though…" He trails off, then he clicks his fingers. "I wonder if one of Nikolas's t-shirts is in there. Let me check."

Mydei nods and follows Phainon over to where they keep the lost and found box. Phainon heaves it up onto the desk and they sort through it together, but each item they come across near the top seems to be either pairs of shorts or joggers, none of which will help Mydei in the slightest.

"I swear we had one…" Phainon says to himself, sticking his arm right into the bottom of the box so he can grab the lower buried items. He grins, clearly having latched onto something promising, and yanks it out quickly. "Here it is! It should be okay," Phainon holds it up to show Mydei, but when they both see the whole thing, they both go silent in shock.

"Phainon," Mydei grits out through his teeth, eyes narrowing. It only earns him a nervous laugh in response. "I can't wear that."

"Why not?" Phainon asks, handing it over to Mydei to take as he tries very hard not to laugh. "I think it'll be a perfect fit!"

"Yeah, for a toddler! Why is his shirt so small?!"

"Oh, leave it alone! He must've had a washing mishap," Phainon replies, jutting his bottom lip out slightly. He briefly pulls the shirt back and holds it up again by the shoulders, pulling at the material. "It's still super stretchy at least?" He reassures, though he doesn't look convinced by either his own words or demonstration.

Mydei considers shoving the shirt up where the sun doesn't shine just so he never has to look at it again, but he really doesn't want to spend the rest of the afternoon stinking of stale coffee and having a physical reminder of what a dumb-struck idiot he is at the moment. His shirt is beyond saving right now until he can get home and hand wash the stain out, so he snatches the shirt out of Phainon's hands in a huff.

"It's not my fault that you're fuc— freaking huge, Mr Kremnos! You can borrow one of my hoodies instead if you'd like?"

"No," Mydei chokes out, refusing to walk around topless and only in Phainon's hoodie that will smell of his masculine deodorant and remind him of Phainon even more than he already is, making his distracted mind a true danger to society. At least the shirt he's currently holding is freshly washed and smells of nothing but generic detergent.

Phainon shrugs his shoulders at the blunt dismissal and sits back down at his desk, putting the lost and found box on the floor for now.

"Are you—" Phainon begins when he sits back up, but cuts off with a sudden squeak. "What are you doing?!"

Mydei has shucked off his suit jacket and placed it neatly on the desk as he works on undoing his shirt buttons, and he's about to unbutton the final one when he stops at Phainon's outburst. He pauses, hands stilling, eyebrows raising.

"Getting changed?" He says, taking off his shirt. He grimaces when he gets a clear view of how large of a coffee stain he has on his chest—he's not even sure how the hell barely half a mug of coffee could make such a mess, but he's just glad it's dried off now. "Do you have any paper towels?"

"Uh—" Phainon is bright red, his cheeks so warm they're almost glowing. "Yeah." He finishes, sounding practically robotic.

He stands up and grabs some kitchen roll on the side counter, walking over to Mydei as he rips off a few sheets. Phainon balls it up and leans in, and Mydei's eyes widen as he realises what he's going to do before he can stop it. Phainon dabs at Mydei's chest with the paper towel, and his touch is gentler than he expected, not letting the rough surface rub raw against his skin.

"You're lucky it wasn't hot or you'd be straight down to Hyacine's office," Phainon says as he works on getting the coffee off his chest, and Mydei stares resolutely ahead so he doesn't have to think about the way Phainon's hair is tickling his skin from being so close.

"Good thing it was practically finished so there wasn't much left in the mug," Mydei says, glad his voice doesn't shake when he speaks.

Phainon hums, and Mydei can't help but shiver when he feels the warm air brush against his chest. He feels his nipples pebbling, growing hard in the coolness of the room and Phainon's touch. Mydei clears his throat, but before he can speak he's cut off:

"Your tattoos are awesome, by the way," Phainon says, his voice full of awe. "How far down do they go?" He asks, poking Mydei's bare hip where one of the red swirls disappears into the waistband of his trousers. He then hooks his fingertip into the waistband, tugging at it suggestively.

Mydei grits his teeth, swallowing down a gasp. "All the way down. I have them all over my body."

Phainon glances up at him through his lashes, lips parted and eyes shining with curiosity. "Can I—"

"I'm not taking any more clothing off just for you to look," Mydei replies sharply, his ears warming at the thought. This is already humiliating enough as is.

Phainon pouts, cheeks puffing out childishly. He harrumphs, pulling back his hand with the paper towel in. "Fine, I guess." He gives Mydei's chest a once over quickly, not lingering. "The stain is mostly gone now, you'll have to shower the rest off later."

"Thanks for your advice," Mydei replies, rolling his eyes. He shakes his head as Phainon turns around and chucks the paper towel into the bin across the room like he would a basketball.

"Nice! I got it in!" Phainon says, fist pumping in sheer joy.

Mydei scoffs, but it comes out more as a soft laugh instead much to his dismay. Phainon grins at him over his shoulder and makes his way back to his desk, flopping down into the chair. "You're still going to get changed here?" He asks, gesturing to the shirt and then to Mydei.

Mydei snatches it up from the desk, glaring at it resolutely. He doesn't want to put it on, but the other options available to him aren't going to happen. He knows he's being petty—childish, even—about denying wearing Phainon's hoodie which is clearly the better option, but he's got an image to uphold and his sanity to work on. The t-shirt should be the same dark blue as Phainon's P.E kit, but instead the colour is so faded it looks like it's been through a few bleach baths. Seeing this, Mydei suddenly doesn't feel too bad about that one time a few weeks ago where he messed up his own washing by accident.

"Well I'm not exactly going to go into the bathrooms looking like this," Mydei snarks. He'll have to try and get this thing on eventually, what with goosebumps rippling across his skin from Phainon's gaze and the coldness in the room, and there's no way he's putting his dirty shirt back on now.

Mydei peers down at the offending item over his glasses, giving it a few tugs at the seams to see if it really is stretchy. It moves easily with the pulling, so maybe it will fit despite being a few sizes too small. He adjusts his glasses higher up his nose and stretches the neck over his head so it doesn't catch on them. The stitching makes a suspicious ripping sound once he gets it further down, but then there's just enough give that he can actually move enough to get his arms through the sleeves.

"Are you sure this is the only shirt left?" Mydei wheezes, wrestling with it to try and get it over his chest. It digs uncomfortably into his pecs, making them half bulge out at the bottom and feel like they're being compressed on the top half. The hem is scraping right over his hardened nipples too, which makes him jerk from the sensitivity. It's like a whole body workout trying to get this t-shirt on, but once it's over the swell of his chest it goes down easily over his slimmer torso.

Mydei stares down at his body with disdain, feeling absolutely ridiculous in it. It's clinging horribly to each ridge and bump of his body, and doesn't even reach the top of his trousers either, leaving a thick stripe of skin bare around his waist. He scratches over his stomach, feeling the hair from his happy trail. The cold air makes him shiver, and he hopes Phainon isn't about to make fun of him for looking like an old fool.

Even though he's done and the t-shirt is on, Phainon doesn't say anything at all, but a weird noise comes out of him which makes Mydei glare at him, adjusting his glasses as they were knocked askew in the fight to get the item over his head. Phainon quickly wipes his mouth with the back of his hand and doesn't meet Mydei's gaze.

"That funny, hm?" Mydei asks, completely miserable in his new attire. He can't even move his shoulders too much in fear of the t-shirt completely ripping in half on him. He's just glad he can slip back into his suit jacket soon and do up all the buttons so his skin doesn't show, and after that he's only got two more lessons to suffer through before he can forget this ever happened.

"Huh?" Phainon finally answers, looking weirdly flushed and fidgety. "I think it looks fine."

"I look stupid, I think is what you mean to say," Mydei deadpans, eyes thinning at the slight curl of Phainon's lips. He must be trying to keep his laughter at this debacle inside, and that's why he's acting so suspicious. His arms feel like they're losing circulation with how tight the sleeves are around them.

"No!" Phainon says, going to stand up but he quickly sits right back down again and blushes even brighter. "It just… Y'know… Really emphasises…" He gestures over his own chest, making it look like as if he's holding two watermelons in his hands.

"Mr Khaslana!" Mydei shouts, humiliation roaring through his body at the mere suggestion of— of—!

Phainon finally loses it like Mydei knew he would and begins slapping the desk with his hand as he cackles away, eyes shut tightly and mouth wide open as he laughs so loud it echoes around the room.

"Your stripping technique could use a little bit of work!" Phainon laughs, his eyes shiny with unshed tears from how hard he's still laughing.

"You little—"

"Why are we talking about stripping?" Cipher's voice suddenly comes from behind Mydei, making him spin around in horror to look at her.

Cipher blinks down at Mydei's tiny shirt and seems equally as horrified. "What the fuck are you wearing, little prince?"

Mydei groans and runs a hand through his hair, making sure not to catch it on his braid. It smooths down a few odd ends that were sticking up from when he was getting changed. "I spilled coffee over myself."

"Right," Cipher says, dragging out the word sceptically as she looks between him and Phainon. "Still don't get what that has to do with stripping."

"Because he took his shirt off right in front of me!" Phainon exclaims, his laughter finally quietened down.

"So?" Cipher asks. "You're both boys, who cares?"

"I didn't say— I don't care—" Phainon stutters, scratching behind his ear sheepishly.

Mydei clicks his tongue in annoyance. "What are you doing here?" He asks Cipher.

"Oh, me and Phainon usually go on break around this time," Cipher replies, purposely ignoring Mydei's glare directed at her from that new piece of information.

"Well, don't let me keep you," Mydei huffs, turning back around to snatch up his ruined shirt from the desk.

"Are you sulking?" Cipher whispers through her teeth as Mydei walks past her. He doesn't answer, but pauses in the doorway, feeling very silly that he actually is sulking. He wants to take more breaks with Phainon, too.

Cipher sighs and rolls her eyes, shaking her head at him. "Phainon, are you ready to go?"

"Um," Phainon glances down at his lap, lightning fast, and then back up to Mydei and Cipher who are both watching him. "In a minute?"

Cipher's face looks like every part of her life force has been drained out of her at his answer, leaving her cheeks looking slightly hollow to match the dead look in her eyes. Mydei furrows his brows, eyes darting between them as the silence stretches out with their silent communication.

He clears his throat, no longer wanting to be stuck in between… whatever is going on right now. "I'll see you tomorrow, Phainon."

Phainon looks away from Cipher and beams at Mydei, his eyes curving up sweetly as he does so. "Yeah, definitely," He replies, cheeks slightly flushed and the ends of his hair curling.

Mydei's heart clenches at the adorable sight but he shakes his head and leaves. As he's walking away, he hears Cipher's voice coming through the door:

"Seriously, Phainon?" Her tone is so flat that Mydei can vividly picture her signature deadpan look that still sends a chill down his spine when it's aimed at him, as it usually means trouble.

Mydei has taken to wandering around the East Block today. He doesn't hope for anything, especially not a quick glance of Phainon, but his heart is beating steadily in his chest either way at the thought. He'd scrunched up and shoved Phainon's timetable at the back of his drawer in his bedside table once he got home the day of his slip up, but later on that night he'd sheepishly fished it back out to smooth over it and folded it up neatly. After another close inspection, the majority of their lessons overlapped, but every other Friday when Phainon was in class, Mydei had a free afternoon.

Of course, Mydei knows he should be using said free afternoon to catch up on his own work—like marking student's homework or drafting up his lesson plans for the week after—but his feet end up taking him on a journey to outside the P.E hall instead.

Mydei makes sure to stay just out of sight through the windows. He doesn't want to get caught; the curious gazes from passersby are already enough to put him on edge and he's moments away from storming back to the history department and forgetting this ever happened. But then he catches sight of silver-white hair, the two strands on top of his head bouncing as he walks, and Mydei is completely rooted to the spot. He just wants to watch and admire in a way that doesn't require any probing questions—he's gotten good at ignoring the ones coming from himself, at least.

Phainon seems extra excited today. His hands are flying around and his facial expressions are exaggerated in a way he knows will make the kids laugh. That type of genuine joy in teaching has become rare, Mydei thinks, so much so that as he watches it take place right in front of him, he finds it almost bizarre. He knows he'd been like that once—happier. He would guide his students through the curriculum with a youthful enthusiasm that had been lost to time, although back then he would always be working on more and more exciting ideas to change the way they could learn.

Phainon's lessons seem just as vibrant as he is—a beaming smile on his face as he walks the students through the plan for the session, or as he demonstrates the activity. Even when he's concentrating and has a more serious look on his face, the kids seem to naturally mirror his energy; surprisingly the quieter kids that Mydei struggles to encourage to participate in group discussions join in here as well. Phainon commands everyone's attention without really trying, his laughter and instructions echoing around the hall, spilling out into the rest of the building where Mydei can hear them clearly.

Mydei has to admit to himself that after almost fifteen years of doing the same job day in day out, he's felt himself burn out slowly but surely. He still loves what he does—and despite his father originally pushing him into it, it's actually the only thing he'd ever do. Watching Phainon teach makes him feel hollow and full at the same time, and he can only hope that Phainon never loses his spark the way he did.

Mydei drags himself out of his thoughts as they begin taking a turn into a topic he wasn't expecting to mull over when he just wanted to see Phainon for a bit. He scrunches his eyes shut, a kaleidoscope of colours bursting behind his closed eyelids with the force of it. He rubs the bridge of his nose with his thumb and index finger, feeling the tension slowly seep out with the pressure.

"Y'know, you can just ask to see me instead of lurking outside, Mr Kremnos," A voice suddenly says, making Mydei jump out of his skin.

"Gods!" He exclaims, knocking his glasses clean off his face as his hands jolt from the scare.

"Oh shoot!" Phainon yells, scrambling after them to where they've slid a few metres away. Mydei is too shocked from the abrupt interruption to congratulate Phainon on censoring himself.

Phainon laughs—soft, breathy, a little nervous—as he bends down to pick up the fallen glasses. But instead of handing them back, he hesitates only a heartbeat before stepping closer. Mydei barely has time to inhale before Phainon lifts the frames with both hands, sliding them gently into place over Mydei's ears. His touch is feather-light, almost reverent with the amount of concentration in his face.

The laughter is gone now; Phainon's expression shifting into something quieter, more intent. As he adjusts the glasses, his fingertips skim across Mydei's temples, warm against his skin. He pauses when he notices a stray lock of hair caught beneath the frame, and—slowly, deliberately—he brushes it aside. His knuckles graze Mydei's cheek, sending a faint, electric feeling down his spine.

Phainon doesn't say anything, so Mydei doesn't, either. Phainon's face is close enough that he can see every detail: the faint flush painting his cheeks, the way his lashes lower, fluttering, as if he's afraid to meet Mydei's eyes too directly, the soft parting of his lips as he exhales a shaky breath. Mydei's own pulse stutters in response, something deep and gentle curling around his ribs like unruly vines.

Phainon's fingers linger a moment too long near his jaw, unsure and trembling, and a tension between them hums like a taut string. When Phainon's hand finally falls away, Mydei almost leans forward without meaning to, caught in the gravity of the younger teacher.

"There we go, all done," Phainon whispers, as if he's trying not to break the silence between them even as he speaks.

"Thank you," Mydei breathes out, the first grateful response he's ever spoken towards Phainon. He's too stunned to stop it from rolling off his tongue, too caught up in how much he wants to kiss Phainon that he feels stupid with it.

Mydei doesn't know why those words mean so much to him.

Phainon doesn't linger on him for long—he claps his hands once to gather the student's attention. "With that done, you guys go ahead. No arguing over who goes first! He points two fingers at his eyes before pointing them at the students, scanning the whole crowd with the gesture.

Everyone seems to work like a well oiled machine after that—only a few games of rock, paper, scissors are needed until the class has completed the exercise. Phainon cheers loudly once they all finish as the students all stand still and silent, waiting for the next instruction.

"Great work, everyone. No one got hurt, mentally or physically, so I'd say that's a job well done!" Phainon says, smiling when the class laughs back at his joke. "You can all head out now. Me and Mr Kremnos will handle clearing up. Mr Nikolas and Miss Cipher should already be in the changing rooms, so go straight there."

The students say their goodbyes, some lingering afterwards as if they want to come up to either of them and ask something, but ultimately they're all dragged away by their friends until everyone has cleared out. It leaves Phainon and Mydei alone on their mat, but only for a second before Phainon rushes off towards the chairs laid out on the sides of the hall. He bends over and turns off the little digital alarm clock he has set up to signal the end of the lesson.

"Why do I have to help you clear the mats away?" Mydei grumbles, but he doesn't hesitate to help anyway. He follows Phainon's lead once he's back from resetting the timer, grabbing the opposite end of the mat to stack it against the wall.

Phainon chuckles at his contradicting words and actions, but wisely doesn't say anything about it. They work in silence, and they're almost finished when Mydei sees the class walking past the hall windows on their way to the next lesson. When he looks back, he spots a hairband on the floor, making him frown. Usually the item isn't worth keeping in lost and found, but maybe Phainon could put it aside for anyone who comes looking for it? He walks off from Phainon to go pick it up—he'll hand it into the P.E office once they're done.

"Last one and then you're free," Phainon calls from across the hall.

"Just a second," Mydei says back, bending over to grab it from the floor.

A strangled sound comes from behind him, making him startle. The sudden rush of blood to his head makes him dizzy when he springs back up, turning around to face Phainon. He catches the younger teacher's eyes flickering back up from where they were focused on his ass, his expression akin to being caught red handed doing something he shouldn't have.

Mydei raises an eyebrow. "Was there something there?" He asks, and the question seems to make Phainon's entire body go red as he flinches.

"Shut up," Phainon shoots back, storming over to the last mat.

He'd assumed that Phainon was laughing at him again, like when he spilled coffee all over himself. He's suddenly very concerned that he's accidentally sat on a piece of chewing gum somehow and not noticed. Kids are disgusting and unfortunately, it's happened to him before. Mydei twists at the waist to check if there is anything there, but all it does is result in his back cracking in multiple places with the movement. He winces at the noise, but doesn't see anything on his ass that shouldn't be there.

That just makes Mydei think that he's taking the piss and that there is something stuck on his trousers after all. He pats over his behind just in case, but all he can feel are the slits for his pockets and nothing else.

Mydei narrows his eyes at the back of Phainon's head and lets it go for now, putting the hairband in his pocket before walking over to finish their job. He goes to grab onto one side of the mat, but Phainon stops him.

"Wait, I'll take that side. I don't want you walking backwards," Phainon says. Mydei relents without complaint and watches Phainon begin to make his way across the mat.

Just as Phainon takes his first step, the tip of his trainer catches on the curled up edge, and he goes flying forward.

Phainon tries to find his balance again by windmilling his arms around as he stumbles, but the full brunt of his weight slams into Mydei either way. Their foreheads knock together as they fall into each other, making them both yelp with pain. Mydei loses his footing with the sudden clash, completely taken by surprise, and all he can do in a panic is wrap his arms around Phainon's waist protectively as they fall backwards.

They land with an almighty slam. None of them move for a moment, but everything hurts with the impact immediately after landing. Of course it's just Mydei's luck they fall away from the mat and not onto it. Gods, he's going to regret this later on when he can barely move because his back is sore. He blinks his eyes open once his head stops spinning, panic surging when he feels Phainon on top of him.

He gives Phainon a little nudge, trying to get him to sit up so they can assess the damage, but Phainon doesn't move. His face is buried in Mydei's chest, hiding his expression completely away from him as Mydei tilts his head to try and see if Phainon's eyes are even open.

Awareness slams into him then, and Mydei is suddenly very conscious that he has a wriggly, very much awake Phainon lying right on top of him. Their bodies are pressed together from their chests to their shins, completely lined up. He's sure that Phainon can hear, if not feel, the way his heart begins to slam against his ribcage at the realisation.

"Phainon?" Mydei says, the name coming out strained.

Phainon shuffles his head to peer up at him, one of his cheeks pillowed on top of Mydei's chest. "You're comfy," Is all Phainon replies with, rubbing his cheek against the area as if to demonstrate his statement.

Mydei's face spasms with every emotion known to man as he can feel his nipple hardening under the stimulation. He curses himself for being so sensitive there, but he can't help it. His chest just seems to feel things more than the rest of him. Mydei suddenly wishes he had hit his head hard enough to have knocked him out cold instead of having to deal with this.

The glow catches on every strand, turning them almost golden somehow, like a faint halo crowning him. Mydei's hands slide down from his waist to settle on his thighs instead, feeling the muscles beneath his palms flexing subtly at the touch as he spreads his fingers over the material of his shorts. His glasses are barely hanging on with the change in position, dangling precariously off his face by the tips of the curved arms hooked over his ears.

Phainon's gaze feels like a trail of fire licking at his skin, as if searing the path his eyes take into his skin permanently. His whole body tingles with the sensation, his toes curling in his shoes with it. He wants to be on top of Phainon again, to feel his firm thighs beneath him, to feel his chest heaving, breathless and beautiful. He wants to sit in his lap like he was born to be there.

"Just this once," Mydei replies eventually, bottling everything up in favour of bathing in the grin Phainon gives him at his answer. He lets go of Phainon's wrists just as the other unhooks his leg from his waist.

He wants to cup Phainon's face in his hands, to trace the elegant slope of his cheekbones, to feel the warmth of those soft cheeks rounding beneath his palms—as if his touch alone could keep him safe, held, cherished. Phainon then playfully kicks him in the shin when he starts taking too long, so they hurry up and put the final mat away without any more fanfare.

"I'm free tomorrow," Mydei says, even though he technically isn't. His father had asked to see him, but he can easily just phone up the landline and say something has come up and he's no longer able to make it. His father has heard all sorts of excuses by now—and Mydei doesn't know whether he believes them or not, but he never calls him out on it.

Mydei nods in surprise. He lives near the coastal line of Okhema anyway, so he's looking forward to whether or not he recognises the place.

"I'll text you the details later then?" Phainon asks.

Mydei hums, nodding. Hope blooms in his chest, its roots taking place superficially in his heart. "I hope the offer to show off your bar tending skills still stands, too?" He asks.

Phainon snorts, waving him off. "You bet! I'll make it so you'll never be able to have a drink made by anyone else but me."

Mydei chuckles fondly, folding his arms over his chest. "Bold words. You still haven't guessed what I like to drink, have you?"

"I sure have," Phainon puffs his chest out confidently. "Pomegranate milk."

Mydei's jaw drops. "How—"

Phainon laughs, "Cipher told me. Don't worry, I'll make sure the bar we go to has some of everything so we can try a variety and see what else you like, yeah?"

"Yeah," Mydei says, breathless all over again.

"Okay, cool," Phainon says, then looks down at the floor before looking back up at Mydei through his lashes, "Then it's a date?"

Mydei's heart expands, the roots of hope burying themselves deeper and deeper until there's no way to get rid of them.

When he first got Phainon's number, he'd only sent a quick and simple 'Hey, it's Mydei.', to which Phainon had reacted to the message with a blue heart emoji that matched his contact name. It must be his thing, Mydei thought at the time. Seeing it again, directed at him, made Mydei feel like he was walking on air for the next three days straight. Usually, Mydei prefers calling—hearing the other person's voice rather than having to read their words inside his head, but he's found that with Phainon, he doesn't mind it. He can hear his voice in his head whenever he reads his texts, loud and clear, and especially when he puts little emojis next to everything.

He sinks deeper into the sofa cushions, legs tucked up beneath him and hidden under the warmth of a soft blanket as he opens his messages log. The book he'd been reading lies abandoned beside him, half slipped between the cushions where he carelessly dropped it as soon as he heard his phone buzzing with a text message. The room around him is dim and quiet, lit only by the yellowish glow of the lamp beside him, but the brightness on his screen—and the thought of Phainon—fills the space with its own kind of warmth.

As soon as he sees what Phainon's sent him, Mydei can only stare down at his phone, biting the inside of his cheek in a desperate attempt to hold back his laughter. The effort lasts all of two seconds before the laugh bursts out of him in a fast, breathy rush.

Phainon 💙 [06:47 pm]

[Image Attached]

it's you

Mydei [06:47 pm]

That's a tennis ball with a smiley face drawn on it.

Phainon 💙 [06:48 pm]

yeah but i gave it your little face tattoo

it's ur son now :-D

Mydei [06:48 pm]

Is this a new way to insult me and my tattoos?

Phainon 💙 [06:48 pm]

no i thought it was cute

not that i think ur cute or whatever… the tennis ball is

ur handsome tho

Keep digging, Phainon.

Phainon 💙 [06:50 pm]

ok sorry you and the tennis ball are both cute

HAPPY?

Mydei [06:51 pm]

Very.

Is that how you spent your afternoon instead of working?

Phainon 💙 [06:51 pm]

not hearing a 'thank you' for creating such a masterpiece???? :-(

Mydei [06:52 pm]

You're avoiding the question.

ur so mean to me

i did it on my break actually lol

Mydei [06:53 pm]

How well behaved of you. Good boy.

Phainon doesn't reply, even as almost twenty minutes pass after he's sent the last text. Mydei assumes the conversation is over, and goes to put his phone back down so he can resume reading his book, but something nags at him. He wants to keep talking to Phainon, even if that means starting a whole new conversation or forcing himself to continue the same one.

Mydei doesn't do things by halves, so he texts Phainon again:

Mydei [07:13 pm]

Phainon 💙 [07:15 pm]

i'm keeping it btw

Mydei isn't expecting the swooping feeling in his stomach at reading those words, and even though he knows it wasn't Phainon saying it to him, he still has to spend the next few minutes in silence until his heart and brain calm down. He clears his throat a few times to try and rid himself of thinking more about that, and feels silly that even for a split second he had wanted Phainon to say that he loved him too. Mydei sighs, glancing down at the book by his side. It's truly a losing game he's playing tonight, he thinks as he gets up from underneath his blanket to clamber into bed instead. His silk sheets greet him immediately, his bare skin sliding across the smooth, cool surface until he's gotten himself comfortable.

He picks up his phone again and unlocks it back into his and Phainon's chat. He sees that he's received another text while getting situated.

Phainon 💙 [07:18 pm]

oh also before i forget

He doesn't tend to explore that general vicinity much since it's on the opposite end of the city, but the bar in the review photos looks nice and relaxed. It's quite different from the places he frequents on his own or with Castorice and Cipher, but he's still looking forward to going despite the change—especially since it's somewhere Phainon picked, and the fact they'll be together as well definitely sweetens the deal.

Mydei [07:20 pm]

? do the places you usually go to have one?

if you want!

it's a kitty

Mydei turns his phone on its side so he can see it from a different angle. It takes a few moments of moving his phone around and bringing it closer and further from his face until he can finally see where Phainon is coming from.

Mydei [07:26 pm]

Cute. :3

Phainon 💙 [07:26 pm] oh my gods i'm screenshotting this and sending it to cipher lol

"Why does Phainon have Cipher's number?" Mydei mutters to himself, his mood faltering at the idea of them texting without him knowing. He knows they've gotten close enough to spend their morning and afternoon short breaks with each other, a fact in which Mydei still swears he's not jealous over, but it still stings a little. He adjusts his glasses in annoyance, frustrated at himself for feeling this way over his two friends.

Mydei [07:27 pm]

Glad I could entertain.

Phainon 💙 [07:27 pm]

yay

that was random

i don't own a suit though Mydei [07:28 pm]

Phainon 💙 [07:29 pm]

nah why would i need one

Mydei [07:29 pm]

Every man needs a good suit.

Maybe I'll take you to one of my bars sometime, just in case I don't enjoy your drinks.

Phainon 💙 [07:29 pm]

guess you'll never see me in a suit then bc you're gonna LOVE my drinks >:-)

anyway why aren't you in bed

Mydei glances at the clock on his bedside table, the red digits signalling it's just turned half past seven.

Mydei [07:30 pm]

I am.

Phainon 💙 [07:31 pm]

[Incoming Call]

Mydei gapes down at his phone, shooting up straight so he can sit properly against his headboard instead of slumping against his pillows. He winces when the fast action strains his back—it's still sore from this afternoon after tumbling around on the floor that he'd had no choice but to put multiple heat patches wherever he could reach to help soothe his muscles as soon as he'd gotten home.

He waits a few minutes to see if it stops ringing, but it keeps vibrating in his hand, his ringtone blaring out across his bedroom. Phainon really is calling him. Mydei shakily presses the accept button and holds the phone up to his ear.

"Hello?"

"Are you actually in bed right now?"

Mydei pauses at being cut off, but also at the question. "Yes, why?"

"I was just gonna make an old man joke, but you're doing it for me!" Phainon says, breaking out into the loudest laugh he's heard from the younger teacher.

"Hey!" Mydei exclaims as the spluttering laughter filters through his speakers. He's not sure if he's offended or just happy that he's made Phainon laugh—even though it's at his own expense. "Did you call me to laugh at my old bones?" He grouses.

Phainon coos at him down the phone, still laughing. "I swear I didn't. I just thought this was easier than texting, but thanks for the laugh anyway."

"Glad I could be of service again," Mydei rolls his eyes as a fond smile crosses his face. He doesn't bother dimming it or hiding it away, safe in the privacy of his own home.

He's also relieved that whatever awkwardness formed from them first speaking properly again after they'd finished clearing up the P.E hall this afternoon isn't there. Mydei is hardly willing to admit that being on top of Phainon has been on his mind since, their positions suggestive in a way that makes him feel very ashamed of doing that on school grounds, even though it was just play fighting. But something else, something deeper, something more feral that he barely answers to nowadays purrs at knowing their fighting would be fun. Even though Mydei is holed up in bed with an aching back and creaky knees, he doesn't regret it at all.

He clears his throat as his skin prickles with heat at remembering the way Phainon felt beneath him, and he's glad when Phainon begins speaking again:

"I actually called to talk about tomorrow," Phainon says, the humour in his tone melting away into something softer. "I'm… really excited to see you."

Phainon's voice sounds different through the phone—gentler, but no less boyish, like he's trying to keep his words just between him and Mydei, and he feels so close that Mydei can practically imagine lips ghosting across his ears with each word.

"Me too," Mydei replies, and for once he's glad that they can't see each other because he's still having a hard time keeping the sappy smile off his face. "You better leave the kid at home, though."

"The wh—? Oh, you mean Mydei Junior?"

"You couldn't have called him literally anything else?" Mydei says flatly, an eyebrow twitching in annoyance.

"Why not? Is that name already taken?" Phainon says, and Mydei can hear the leer in his voice as he says it and he can picture him waggling his eyebrows at the same time too, his eyes twinkling with mischief.

Mydei scoffs, "Put it this way— even if I did name it, I don't think it'd be called Junior."

Phainon goes so quiet that Mydei thinks he's been hung up on. But when he checks the phone call, it's still ongoing, the little timer ticking upwards. "Are you okay?" Mydei asks, concerned.

"Yes!" Phainon practically squeaks, "I— uh, accidentally muted my phone, sorry." He clears his throat and his tone evens out again as he speaks once more: "Do you seriously go to bars where there's a dress code, by the way?"

Mydei sighs quietly, "You do realise that this city is full of retired old people with too much time and money on their hands, right? It's either bars or the communal baths they frequent, so of course there's a dress code."

Phainon huffs a laugh, "I bet you fit right in, too. You probably sleep in a suit."

Mydei glances down at his bare chest, and then even lower to where he can see the waistband of his silk sleeping trousers peeking above his quilt. "No, I wear pyjamas." He says.

"You do realise this is only fuelling the old man rumours, yeah?" Phainon chortles.

Mydei bristles, "What, you don't sleep in pyjamas? And what are you imagining— I'm not sat here in a gown and nightcap!"

Phainon howls, the combined sound of him slapping his thigh in elation is enough to make Mydei pull his phone away from his ear, waiting for the younger teacher to settle down again. His laughter continues to echo through his speakers, his phone vibrating slightly with the volume even as he turns him down quickly.

"Oh my gods, that was great. Do you own those though? Wait, no— you're probably in some fur-lined plaid set instead!"

"I actually get too hot in that sort—" Phainon's laughter cuts him off with the insinuation that Mydei has worn them at some point. "But generally, I favour silk pyjamas. Happy now?"

"Fancy. Very proper of you," Phainon says, his voice wobbling slightly as he's clearly fending off more laughter.

Mydei snorts. "Definitely not. I had the heating on earlier, now it's too warm for the shirt and robe, so I don't think I'll be allowed into any bars in this state."

The line goes silent yet again, but as he goes to check to see if they're still connected again, Phainon's voice filters back through the speakers. "— fuck, shit, sorry, I muted again," His voice cuts in and out, clearly at the tail end of some very impressive expletives. He sounds winded, his words a little shaky.

"Did something happen?" Mydei asks.

"Nope!" Phainon says a bit too loudly. He chuckles, the sound nervous, "I, uh— I have to go! I hope you sleep well!"

"Phainon?!" Mydei shouts after him, but the call is actually disconnected this time.

He blinks owlishly at his phone until the screen goes dark and his reflection stares back at him. Maybe it is time to go to sleep.

"Cipher, help me," Is the first thing Mydei says as soon as he hears his call being connected.

"What?" Cipher replies groggily, "What fucking time is it?"

"It's five past seven. I need your help," Mydei replies.

"Someone better be dying, dead, or—"

"I'm meeting up with Phainon tonight for drinks," Mydei cuts her off.

The screech that comes down the phone line makes him flinch away. He patiently waits for Cipher to calm down as she spews Dolos profanities until she finally stops and he hesitantly puts the phone back to his ear again. He's pretty sure they're still ringing from his conversation with Phainon last night.

"Fucking finally! Oh my gods, Cassie, wake up right now. Mydei and Phainon are going on a date!"

"It's not—" Mydei can distantly hear Cipher waking up Castorice, yelling to him that he's now on loudspeaker. "Cipher! Stop, it's not a date."

"What do you mean it's not a date?" Cipher's voice emerges again, closer than it has any business being. Mydei's pretty sure that it's not a poor phone line causing the static, but Cipher's heavy breathing instead.

"I mean it's not a date, it's just a way for him to pay back a few favours I've done for him," Mydei explains, pacing up and down his bedroom.

"You and I are going to have a very nice, very long conversation about this later. You've been mooning over him for months and now you're telling me it's not a date?!"

"I've not been mooning, gods," Mydei snaps, rolling his eyes as he pauses in his steps.

"Mydeimos, my little prince, I'm begging you to think about my feelings here too! Why isn't this a date? You're meeting him for drinks, and then seeing where the night takes you, right?!"

"Where did you pull that scenario out of? Your ass? It's just a friendly co-worker get together, that's all."

"Then invite me along," Cipher says bluntly.

"No way," Mydei retorts.

"See! Wait, Cas— just go back to sleep actually, Mydeimos is being a fucking idiot. False alarm," Cipher says, the sound of rustling as she seemingly gets out of bed and closes a door behind her comes through the line, so Mydei waits in silence to gather his thoughts before Cipher starts talking again.

Cipher sighs once she's situated, which immediately isn't a great sign. "Do you want it to be a date?" She drawls.

"…Yes, I do," Mydei admits, voice small as though he's said something he shouldn't have.

"Then why can't it be one?" Cipher asks.

"We're not like that," Mydei replies simply because it's true. They're good friends—close friends now, he assumes—but that's all, even though his feelings are running miles ahead of him and he's not able to catch up to them to wrangle them into submission.

Cipher scoffs at his answer. "Okay."

"Okay? Is that it? No lecture or motivational speech that inevitably turns into you just insulting me?" Mydei says, eyebrow raised.

"Nope," Cipher says, and Mydei can imagine her inspecting her sharp nails out of boredom. "You'll have to pay extra for the lecture and speech, but I'll give you the insults for free. Maybe you should get your brain checked as well as your eyes, hm?"

"I was only joking about the insulting thing," Mydei says through gritted teeth, rubbing his forehead in frustration. "Can you at least help me pick what to wear?"

"Why didn't you say that earlier? Tell me where you're going!"

"A little place on the coast," Mydei says, and then explains further as he forwards over the location to Cipher so she can have a look.

Cipher suggests a few clothing items, but he shoots them down immediately. "Fine, we'll leave the leather trousers for another day… How about you just go simple then? A t-shirt with a jacket, and then a pair of jeans?"

Mydei hums in response, opening his wardrobe doors to look through his clothes himself. He spots a few potential items, like a few band t-shirts he's kept since he was in university, and a couple of pairs of jeans that are slightly worn. Not everything he owns is designer or 'fancy', a fact which he knows Phainon would be shocked to hear about. He snorts a laugh and ignores Cipher's questioning sound at the noise.

"You don't think I should wear a shirt instead?" Mydei asks. A t-shirt and jeans sounds almost too casual, and he doesn't want Phainon to think he didn't try or anything when they meet up.

"And have you out and about with it undone down to your belly button? Absolutely not! You'll kill Phainon before the date even begins!"

"Not a date," Mydei corrects immediately before the rest of the sentence sets in. "Why would seeing my chest kill him off anyway? He's seen me topless before, I don't look that bad."

Cipher curses him out, not bothering to cover any of it up. "That's not the issue. Put the black shirt down, little prince."

Mydei sheepishly lets go of the clothes hanger he was holding onto with said black shirt. "How about a band t-shirt, a pair of jeans and a leather jacket?"

"Ooh, very rock star, even in your old age," Cipher jokes, but she sounds happy at his suggestion. "Wear your hair up tonight, and make sure you do your braid extra nicely. Put in some serum that Cassie got you for your birthday last year."

"Sure thing, boss," Mydei says, rolling his eyes at the demands being fired at him.

"And then you can top it off with all your gaudy gold jewellery!" Cipher says, laughing.

"Now you're starting on my jewellery?" Mydei says, glancing at the rings, necklaces and bracelets he has on his accessories tray on his dresser. He usually only wears his mother's signet ring, but perhaps tonight he could go all out with some more. "They're vintage."

Cipher's cackling laugh echoes down the phone line, and it's the final straw. Mydei hangs up on her and chucks his phone on his bed, far away from him. He storms off into his en-suite bathroom, ignoring how much his phone is buzzing from Cipher calling and texting him as he starts up the shower.

Mydei spends the next few hours pacing around his penthouse, or sitting out on his balcony trying to calm down by watching the ferries and yachts come and go in the docks. It's barely even midday and he's ready to go—dressed up, fed and watered, and now all that's left is to dot on a bit of cologne and drive there and that'll be it.

But he's restless because he wants to see Phainon now. He wonders what Phainon's doing—if he's just as nervy as Mydei is or maybe he doesn't care much at all; their friendly get together only meaning as much as that sounds. Stupidly, Mydei wishes he could have him right here with him—out on the balcony, curled up next to each other on his swinging bench as they watch the ocean glisten in the warm sunlight. It's so peaceful on this strip of the coastline, and it's all Mydei can see as he looks onwards in a vast expanse of water and nothing else.

Despite this area being popular with tourists, Mydei is high up enough in his top storey apartment that it all disappears amongst the sound of the breeze and the quiet squeaking of metal springs as he swings back and forth in his chair. It's extremely soothing, and he's glad he bought this thing even if it was a little pricey. He enjoys sitting out here when the sun is about to set as he reads a book, the weather mild and pleasant enough that he can get away with wearing a thin jumper and shorts.

The more he thinks about it, the worse he feels. Having Phainon right next to him would mean inviting him into his apartment—his home—and guiding him through the bedroom and out through the French doors to be able to get to his balcony. The thought of Phainon being in his living space, let alone in his bedroom, even if just for a split second, sends Mydei into a tailspin.

Mydei scrubs his hands over his face, thankful he doesn't need to mind his glasses as he's opted for contacts today. He lets the darkness of his palms over his eyes try and calm him, the sound of the ocean and the breeze assisting in the only way they can. It's easier to want Phainon in a purely physical way—only having to think about tearing his clothes off and having a good few hours together and then moving on—but wanting something more than that is a completely different thing, and a game he hasn't played in a while.

He hadn't been lying to Cipher when he told her that it wasn't a date—it can't be. It was just a figure of speech, that's all. They could've said 'it's a plan' and it would've meant the exact same thing. But he also hadn't been lying when he told Cipher that he wants it to be a date anyway, despite all his hang ups and concerns.

Mydei feels past his prime now. Just a grumpy old man who's trying to keep up with the energetic, almost fresh out of university graduate. He can't hide the way he's ageing, with his silver strands that thread through the blonde, his crow's feet and his aching knees, but he doesn't find it anything to be ashamed of. Well, most of the time, anyway. Being near Phainon has brought out more sides to him than he thought was possible—especially considering he's almost forty now and hasn't acted like this since he was a teenager. If Phainon even liked men to begin with, it wouldn't be him; it'd be one of those young gym fanatics that he follows on Instagram, or at least someone whose knees don't crack every time they stand up, and someone who isn't going grey all over.

Mydei leans back in his chair, letting the soothing back and forth movement of the swing relax him and get him out of his own head. There's no denying there's attraction there, especially for him, but he's still not entirely sure about Phainon. Sometimes he feels it—the spark between them that's so strong it feels impossible to think that it's not mutual, but Mydei isn't the type of man who likes to assume without concrete facts.

His phone starts buzzing again, taking him out of his reverie. Mydei considers ignoring it—it's probably just Cipher or Castorice trying to get a hold of him after this morning—but he supposes he should at least reply to get them off his back while he stews for a while. Mydei pulls out his phone and it's not until he's pressed on one of the random notifications that he realises that it's not Cipher or Castorice texting him, it's Phainon.

Mydei's heart rate is probably breaking a world record right now, and he's very glad that he's sat down as he watches an influx of photos arrive. He taps on each one, taking his time looking and marvelling at how talented Phainon seems to be at photography. He hadn't expected that, and maybe he's biased at this point, but all the photographs are beautifully coloured and framed in a way that makes him feel warm, a small smile appearing on his face as he swipes through them all as they come.

There's one of a blue morning sky, not a cloud present. Then there's one of a cat that's sprawled out on the pavement, showing its belly and wanting fuss. One of a sandcastle he assumes Phainon built—it even has little windows and spires, along with a photo of a massive ice cream cone that's practically overflowing with scoops of different flavoured ice creams with a massive bite taken out of the side. Last of all, one that Mydei can't seem to swipe past even when he tries, is a photo of Phainon himself.

Mydei almost drops his phone when it sets in what he's looking at, and he shoves his face so close to the screen that he goes cross-eyed and fogs up his screen as he breathes harshly.

In the photo, Phainon is relaxing on the beach, wearing nothing but a yellow loose vest top that barely covers anything up and a pair of knee length board shorts in the colour purple. He didn't even know they made clothes in such colours, and it's an especially garish combo to put together, but Mydei supposes that he could've just thrown together the outfit in a rush?

Anyway, all Mydei can see is miles of bare skin as he takes in the rest of the photo. The hems of the vest are all pulled and worn, and the neckline is so low that it makes his collarbones visible. It's then that Mydei spots something he's never seen before: another tattoo. It's a simple one, a clean semi-circle line made of gold that dips down his chest. One of the straps has fallen off his shoulder, too loose to stay up, and it feels like Mydei shouldn't be allowed to witness this—the strong corded muscles of his arms flexing and contrasting with his delicate decolletage.

Phainon's leaning back on his forearms, elbows digging into the sand to support his weight. He's got one leg stretched out, the other bent at the knee in a way that allows his shorts to gape loosely around his thigh teasingly. The sun that's beaming directly on him makes him positively glow, and there's a thin layer of sweat covering his pale skin from the heat.

Mydei's heart aches with how beautiful Phainon is; the half-lidded, serene expression on his face with the tiniest smile accompanying it is almost too much for him to handle. Mydei swallows down pooling saliva in his mouth a few times, despite his throat feeling drier than ever. He doesn't even have to be beaming wide with a smile to glow, it seems.

He only comes back to himself when he realises that someone else has clearly taken the photo, causing a terrible spike of jealousy. Who is close enough to see Phainon like this? Who's Phainon even smiling at—the person behind the camera? Questions like this continue flooding in until shame overtakes it, especially since he realises the photo has come with a caption: my sister took this one lol

Mydei shakily taps on the photo to enlarge it, barely resisting the urge to pinch and zoom in on every pixel as he hovers his finger over the save button. He wants to set it as his lock and home screen wallpaper so he can see it every time his phone lights up, or when he's scrolling through his apps looking for the one he wants to use. As a compromise, he allows himself to use the photo as Phainon's contact photo instead, and even in the form of a tiny circle at the top of their conversation, it doesn't dim how utterly radiant Phainon is.

Mydei's phone chimes with another text message, and his heart almost beats out of his chest at the thought of another photo of Phainon coming through. Much to his dismay, or his saving grace, it's just a normal text.

Phainon 💙 [12:13 pm]

hey, don't leave me on read :-(

Mydei [12:13 pm]

Sorry. I was still looking at the photos.

Phainon 💙 [12:13 pm] send me one back

Mydei freezes at that. Should he take a photo of himself and send it over? He's not a very skilled 'selfie taker', as it were, so instead he opens the camera to take a photo of the scenery instead. The photo catches his balcony railing, the black iron contrasting against the cloudless blue sky that stretches on endlessly, melting in with the darker ocean before him.

Mydei [12:16 pm]

[Photo]

Here.

Phainon 💙 [12:16 pm]

whoa nice! i love it

which one of mine did you like the best? :-)

Mydei could lie. He could blag his way out and say it was the cat, or say how much he loves looking at the clear blue skies on a warm day too. Maybe, even, he could say that he wishes he could have a bite out of Phainon's ice cream cone, and ask him which flavour was his favourite. All those would be safe, pleasant ways of striking up a conversation without too much risk on his behalf.

But this time, he wants to tell the truth.

Mydei [12:18 pm]

The one of you.

"You sound so regal, just like a little prince," Phainon replies, laughing quietly. "So el— eloquent—"

"You said that correctly," Mydei comments, chuckling when he gets a glare in response.

"Anyway, it's what ended up holding me back. Staying there. So… Yeah, I'm glad I'm here, and I'm always gonna be grateful for what you did for me when I first started at school. I really thought I messed up and it was all over for me, but you got me through it. Then you defended me against your dad, and reassured me after… I definitely didn't thank you enough back then," Phainon takes a deep breath and stretches out his legs, wiggling his feet to dig his heels into the sand. "So thank you, Mydei."

Mydei feels his cheeks warm as the waves lick dangerously at their outstretched legs, but Phainon doesn't seem to care, so neither does he. He feels slightly embarrassed at such an honest thanks. "Of course I defended you against him, he was out of order, and we're… friends, so you don't need to thank me."

"Friends, yeah," Phainon sighs, almost wistfully, and Mydei wonders what he's thinking about. He almost feels like he's said something wrong. "I miss loads of things from Aedes Elysiae though. Like the fishing, the cows and the chickens… my parents, Cyrene… Even though it's better that I left."

"Is your relationship good with your parents?" Mydei asks, curious.

"Sure is! I love them," Phainon replies, beaming at Mydei. He can tell instantly that he means it—that he truly loves his parents, and they love him just as equally back, their darling son.

It makes Mydei wonder if he ever loved his father. Maybe as a child before he was old enough to understand his controlling ways, he did. Maybe before he could even say the word father, that's when it happened. He wonders if his father loved him, either. Maybe when he was easier to impress, easier to control and manipulate and mould. He wonders if his father loved his mother, too, or if it was always a complicated mess that was presented to him.

Mydei shuffles closer to Phainon, not caring if the sand beneath him smears across his jeans or as the wetness of it completely ruins the material. He just finds himself suddenly desperate for a point of contact between him and Phainon, so he forces their shoulders to knock gently against one another, bridging the gap and causing the pit in his stomach to ease up, especially when Phainon shoots him a confused smile.

"Did you have fun with your sister today?" Mydei asks, wanting to keep talking.

"I did! We spent hours on the beach today, I'm surprised I didn't burn. I don't tend to tan, so…" He trails off with a nervous laugh. "Maybe during summer you'll see me looking like a scorched lobster."

During the summer, Mydei thinks, when the kids are all off for the holidays and there's no school. Maybe then they'll still meet up, seeing each other as much as weekly to make up for the lack of seeing each other during school time. The thought sets Mydei's stomach a flutter, a thousand butterflies exploding as he gets carried away with the subtle implications. Phainon probably just meant in general—like, when he returns off the summer holidays and he's still burnt to a crisp, not having seen Mydei at all for the past six weeks. But he wants to see Phainon even when they're off, although weekly or anything less wouldn't be enough for him. He's been spoiled by seeing this man five out of seven days a week.

"I'll be sure to take plenty of photos of you looking like that," Mydei replies. "But Cyrene sounds lovely."

Phainon sits there quietly and searches his face, the moonlight reflecting in those blue eyes and illuminating them in a way he thought only possible in fairy tales. Mydei is completely enchanted as he looks into them, unable to tear his gaze away. They shine so brightly, brighter than the moon itself, and he can tell that Phainon is starting to smile just by the way his eyes are curving upwards, not needing to look at his mouth.

"You're a good friend," Phainon murmurs.

Mydei scoffs, his heart feeling as though it's being squeezed as he thinks about all the totally 'not friendly' things he's thought about Phainon. He glances away, staring down at his hands. "Hardly."

He has to look away briefly because Phainon looks at him like he's seeing right through his body and soul—peeling back every layer of protection he's built up over the years to actually see him in his entirety. It doesn't last long, he can still feel Phainon's gaze on him, so he looks back, connecting their eyes once more.

"You are. Even if you don't think so, you put up with me all the time," Phainon laughs as he sways to the side to nudge their shoulders together again. "So you're not allowed to argue."

"Not even a little bit?" Mydei asks, nudging Phainon back. Even though he doesn't agree that he's a 'good friend' in the slightest—he can't be with how much he wants Phainon in ways that aren't platonic, he doesn't say anything else, not wanting to ruin the tranquility that's settled between them.

"Being around you makes me happy. What else do you need to be good at when you're friends?" Phainon says.

Mydei stares at him, long and hard, letting the truth of the statement settle in as it finally makes everything click into place; being around Phainon makes him happy, too. With every glance, every touch, and every laugh that Phainon has given him over these past few months feels like nothing but a drop in the ocean compared to this moment. The ease they've always had when they talk, the conversations coming so naturally he's never had to scramble to find something new to bring up. The teasing, the silly talks, the way he lets Phainon run amok around him just because. Even the silences between them are comfortable, like there's no pressure to try and keep something going when there's nothing to say. He's more than happy sitting next to Phainon in the staffroom on the worn leather sofa as he does his crossword puzzle all while Phainon taps away happily on his phone until the bell rings.

He'd been subtly hoping and praying that what he felt towards Phainon was nothing more than sexual attraction—or something that would wear off just as quickly if he waited long enough—but no amount of waiting will remove this feeling from his heart. He wants to do things he hasn't even thought about in years, like taking Phainon on more dates around Okhema, showing him all the niche tourist places that will hopefully stock a bunch of relics and antiques for him to look at. He wants to hold his hand, to hug him when he's happy or sad, to kiss him better when he's ill, to fuss over him until Phainon gets all huffy and tells him off. He wants to cook them breakfast, lunch and dinner—sharing stories and jokes and laughter as they eat. He wants, he wants, he wants.

Mydei wouldn't even mind being made fun of—about his age, the way he dresses, the way he speaks, all as long as it makes Phainon laugh, never taking his eyes off of him.

He'd do it all a million times over if it makes Phainon happy.

"What are you thinking about?" Phainon asks him, voice impossibly soft.

"You." Mydei replies without hesitating, sitting back on his hands, letting the sand hold his weight up even as it scratches against his palms.

Phainon's eyes only curve upwards even more as his smile widens, "Funny. I was thinking about you too."

Mydei's breath stutters, his heart pausing while also racing at the same time. The only sound between them is the gentle lapping of the ocean as neither of them speak, not even the sound of their breathing can be heard, as though they're both holding their breaths. Phainon blinks up at him slowly, those snowy white lashes fluttering so sweetly against the sudden gust of wind that Mydei can't help but be reeled in.

The tips of their noses bump against each other, but Phainon doesn't flinch back like Mydei assumed, nor does he tell him to stop. Instead, he keeps watching, gaze as saccharine as the drinks he made for them, even as their breaths begin to mingle from their close proximity. Mydei feels like he's in a daze, the fruity scent from Phainon's hair wax completely cancelling out the salty sea air between them. It's addicting in a way that he'd be happy to never have fresh air again if all he could smell was Phainon instead.

Mydei only needs to close in an extra inch or so and he'd be there, with his lips on Phainon's like he's been dreaming about and wanting ever since he first saw him, or in all those moments where he'd feel like a magnet was pulling them closer together. He can't make sense of it all—why Phainon hasn't shoved him away yet, asked what the hells he was doing, or started getting angry at him for being so close. Because instead of all that, he looks like he's waiting.

Swallowing past the lump in his throat, he feels his pulse even in his fingertips as they dig into the ground, the grains of sand getting stuck underneath his trimmed nails. Phainon tilts his head ever so slightly so that their noses slot against each other perfectly. It makes Mydei hesitate—the air between them feels so hot and electric that it's almost stifling, his whole body rippling with goosebumps. He can feel Phainon shivering against him, whether from the cold wind or from something else, he's not sure. But it's enough to make him move forward to brush their lips against each other anyway.

Mydei's eyelids begin to fall shut so he can finally—finally—kiss him, the culmination of months worth of feelings overflowing, pouring out of him and through his lips as he kisses Phainon. Phainon surges the rest of the way and it's done, their mouths are fully on each other, encapsulated. The gentle press of lips makes Mydei gasp, and he can't move for a few moments from shock. Phainon goes to pull away, a horrid, disappointed sound escaping him as he does so, but Mydei immediately cups his jaw in panic to make him stay put. He doesn't want to hear that sound again coming from Phainon, not if he can help it.

Phainon doesn't move again, leaning into his palm instead. He's so dazed from the feeling of actually kissing him that he doesn't notice at first that he's getting wet sand all over Phainon's face until he feels the scrape of grains against his hand. It shocks him again then that this is real. He's really kissing Phainon, on the beach, out in the open with the moonlight as their only witness.

It's chaste, their lips not moving quite yet, as Mydei is too scared to deepen it as if asking for more will cause Phainon to pull back for good this time and then it'll be all over. But Phainon places his hand so gently, so delicately, over Mydei's on his jaw to steady the way it's shaking, the weight and warmth of it comforting against his skin. Mydei repositions himself, tilting his head even more so he can get the angle just right to slot his bottom lip between Phainon's.

Mydei presses firmly against Phainon's lips then at the assurance that he isn't going anywhere. They begin to move in tandem, not much unlike the ocean—ebbing and flowing against each other, pressing and pushing, biting and nipping softly as they gradually melt into it more and more. Mydei can't help but run his tongue over the seam of Phainon's lips, soothing over how swollen he's already made them, desperately wanting whatever he can have and take now that he has it. Phainon opens up quickly to let him in, and Mydei feels his whimper against their lips as their tongues finally touch. He's emboldened at Phainon's response as their tongues curl together, wet and slick and addicting.

The first thing Mydei can taste is something sickly sweet, like pure syrup with a hint of coconut, and he can't help but moan at how good it tastes as he swallows it down with each swipe of his tongue and pressing of their lips. His whole body feels like it's boiling over, the base of his spine tingling and his heart thumping wildly behind his ribcage. It's blazing hot inside Phainon's mouth as he explores more, needing to reach every crevice possible as he seeks out more of the lingering sugary taste. Phainon shudders, whining high and pitchy as Mydei devours him, shuffling his body closer as Mydei licks into his mouth, slotting his fingers in between his to press his palm harder against his jaw.

Mydei loses track of time, losing himself in the taste and feel of Phainon's mouth, the plushness of his lips pressing and pushing against his. He swallows it all down, wanting more and more, his fingers itching to push Phainon back into the sand and straddle him then and there, cupping his cheeks with both hands that are covered in sand, not bothering to dust them off as all he wants is more.

The sugary sweet taste in Phainon's mouth begins to dim slightly, and Mydei chases it even harder, but it leads onto something more acidic, something more unpleasant.

The taste of alcohol.

Mydei freezes instantly, and Phainon makes a curious noise in his throat and nips at him to try and get Mydei to carry on. He can't though, because Phainon is drunk—he's kissing him after he'd practically drowned himself in shots and cocktails, so much so that he couldn't even walk in a straight line twenty minutes ago. And no amount of cool, brisk ocean breeze can fix that.

They both pull back at the same time, lips spit-slick and swollen, their chests heaving as they look at each other. Mydei can see the realisation dawning on them both, and he can feel it in the way his hand starts trembling against Phainon's jaw where it's still cupping him gently. Phainon's expression—always so open, so beautiful—shuts down and his grip around him loosens until it falls away, and Mydei lets go along with him. Phainon still looks so lovely under the pale light despite everything, eyes blown wide and lips sore and parted. The intensity of Mydei's eyes on him as he takes him in makes him look away first, his face flushed and embarrassed.

"Sorry," Phainon says, his voice muffled from where he's now covering his face with both hands. "I think I'm more drunk than I originally thought."

"Yes," Mydei says, past the stinging in his eyes and the weight of guilt consuming him as reality sets in. "Me too." He lies. Because he's not drunk —not even in the slightest—but it's easier than admitting to the younger teacher that he kissed him completely sober.

Phainon nods into his hands and Mydei lets him have a minute to himself. He looks out at the ocean again, the tide still coming and going, and Mydei realises that the world didn't stop for them when they were kissing, even though he felt as though it had.

After a few minutes, Phainon pulls his hands away from his face, turning towards Mydei again. The air feels cold again, icy and breezy as it bustles by, rustling their clothes and hair. The atmosphere has turned tentative, unsure and prickly, and Mydei has no idea what he's supposed to do now.

He clears his throat, "You've got a bit of…" He trails off, gesturing to where there's still sand sticking to Phainon's face, grains and wet smudge marks all the way up to his cheekbone.

Mydei wants to reach out and wipe it off himself just to use it as another excuse to hold Phainon in the palm of his hands, but before he can even think twice about it, Phainon's eyes are widening as he dusts it off harshly. Mydei winces from how rubbed raw his skin must feel after that, little scrapes littering across his cheek that makes the lump in his throat feel more like a boulder.

"It's getting late. We should probably head back now," Mydei says, forcing himself to talk when neither of them make a move to do so. He offers Phainon a small smile, but it falls completely flat between them.

"Yeah, sure," Phainon says, his voice frustratingly neutral.

Mydei stands up numbly, brushing the sand off the back of his legs as he watches Phainon do the same. His jacket and white trousers are completely ruined, tinged ochre and damp from the sand and still covered in grains even after he brushes it off the best he can. Mydei doesn't say anything though, doesn't dare to, as they make their way back up the hill, the entire walk completely silent.

His brain is blank, completely silent even as he tries to conjure up something—anything—to think of. Not even the thought of kissing Phainon crops up, only focusing hard enough to put one foot in front of the other until they're back at the car park, standing next to Mydei's car.

"I had a nice time," Phainon says, bravely breaching the silence. Mydei nods in agreement, feeling as though all the strings in him have been cut.

Phainon rocks back on his feet, shoving his hands into his jacket pockets. He looks nervous, antsy in a way that Mydei has never seen him before.

"Let me know when you get home?" Phainon asks.

Mydei nods again and he's sure he can feel his brain rattling around inside his head from the movement.

"And I'll see you on Monday?"

Another nod.

Phainon looks distraught, and Mydei hates himself knowing he can't make it better. "Mydei, I…"

"I'll see you on Monday," Mydei cuts him off, not wanting to hear whatever Phainon has to say, especially if it's about the kiss. If anything though, his reply makes Phainon look even more crushed.

He doesn't want to hear Phainon say what a mistake kissing him was, how inappropriate it'd been to do something like that with his co-worker, or even worse—to hear Phainon apologise despite it being Mydei's fault that it happened in the first place. But Mydei can't stop thinking about it now, how Phainon kissed back, how he wanted more, too. Yet he was drunk, and if Mydei has to hear Phainon say that it was a one-off drunken mistake, he doesn't know what he'll do.

Phainon pulls his hands out of his pockets, balling them into fists so tightly that his knuckles turn white. He blinks a few times before he squeezes his eyes shut, letting out a long breath. The muscles in Phainon's jaw are jumping with how hard he's clenching down on his teeth, and all Mydei is reminded of is how that felt beneath his palm, feeling the way Phainon's jaw worked as they kissed.

Mydei waits, confused and subdued, and when Phainon opens his eyes again, they look like the colour of steel.

"Get home safe, Mydei," Phainon says, voice trembling as he leans forward to press a soft kiss to Mydei's cheek. Mydei's eyes almost fall out of his head as he stares at Phainon in silence. He's turning steadily redder and redder with the attention, until he looks like a tomato with white hair on top.

Mydei opens his mouth to ask him what that was for, but Phainon's whole body tenses up and he runs.

"Phainon!" Mydei yells, snapping out of his daze. He tries to reach for Phainon, but he's already sped off half way up the street within a blink of an eye.

Mydei shakily reaches a hand up to press his fingertips onto the spot where Phainon had kissed him, and he doesn't know what to think anymore.

home now

Mydei [10:15 pm]

I just got home too.

night 💙
