chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Mydei kissed Phainon.

Phainon kissed him back.

Mydei's hand suddenly shoots up to his lips, touching them lightly as if that'll explain anything that occurred last night; yet it doesn't help in the slightest. He remembers them talking endlessly over drinks, sipping at things sweet and tasty, and then Phainon suggesting they sit on the beach. The rest… Well, that's the bit Mydei can't get over.

Chapter Notes

this is more of a transitional chapter in preparation of the finale!!!

enjoy! (´▽`ʃ♡ƪ)

Mydei wakes up on Sunday morning feeling like he has the worst hangover known to man—all despite not even being drunk the night before. There's a lingering queasiness in his stomach, and his head feels full of cotton. He hopes Phainon is faring better than him, considering how many empty glasses belonged to him alone, and—

Mydei kissed Phainon.

Phainon kissed him back.

Mydei's hand suddenly shoots up to his lips, touching them lightly as if that'll explain anything that occurred last night; yet it doesn't help in the slightest. He remembers them talking endlessly over drinks, sipping at things sweet and tasty, and then Phainon suggesting they sit on the beach. The rest… Well, that's the bit Mydei can't get over. The whole night replays on a constant loop inside Mydei's head, never stopping or slowing down for his heart to catch up to. It's pounding away in his chest uselessly as though he's still kissing Phainon and not just remembering it.

He's not sure how long he stays like that—fingertips touching his lips, his mind running at a thousand miles per hour—but he's shaken out of it when his phone on the nightstand starts buzzing. Mydei glances over at it, the vibrating finally stopping after a slew of messages coming through, so he braves unplugging it from the charger to see who's texting him so early.

Phainon 💙 [08:09 am]

i have something to show you

haha

[Image Attached]

mydei junior's first shopping trip

Mydei forgets his earlier panic and ruminating, and blinks at the tennis ball sitting in Phainon's shopping basket, its big eyes and red face tattoo staring up at him menacingly.

Phainon 💙 [08:11 am]

[Image Attached]

you better stock up on custard creams, they're his fave

Mydei taps on the photo to enlarge it, and it's of Mydei Junior placed precariously on a shelf, hidden amongst a large variety of biscuits. Phainon clearly has him turned towards the custard creams in particular though.

Phainon 💙 [08:14 am]

oh no

[Image Attached]

he likes pomegranate juice too

Mydei can't hold back his laugh anymore, but the sound comes out croaky from how dry his throat is. Mydei Junior is nestled up against a carton of pomegranate juice in the large fridge, and Mydei doesn't even know how to react or what facial expression he has on right now, but the ridiculousness of everything makes him feel hysterical as he begins to type out his response.

Mydei [08:16 am]

Like father, like son.

Wait, I have to stock up on his favourite food now? I thought I wasn't allowed to see him.

Phainon 💙 [08:16 am]

morning!!! :-D

also i changed my mind, we can have shared custody now

Mydei [08:17 am]

Good morning. :)

I can't wait to meet my son for the first time. Will he even recognise me?

Phainon 💙 [08:17 am]

lol dw he knows who his daddy is

Mydei goes slightly red at the wording. He wonders if Phainon is doing all this to smooth things over after last night, to put a line in the sand (although the mere thought of sand makes Mydei's stomach flip), and forget about it. He's not opposed to it, per se, as it's better than them not speaking at all.

Mydei [08:19 am]

Then what does he call you? We can't both be daddy.

Phainon 💙 [08:19 am]

he calls me qt Mydei furrows his eyebrows at that one. He mouths the letters a few times to see if he can make sense of them, but it's not until he says it aloud that he realises what it must mean.

Mydei [08:21 am]

Cutie?

Phainon 💙 [08:21 am]

aw thanks ;-)

Mydei sighs, looking at his wall with a deadpan expression, but he's not angry. He's trying to keep a smile off his face. He glances back at his phone to type again.

Mydei [08:22 am]

Phainon. Seriously?

Phainon 💙 [08:23 am]

hahahaha got youuuu hahaha

did you say it out loud as well??? hahahaha Mydei [08:24 am]

It's too early for this.

Phainon 💙 [08:24 am]

noooo don't be madddd hahaha

and it's way past your usual get up time!!

Mydei frowns, eyebrows furrowing.

Mydei [08:25 am]

I didn't sleep very well last night.

Phainon 💙 [08:26 am]

oh sorry

Despite the words in text form, he can practically hear Phainon's cautious tone—he slips into it sometimes when he teases too hard and he's not sure if Mydei is actually mad at him or not. Usually, he's never mad, although it's always good to keep the younger teacher on his toes after being victim to an onslaught of nonsense. Mydei realises how his message has perhaps come across; like what happened last night caused him not to sleep well. And while it did, it isn't Phainon's duty to feel bad about it. It was his fuck up, and Phainon has clearly forgiven him for whatever reason considering the way they're chatting via text as if nothing happened. He doesn't want to ruin this now while he can still have Phainon in his life—romantically or not.

Mydei [08:27 am]

Maybe nights out aren't my forte anymore. :)

Phainon 💙 [08:27 am]

guess i wont be taking you bar hopping with me in the town centre then

Mydei's eyes widen and he panics, typing quickly:

Mydei [08:28 am]

No i still wanna go

Phainon 💙 [08:28 am]

omg

who are you

WANNA? LOWERCASE I?

NO FULL STOP?

Mydei [08:29 am]

>:(

Phainon 💙 [08:29 am]

new emoji unlocked too wow

i'm almost honoured lol

ok, so no bar hopping on our next date

Phainon has unsent a message.

Mydei could've sworn he caught the word date, but the message is gone before he can blink. His phone chimes again, signalling another text message.

Phainon 💙 [08:31 am]

ok, so no pub crawls when we next meet. got it

He huffs a laugh.

Mydei [08:31 am]

Not if I want to be functioning for Monday morning.

Phainon 💙 [08:32 am]

what about a tea party instead?

Mydei [08:33 am]

Now we're talking. I'll take you to my favourite afternoon tea place, I think you'd enjoy the cakes there like I do.

If you'd like to go with me, that is.

Phainon 💙 [08:34 am]

YES of course i wanna go with you!!!

Mydei smiles, something small and warm curling around his ribs, invading his heart as he reads that message. He can feel Phainon's youthful enthusiasm through the screen.

Mydei [08:35 am]

Make sure to bring Mydei Junior with you then.

Phainon 💙 [08:36 am]

pretty sure you've got that one covered ;-)

haha but seriously i will, it'll be the long awaited family reunion :'-( Mydei [08:36 am]

Very funny.

Phainon 💙 [08:38 am]

you know it!

i need to go sort my shopping out now so ttyl

Mydei has to look up 'ttyl' on the internet.

Mydei [08:40 am]

TTYL.

Phainon reacts to the message with a blue heart, his signature.

Mydei sits with himself for a few moments—his heart racing from that quick glimpse of the word date before it was removed. At this point, he's convinced his brain is looking for anything to cling onto to give himself hope that there could be more between him and Phainon. Wishful thinking, he assumes, and locks his phone and hides it under his pillow. He spent the whole night tossing and turning—either the covers felt too hot and suffocating around him, or he was shivering with the cold and felt too exposed. He couldn't win at all. No matter what he did, how he lay, he was restless and uncomfortable and his brain wouldn't settle along with him.

Mydei flops back down onto his bed, shoving his face into his pillows as he tries to get the taste and feeling of Phainon's lips out of his head. He'd tasted so sweet, so addicting, and despite knowing it was from the alcohol he's consumed, a bad part of him doesn't care and would be happy to keep tasting that forever if it meant kissing Phainon again. The noises he'd made too as Mydei kissed him, the way he gripped his hand like a lifeline, as though he didn't want to ever let go. The way he opened up so easily for him, letting him lick straight into his mouth without any preamble—it all still feels so unreal that he can't process it.

The normality of their text exchange has settled the majority of his worry for now, but the clear avoidance of anything from last night being mentioned is as relieving as it is anxiety inducing. As much as the kiss itself won't leave his mind, the part where Phainon hid away and apologised stands out an equal amount. And what did the cheek kiss right before their parting mean as well? Mydei shakes his head, his grumbling muffled by the pillows he's still buried in despite the lack of oxygen making its way to his lungs. He eventually pulls back, lifting his head just enough to rest his arms underneath his chin, and he finds himself falling back asleep just like that.

Mydei is rudely awoken from his sleep by the sound of his name being screamed through his apartment and the sound of someone banging incessantly against his front door. He groans, rolling over on his bed to stare up at the ceiling. He grimaces, wiping the drool from his chin that must've leaked out at his odd sleeping position. Mydei sits up, scrubbing a hand through his messy hair as he slowly comes back to reality after his dream— he can't quite remember it now, but he knows Phainon was there in it. He wishes he could recall it, as he wants to see Phainon again already, and having him vividly portrayed in a dream is the next best thing to seeing him in person.

"Mydeimos!" A voice shouts from his front door, and the following banging scares him out of his thoughts. He sighs, burying his face into his hands in the hopes of suffocating himself. More banging and shouting commences. "We know you're in there!"

He tries to ignore the loud noises for a bit longer, hoping if he stays hidden away and quiet enough that it'll stop, but then the banging only gets louder and more frantic. He's blessed by being the only one on this level, but he's sure that his downstairs neighbours will be able to hear all of this going on at this point.

Mydei finally cracks when he hears a particularly loud shout coming from outside his door. "Stop it!" He yells, flinging the covers off of him before grabbing his glasses. He shoves them on his face and clambers out of bed, rushing towards his front door to rip it open almost off its hinges.

Cipher's hand is held half up, ready to knock again. "Oh wow," She begins, hand dropping. "You look like shit."

"Thanks," Mydei deadpans, but is thankful when Castorice smacks Cipher on the arm for the comment.

"Gonna let us in?" Cipher asks, although the question is redundant as she's already pushing past Mydei before he can answer.

Castorice pats him on the shoulder and offers him a supportive smile as she joins Cipher, albeit sliding past Mydei with a bit more finesse. Mydei sighs and closes the door behind him, listening out for the automatic clicking sound of the lock. He joins the other two, Castorice already situated at a seat around his dining table while Cipher helps herself to food in his kitchen.

"I regret giving you both permission to be let up now without prior knowledge," Mydei says, surveying the mess that Cipher is making of his kitchen. "What are you two even doing here?"

"You think we'd leave you alone after you went on a date?" Cipher scoffs, her mouth full of a croissant that she's stolen from the pastry basket on the counter as she sits back down with them.

"It wasn't a—"

"I don't want to hear you say that phrase again! Did Phainon secretly turn out to be a mass murderer or something? Why else would you look like this…" Cipher trails off and gestures to Mydei as a whole, clearly concerned even through her jabs.

"No, nothing like that," Mydei replies, rubbing his palm over his forehead as he weighs out his options. He could tell them everything that happened, play by play, and then make it end after they left the bar and as if they went their separate ways then. It'd still be technically true, after all, and they're not entitled to all of his personal business. Or he can tell them the full truth, that he'd kissed Phainon while he was horrifically drunk and now he doesn't know what they're doing anymore.

Cipher squints at him, her fangs poking out. "Did you two fuck or something? What is it?"

Mydei shoves at her shoulder in a childish outburst. "No!"

"Oh, Mydeimos, you're blushing," Castorice says softly, pinching a bit of Cipher's—no, his—croissant to pop into her mouth.

"Stop eating my food!" Mydei grouses because he is blushing and he can feel how warm his face is at the thought of them sleeping together.

"So, not a date, and there was no fucking… What the hell did you two do then?"

"We had drinks and talked," Mydei replies plainly.

"Okay…? And…?" Cipher says, dragging each word out.

"And it was nice," Mydei replies through gritted teeth.

"You're being rather obtuse, Mydeimos," Castorice says lightly.

"You mean this is like getting blood out of a stone," Cipher says, rolling her eyes as she finishes the last half of the pastry in one bite. Mydei cringes at how many crumbs go flying when she speaks: "Did you get bored of him or something?"

"Of course not! No, never, I—" Mydei cuts himself off before he can get too carried away. Even the mere idea of getting bored of Phainon sends him into a tailspin, how would that be possible?

Both Castorice and Cipher are staring at him now, mouths slightly agape. "Oh wow, you're in deep," Cipher comments.

Mydei slouches slightly, his shoulders caving inwards as the weight of last night finally catches up to him. He sighs deeply, staring at the whorls of wood patterning on his dining table. "We… kissed," Mydei admits, trying to keep his words stable.

"What?!" They both yell at the same time, wide eyed and in shock.

"Not a date, he said!" Cipher throws her hands up in the air. "Did you also enjoy a nice long walk across the beach too?!"

"Gods, no! Let me finish!" Mydei clenches his jaw, a queasy feeling filling his stomach. "Phainon was really drunk and I still kissed him."

The kitchen is quiet again, but Castorice reaches a hand out to place over Mydei's knee and gives it a gentle squeeze. Mydei offers her a small smile in response. "Did he react badly?" She asks.

"He kissed me back," Mydei replies, hanging his head in shame, his long hair coming down in waves beside his eyes so he can't see either of his friends.

"Honestly then, not seeing the problem here," Cipher comments. "Has he said anything to you about it since?"

Mydei sighs, lifting his head. "Not yet. We were texting earlier though."

"Mydeimos," Castorice begins, managing to come across calm while also extremely tired at the same time. "Why don't you just talk to him about it?"

"Because!" Mydei begins, frustrated that they're not getting it. He can't form all his thoughts into words as they get stuck in his brain, muddling themselves up.

"He's not gonna scream in your face if you bring it up," Cipher says, leaning over to grab a red apple from the fruit basket in the middle of the table. "He's a good guy, Mydeimos. Good for you."

"He is," Castorice agrees.

"But you're too scared to do anything about it now that it's getting serious," Cipher shrugs off the glare Mydei shoots her for that, instead chewing obnoxiously loud on the apple. "I'm just saying, yeah?"

"Cipher—" Castorice warns, but she's cut off.

"He is, Cas! He's finally made a move after all this time, but he's too worried about things that don't matter. You're too chickenshit to do anything actually meaningful."

"Alright, that's enough," Castorice holds her hands out, "We didn't come here to berate him, did we?" She finishes, speaking as though she's handling an unruly child. Cipher huffs and doesn't make any further comments.

Castorice turns to Mydei, her hands worrying themselves until her fingers are all linked together in knots, as though she wants to say something but is holding herself back.

"Just say it," Mydei says, exhausted and already expecting the worst. Being told off by his closest friends about his fuck-up isn't exactly how he wanted to spend his Sunday morning—but the alternative was stewing more on the kiss that shouldn't have happened, no matter how much he wanted it to.

"It's just… We haven't seen you this happy in a long time, okay? We want what's best for you and Phainon. He's our friend too," Castorice says, and Cipher nods her head in agreement, still staying silent. "When you're around him, you just… Light up, like everyone else in the room disappears as soon as you see him."

"It's really obvious too, by the way. You're terrible at hiding it," Cipher finally speaks up, giving Mydei a teasing grin.

"We're only trying to help," Castorice finishes, looking at Mydei imploringly.

Even though Castorice's little speech sounded like something from her novels, he can't help but feel supported and cornered at the same time. He looks between them, lost. "I don't know what I'm supposed to do."

"What would you like to do?" Castorice encourages.

"But keep it family friendly! We can't be hurting little Cassie's ears so early in the morning!" Cipher cackles.

"You're the one asking me earlier if we'd fucked yet!" Mydei glares at both of them when they burst into laughter. He sits back in his chair, sighing loudly enough to cut them off. "I don't know. After we kissed last night, he said he was sorry and said that he was drunker than he thought. Sounds to me that if he was sober, he wouldn't ever have done it."

Even Castorice grimaces slightly at that.

"Yeah, ouch. I still think you're being a coward though," Cipher replies, finally continuing to eat her apple.

"What did I say to you earlier?" Castorice says, a frigid smile appearing on her face as she looks at her girlfriend.

Cipher groans, her expression flattening out to repeat the words robotically as though she's reading off a script: "We're your best friends. We will love and support you either way, no matter how stupid you're being right now. We may not agree on everything or make the same choices, but that's okay too."

"I never told you to say the stupid bit," Castorice sniffs.

"I added that bit of my own volition," Cipher grins, blowing Castorice a kiss across the table. Because everything and everyone seems to be mocking him right now, Castorice pretends to catch it and presses it against her cheek, blushing sweetly at the action.

"Thanks, you two. Really feeling the love here," Mydei says flatly and stands up from his seat to go put the kettle on. "I think the ball's in his court now, and it's up to him if he wants to talk about it."

They're quiet for a few minutes as Mydei prepares them all drinks. Tea for him and Castorice, and a strong coffee for Cipher. He waits until the kettle has finished boiling before he speaks: "If he's happy to forget it and move on, then I'll just have to do the same." He shrugs.

"But you need to promise me if Phainon does want to talk about it though, you hear him out— no matter what he has to say," Castorice says.

Mydei pours the hot water into three mugs, watching the colour change as it hits the tea bags and coffee grounds. He knows that with him leaving it to Phainon to talk about first, he may never get an answer, but it's the best way to avoid any confrontation. He can hope that Phainon never mentions it again, they both carry on as if they never kissed in the first place, but then there's no closure for him, and Mydei is left to pine away for the rest of his life. Yet, with the possibility of Phainon bringing it up and telling him it was a mistake, or that he wasn't like that, or that it was all just down to him being drunk and carried away in the moment, Mydei will just have to make that sacrifice of never truly knowing in favour of saving his own feelings and heart. Call him selfish, or stupid, as Cipher put it, but as he's gotten older, he's gotten more serious about protecting himself and his peace. The idea of Phainon upsetting that more than he already has—but in a good way, mostly—makes him more nervous than it should. Where did that courage go that he was famous for?

"Sure," He finally replies, feeling distant as he hands them their drinks, ignoring the pitying look that Castorice gives him that makes it clear she knows what he's thinking.

Monday morning arrives eventually, despite how much Mydei hoped it wouldn't. Phainon hasn't texted him since Cipher and Castorice came over, and Mydei didn't reach out either, even though he wishes he did. He isn't sure how this will go now—texting is different to face to face, and he's nervous to see Phainon again. Mydei knows that he sounded normal over their messages, but what if that doesn't extend to in person? What if Phainon has changed his mind—that he thought about it more and he doesn't actually want to forgive and forget what happened between them? Mydei feels even worse than he did before their 'not-date', and it's starting to eat him alive.

Because he likes what they have now. Where Phainon grins when he sees him as he runs over and reties his scarf first thing in the morning even though he doesn't have to. He likes it when Phainon meets him in the staffroom and they chat while he makes them drinks. He likes the way Phainon laughs at his deadpan jokes, meets him halfway every time and teases him like no one has ever dared to before. He'd gotten so caught up in his feelings before he left for work he didn't trust himself to put his scarf on, so it's still hanging up on the peg by his door. It was only given a forlorn glance as Mydei left. He wants to, despite everything, still have hope that if he did wear it, that Phainon would see and things would be back to normal. But where would that leave him if that didn't happen? There's too many what-ifs, and buts, and contradicting thoughts to really make sense of it all.

A heaviness fills his heart, weighing him down as he reluctantly gets out of his car. He glances around the carpark, spotting Phainon's motorbike across the way, but no sign of the owner anywhere. Mydei heaves a sigh, leaning his hip against the car door to shield his face under the guise of pushing his glasses back up with his thumb and ring finger. He lets himself have a moment to himself as the message is crystal clear, that Phainon is here and yet he isn't, and it stings more than he thought it would. He checks his phone quickly to see if there's anything from Phainon there, but there's no texts signalling any delays or reasoning.

Mydei sets off towards reception even though he wants nothing more than to get back into his car, drive home and crawl back into bed and call in sick —except that in all his years of teaching, he's never done that—even when everything had seemingly been falling apart around him when his mother passed, even when things were at their worst with his father, and he felt he had no one left around him for support, he still soldiered on despite it all.

"Mydei!" A voice comes from behind him, making his blood freeze as he stops dead in his tracks. He hesitates to turn around, and he's so close to the entrance he can see his reflection looking back at him in the glass doors, showing him just how caught between hopeful and trepidation he looks.

He hears Phainon's feet slap against the concrete as he runs up behind him. "Where are you going?" He asks, making Mydei finally turn around.

Mydei isn't entirely sure what he was expecting when he first saw Phainon after Saturday. He pictured the world crumbling around him, shattering into a million tiny pieces that will never be able to be formed back together again—but instead, he's rendered breathless at how beautiful Phainon is. His windswept hair, his wide eyes and parted lips, and his cheeks flushed unevenly from the cold air—yet he's still only wearing those tiny shorts of his and an unzipped hoodie. He looks the same as he always does, and the familiarity of it all comforts Mydei in a way he wasn't expecting to happen when he knows how Phainon's lips feel on his.

He feels relief hit him first, and then everything he'd felt on the beach before their kiss comes flooding back; all those deep, impenetrable feelings, so much so that it makes him feel like he's drowning. Mydei almost chokes on his words: "I thought you'd already gone inside."

"No! Not without you," Phainon says, far too earnestly. "I saw the neighbourhood cat and wanted to pet her, so I got distracted…" He laughs, rubbing the back of his neck.

Mydei's heart stutters in his chest with endearment. Everything feels like it's been doubled inside of him that he almost feels it spilling out as he speaks, his words far too fond. "Did you manage to catch her before she ran off?"

"Sure did!" Phainon replies, his face brightening, and it makes Mydei's heart soar. But then Phainon's expression completely falls. "You're not wearing your scarf today?"

Mydei glances down at his bare neck, his hand coming up to touch the spot in between his collarbones as though he's only just noticed it himself rather than it being a conscious decision. Phainon stares at the exposed skin where his scarf should be, and then looks away to the ground.

Suddenly, everything is stifling between them. Mydei halfheartedly chuckles, the sound forced even to him. "It was supposed to warm up today, so I thought I'd chance it," Everything feels like it's coming out all wrong. "I clearly made the wrong choice though."

Phainon nods sullenly, and still won't look at him. Mydei misses those blue eyes focused on him, and he wants to reach out and delicately cup Phainon's chin and guide his face to look back up at him, even if just for a moment.

"I'll make sure to wear it tomorrow," Mydei says, and he's glad that finally —finally—Phainon meets his gaze again with his assurance.

"You better," Phainon points at Mydei threateningly. He still looks a little downtrodden, his eyebrows pinched and the corner of his lips down-turned slightly, but at least he's looking at Mydei again.

Mydei rolls his eyes. "Never mind that, did you hear about the performance reviews today?"

Phainon goes stock-still. Mydei should've known better than to ask such a question.

"You have your school email set up, how have you not seen the notice yet?"

"I know!" Phainon says too quickly. "I just… Don't check it very often. Or at all."

Mydei sighs, "Make sure you read your emails as soon as you get in. I don't know what time or where yours is, but I don't want you to miss it. They're the end-of-year department based reviews."

"Already?" Phainon frowns. "I can't believe how quickly the time has gone since I moved here."

Mydei huffs a laugh and reaches up to tug at Phainon's earlobe to distract him. "Stop worrying or you'll get stuck like that and get wrinkles."

"What, like you?" Phainon jokes, frowning even harder in a clear attempt to imitate Mydei's serious face. Mydei is glad he's got thick skin against Phainon's jabs and he lets them roll straight off him.

Phainon bursts into laughter seeing his unimpressed face and tickles under his chin patronisingly. Mydei glares at him and tugs even harder at his lobe out of spite, which only results in Phainon taking his chin in between his thumb and forefinger so he can use the grip to shake Mydei's head from side to side.

"Don't sulk!" Phainon cajoles.

"I wasn't— Stop it! I'm not sulking!" Mydei releases Phainon's earlobe to swat at him instead, but Phainon is laughing in the way that makes it so he can barely hold up his own body from how breathless and giddy he is, his shoulders sagging forward.

Phainon finally lets go of his chin after making him feel extremely dizzy with all the shaking and falls into him instead, resting his forehead on Mydei's shoulder to try and hide his snorts and giggles.

"You're so annoying," Mydei groans but doesn't make any move to push Phainon off of him as he begins laughing too, both their frames shaking with it.

Phainon scoffs and pulls back, his eyes glassy and bright. "You're annoying too!" He says, rubbing a fist over his eyes to try and wipe away the tears, but he ends up wincing instead.

"Did you hurt yourself?" Mydei asks, his smile immediately wiped from his face. Phainon shakes his head and keeps rubbing his eye.

"No, I got an eyelash in it," He says.

"Come here," Mydei bats his hand away because all the rubbing isn't going to do it any good. He cups Phainon's face, pulling him in closer so he can get a better look. He tilts Phainon's head back to see if he can spot it, using his thumb to gently pull down his lower lid. He stands on his tip toes to peer down to try and get a better view, turning and guiding Phainon's face in all different directions so he can check everywhere.

"I don't see anything," Mydei surmises after a few moments of looking, still intently trying to find what's causing the discomfort. His eye looks okay though, not even a little red after all the rubbing, but it's watering more than it should considering he can't see anything poking it.

Phainon's cheeks feel very warm under his palms, and when Mydei pulls back to see his whole face, he's staring at him in shock. Mydei can't help but notice how cute he looks, his cheeks all squished up in between Mydei's hands, enough to make his lips pucker slightly from the pressure.

"I think it's gone now," Phainon croaks out.

"Yeah," Mydei replies vaguely, staring down at his pouting lips.

Their faces are so close they're practically nose to nose, their breaths mingling from the proximity. Phainon's breath smells vaguely minty, probably from brushing his teeth earlier on, and Mydei swallows down the pooling saliva in his mouth at the thought of tasting it straight from his lips. Phainon's bottom lip trembles, and he presses them together before relaxing again, enough that Mydei can see his teeth and a flash of tongue. He feels that magnetic pull again, the one that begs him to come closer, to lean in and kiss Phainon stupid.

"Mr Krem— Oh, oh! I'm so sorry!" A young voice comes from behind them.

Mydei yanks himself away as fast as lightning, and takes a few steps away from Phainon so he can breathe again. He whirls around, almost losing his footing as he does it so quickly. His brain is completely frazzled from how close he was to kissing Phainon again right then and there.

"Alexandra? What's wrong?" Mydei asks, trying to clear his throat as his words come out pitchy and breathless.

"I…" She stares at them wide eyed, looking between Mydei and Phainon who's standing behind him. "I… um… Had a question about the test next week?"

"Of course," Mydei says. He turns back to Phainon, who doesn't seem to be faring any better than himself going by how red his face is, his mouth opening and closing like a goldfish. He can't even meet his eyes, staring off to the side. "I better go sort this out. I'll see you later Phai— Mr Khaslana."

Phainon nods at him, but they're practically both looking in different directions as they speak. "Lunch. I'll be there— uh, in the room. The staffroom," Phainon babbles, and Mydei is barely even processing his words as he agrees and hightails it out of there, into the building with Alexandra in tow.

Mydei doesn't have as much of a packed schedule anymore this close to exams, what with the students now being allowed free reign to either self-study or still attend whichever classes they wanted to. He's not surprised when none of his students show up to his early morning lesson, but he isn't too put out since it means he can clean up the room and create more revision worksheets for those who need or want them.

He digs around the filing cabinet to see if he can find the ones from last year to use as a basis, but no luck. He knows he left them in here though, which means he'd probably shoved them in between another folder in a rush and never bothered to organise it properly afterwards. Mydei checks his wristwatch and sees that he's still got forty-five minutes before his department meeting, so he grabs a bunch of the files in the cabinet and puts them on the nearest desk to flick through.

Mydei does this until his neck starts to ache and his fingers begin to get sore from all the page turning. He's also somehow managed to nick himself a few times while leafing through things, which just sours his mood even more. He sticks his finger in his mouth to soothe the pain slightly, but instead he tastes iron which causes him to cringe in disgust. Mydei sighs in frustration, collecting all the checked files and documents and shoves them back into the filing cabinet. He's not even sure why he's kept some of that stuff—a few pages date back almost ten years. He'll definitely sort that out later, when he's not on the brink of a headache.

As soon as he closes the drawer, listening to the aged wheels squeaking as he slams it shut, he remembers that this whole time he kept a PDF version of the sheets on his laptop for easier printing. Mydei's wasted almost half an hour at this point, and needs to breathe in and out deeply to keep the spike of frustration at bay. He storms over to his laptop, opening it forcibly until he's able to type in his password, where he finally sits down heavily in his desk chair.

Immediately, Mydei spots in the corner a notification—an email. He brings up his inbox and looks at it quizzically, confused. It's a meeting request for the review, which is strange because he already accepted it the other week. He opens it, and the red line crossed throughout the date and time stands out against the white background as he quickly realises that this is a rescheduling offer. He follows the line until he spots the new date and time in italics, and his blood runs cold when he sees that it's now being held in the East Block hall, and started almost five minutes ago.

"Shit, shit!" Mydei yells, slamming his laptop lid shut with one hand as he uses the other to yank his suit jacket off the back of his chair with the other. He leaves as quickly as he can, not even caring that he's left his satchel behind with his notebook and pens in it. If all else fails, he'll pinch a pen and a sheet of paper off of someone else.

He reaches the East Block in under two minutes, but he ran so fast that he has shooting pains going up his shins, and he's sweating slightly around his hairline and upper lip. Mydei doesn't stop until he can see the hall doors, and then he slows down to a brisk walk. He rubs a fist across his mouth to get rid of the perspiration and runs a hand through his messy hair, soothing over his braid to make sure that it's still in place.

"Gods," He pants, coming to a complete stop just before the hall windows so no one can see him. He takes in heaving breaths, adrenaline getting him more than the exercise, and straightens out his jacket quickly.

"Oh no!" Phainon's voice rings out, even all the way from down the corridor. Mydei's head shoots up as he watches Phainon come hurtling out of the P.E office, his hoodie slung over one shoulder as he tries to shove his arm through the other arm hole. He sprints towards the hall, but when he spots Mydei he skids to a stop, arms windmilling comically so he doesn't fall face first into the floor.

"Mydei?!"

"Phainon?"

They stand opposite each other on either side of the hall windows, staring unblinkingly in confusion at the other's presence.

"What the hells are you doing here?" Phainon asks, assumingly not daring to take a step forward in case he comes into view of the other teachers already in there.

"I didn't realise my review had changed time and place," Mydei says through gritted teeth, finally having caught his breath enough to talk properly.

"It's here? Right now?" Phainon questions, pointing between Mydei and the hall. "Mine's supposed to be here now too."

Mydei squints at him suspiciously, "Are you late?"

Phainon sucks his bottom lip into his mouth and looks extremely innocent, eyes widening into a pleading glance.

"How are you late and it's in your own block?!" Mydei whisper-shouts, taking a step towards Phainon while ducking down to make sure he's still out of view.

"I got distracted and Cipher didn't warn me! Why are you late?!" Phainon shouts back, huffing.

"They changed the time without me knowing, I only received the email about it!" Mydei replies.

"I thought I heard two pests outside," Cipher drawls from the doorway. Mydei isn't sure when she appeared, but she doesn't look impressed, eyes narrowed and fangs sticking out over her bottom lip. "Are you going to come inside, or carry on your lover's spat?"

"Cipher!" They both say at the same time, and Mydei can feel his cheeks heat at the insinuation.

She rolls her eyes at them and holds the door open, "Just get in here already. You're being way too noisy and disturbing everyone."

"It wasn't a lover's spat," Phainon mutters under his breath, glaring at the floor.

Mydei frowns at Phainon's tone—even though the words were quiet, he still sounded upset. Phainon walks over to follow Cipher inside, but he gets caught in the doorway as Mydei tries to go in at the same time.

"Oh, uh, you first," Phainon says, gesturing for Mydei to go in.

"No, it's fine. You go," Mydei replies.

Phainon narrows his eyes at him, "I was just trying to be nice! Go in already!"

"And I said it was fine, you go!"

"Fine," Phainon states.

"Fine," Mydei responds.

They both try to go in at the same time again, but the same thing happens but more forcefully—Mydei's shoulder catches on the doorframe and he lets out a quiet exclamation of pain, the skin smarting at the jab.

"Sorry!" Phainon says loudly, taking a step back as Mydei does so they're back outside the door.

"Oh my gods! Open the other side of the damn door if you two can't even be separated for two seconds!" Cipher yells from across the hall from where she's currently sat.

All the teachers from the P.E, Art, History and Lang & Lit departments are turned around in their seats watching them, looking caught between confusion and irritation at the commotion. Mydei spots Castorice in the crowd, and instead of looking either of those things, she looks delighted.

Phainon peers around the door and points at the way the other door is bolted shut into the floor. "Oh," He chuckles nervously and stands up straight again. "Mr Kremnos, you can just go in first."

Mydei sighs and feels a twang of pain in his temple, but he doesn't bother arguing now. "Thank you, Mr Khaslana."

Mydei's shoulder aches, and he knows he'll have a bruise form later on. At least they've finally made it into the hall without any more yelling or bashing into each other, which Mydei is very relieved for.

"I didn't know you two got together?" Nikolas from the P.E department asks loudly once they're just about to sit down in the back row together. Every single pair of eyes in the hall turns back towards them, and Phainon looks downright terrified at the sudden attention.

"We're not together," Phainon replies before Mydei can placate everyone's clear curiosity and assure them that that's not the case. But the vitriol in Phainon's voice, something he's never heard before, makes him flinch. Even during the meeting with his father, he didn't seem this… disgusted. "We're just friends."

The word 'friends' is spat out, coming out spiteful sounding and degrading, as if he'd rather call Mydei anything but that. Phainon doesn't look at him at all as he speaks, but his fists are clenched, knuckles white, and Mydei feels his stomach bottom out.

"Oh, sorry," Nikolas replies tentatively, his face scrunching up as he looks between them. Phainon's face is pinched so tightly that he looks barely recognisable.

"Phainon?" Mydei can't help but say in bewilderment at the sudden change in mood from him. Mydei knows he probably shouldn't be showing so much emotion on his face or in his tone right now considering everyone is watching them like a soap opera, but he's so confused he can't bring himself to uphold any type of image right now.

"Mydeimos," Castorice calls softly when Phainon doesn't answer, and Mydei turns to face her. Castorice looks concerned and waves him over, patting the free seat next to her in offering.

Mydei doesn't move straight away, glancing back to check on Phainon, but he's gone—already walking away to sit down at the opposite end of the line of chairs, the furthest away from Mydei he can possibly get without leaving the damn hall. Mydei feels a lump form in his throat as he looks back at Castorice who's still watching him, and he makes his way over towards her.

Mydei goes through the rest of the meeting feeling like he's been trapped in a nightmare, or something equally as terrible. His mind can't stop replaying Phainon's words—the way he spat them out, the way his face looked as he said them. Mydei doesn't understand; they were doing fine before, weren't they? They had been bickering and laughing together as usual, and Saturday feels long forgotten between them, so why at the first sign of someone insinuating anything more between them, had Phainon lashed out?

It hits him then as he tries to listen to Miss Caenis discussing next month's targets that the kiss they shared between them must really have been a drunken regret from Phainon's point of view. That's fine, Mydei tries to tell himself, but as he catches sight of Phainon out of the corner of his eye still looking down, he knows that isn't true.

The next hour feels like a decade, but as soon as their reviews are finished for each department and the individuals in them, Mydei leaves Castorice behind to rush over to catch Phainon before he leaves.

"Phainon—"

"I promised I'd help Nikolas with something, so I can't stick around," Phainon talks over him, not even bothering to turn around as he speaks.

Mydei swallows. "I was just going to ask if you were… Okay?" He says, each word wavering slightly with uncertainty.

"Yeah, I just need to go," Phainon says, and he can't see his face but his ears are turning pink. The lines of his back are tense even through his polo shirt, his hands clenched into fists once again, and despite him being only an arm's reach away, Mydei feels the width of the ocean between them.

"Oh, right. That's… fine," Mydei says.

Phainon doesn't say anything else and pushes through the hall door, leaving it to slam behind him.

When the bell rings for lunchtime, he lets the two students who turned up go immediately so he can be left in peace and quiet for a bit. He contemplates going to the staffroom regardless of how Phainon acted earlier during the meeting because he said this morning that he would be there.

After everything, Mydei still wants to see him, hopefully this time in a better mood. Although, right now he's not sure he could walk in there with Cipher and Castorice waiting to swoop in on him at the first chance to check on him—it was obvious to everyone in there that something was up between them. Mydei isn't sure he can deal with Phainon waltzing in a few minutes later and pretend that everything is fine—maybe only showing up to force himself to be around Mydei for whatever reason. Is that what's going to happen to them now? Forced proximity or gradual distance?

Mydei would rather not find out. Paperwork it is. Mydei sits down at his desk, his eyes immediately glazing over before he's even started on anything. He groans, covering his face with his palms, still being mindful enough to not let them touch his glasses—he really doesn't want to have to pull out his whole cleaning kit because he's moping. His phone begins buzzing a few minutes later, and he already knows who it is without even having to check.

I'm catching up on marking. I'll speak to you later.

Mydei turns his phone off once he sends that text, not caring if he makes Cipher mad for avoiding him. He shoves his phone into the top drawer of his desk, ready to be forgotten about. He knows that it'll only make things worse, but Mydei can't face this situation himself, let alone try and be therapised over it when he's feeling this out of sorts.

He feels a fragile sense of calm settle over him now that his phone is out of the way and he's truly alone, and focuses back on the task at hand, reaching for the smallest stack of papers first.

He's made his way through almost half of them when he hears a knock at the door. He swivels around in his chair to face the door, looking through the glass panel to see who it is. He assumes it's a student coming in for some advice, but when he sees who it actually is, his eyes widen.

Phainon catches his gaze and waves, "Mydei!" He exclaims, his voice loud even through the door. The smile on his face is wide and genuine in a way Mydei thought he'd never see directed at him again after what happened during the year review.

Mydei blinks a few times, unable to move and signal Phainon in from the amount of confusion and whiplash he's getting from the other man within the past few hours. He quickly looks at his wristwatch—it's now 12:32 pm, which means he probably went to the staffroom, saw he wasn't there, and immediately came to Mydei's classroom. His heart stutters at that thought, and he wills himself to take a deep breath before he gets up to let Phainon in.

"That's Mr Kremnos to you, especially around students," Mydei snips, sniffing haughtily as he opens the door.

"I don't see any students…" Phainon says, looking around conspiratorially. "Don't be a spoil sport, we're all friends here!"

'Friends'. That word again. It seems to be haunting him at this point, making a mockery of his feelings and only exists to rub salt into the wound. He ignores the way it makes his heart twinge painfully—how could that word have been so awful to Phainon only a few hours ago, compared to the jovial way he says it now?

Phainon leans in, nudging Mydei with his elbow good naturedly. Mydei allows it because it's better than the twisted expression that Phainon had on his face earlier on. Phainon ignores Mydei's responding scowl and barges his way into the classroom, shouldering Mydei out of the way. The younger teacher looks around, taking his time like he's window shopping and not purposely interrupting Mydei's work.

"Can I help you, Phainon?" Mydei asks, adjusting his glasses.

Phainon glances over his shoulder and grins at him, but goes straight back to snooping around. "I don't get to have my own classroom, so I wanted to see what yours was like," He says.

He wanders further into the room, combing over every inch he can see. Mydei stands up straighter with pride—he knows his classroom looks good; he keeps it clean and organised to a scary degree (minus what's been shoved into his filing cabinets), but the display boards at the back are where his true pride lies. He watches as Phainon catches sight of them, double taking, before he goes up to them for a closer look.

Phainon has a small, soft smile on his face as his eyes rake over the student's work—he's clearly just as charmed as Mydei is towards the crude but colourful mind maps and doodles of Dromases on there. There are far too many post-it notes on there than Mydei had originally wanted when making the display, but they're full of such great thoughts and ideas that he instead had painstakingly pinned each one up onto the boards. There must be at least a hundred he'd gathered across his multiple classes, and his fingers were sore and aching once he'd finished, but the excited looks his students gave him when they first saw it had made it all worth it.

Mydei sighs, giving into Phainon's curiosity about his classroom, and shuts the door behind him as the other makes it very clear he's not leaving anytime soon. He walks up beside him, eyes taking in the sight he's seen a thousand times before.

At this angle, he can't resist taking in how stunning Phainon's side profile is —from the way his nose gently slopes into an upwards curve that reminds him of the way their noses bumped against each other as they kissed, to his plush pink lips that look as soft as they feel against his own, and then to his full cheeks that he knows fit perfectly cupped in between the palms of his hands. Mydei doesn't know what to do with himself when all these thoughts come rushing in—he wants to reach out, maybe entwine their fingers together, or maybe run his fingers through Phainon's hair like he'd done when he'd fixed his helmet hair, or maybe something else entirely new. Maybe he'll press Phainon carefully up against the boards as to not disturb anything and kiss him until their knees turn to jelly.

Phainon suddenly meets his gaze, snapping him out of his useless daydreams, and the smile on his face is still there. Mydei can almost trick himself into believing that he's the cause of that smile—but it's hard to forget the coldness Phainon had showed him earlier on, and the reminder of it turns his stomach into knots as his heart sinks at the same time. He's doing it again: falling into his own mind when the cold, hard facts of what they are has been spelled out multiple times for him—

Friends.

The harsh way Phainon had said it echoes in his head.

Just friends.

"You said it was your dad who got you into teaching?" Phainon asks quietly, clearly not wanting to break the quiet atmosphere that's settled around them.

Mydei breaks their gaze and looks up at the display boards, eyes going over the work again and again so as to not be tempted back into staring at Phainon beside him. "Yeah, I didn't have much of a choice."

Mydei can still see Phainon—albeit only out of his peripheral vision as he nods along.

"I resent him for a lot of things, but never this," He reaches up a hand and smooths his fingertip across a sticker of a Dromas that one of the kids had brought in. Its skin is bright purple, and its eyes are googly and comical. It's cute. He shrugs then, faking nonchalance, but this topic always makes his skin crawl—especially when there's no alcohol to dull it. It had taken him too long, literal years of his life, to realise that his father was not the hero he thought him to be, even after his mother died.

"I don't know why he's so obsessed with me taking over the school. I've never managed to figure that one out," Mydei says honestly.

Phainon huffs a laugh, "Your dad's kind of awful anyway."

Mydei side-eyes him, "Pretty sure you're supposed to add 'no offence' somewhere in that sentence."

Phainon tilts his head in feigned innocence, a smirk playing across the corners of his lips. "You didn't say I was wrong though."

"I didn't say you were right, either."

Phainon hums, "Do you think you would've been in a rock band if you weren't a teacher?"

Mydei laughs, the sound shocking even himself. He shifts his weight over to his right leg, making him sway away from Phainon.

"Don't clam up on me now! Cipher told me you used to play electric guitar," Phainon says after Mydei makes it clear he's not going to answer. Not because he doesn't want to, but because he doesn't have an answer. Teaching is all he knows, all he wanted to do, that being in a rock band seems preposterous.

"What about you? Would you have stayed on the farm working with your family if you didn't go into teaching?" Mydei asks, turning the question back to Phainon. Phainon scowls at him pettily for being ignored, but the expression disappears soon enough, turning contemplative.

"Yeah, probably," He admits, taking a deep breath. "I love the farm and my family, and I wish I could help them out more. But they told me I was 'wasted' there, and destined for greater things, or whatever." Phainon waves his hand around, as if dismissing his parent's words. "But I found that I enjoyed running around far too much, and then I got into teaching the local kids how to swim in the lake."

Mydei hums, letting Phainon know he's still listening.

"I just found another passion in life, y'know? It doesn't make me love my parents, or their work, any less. I wanted other things, but they wanted what I wanted, and that's how it worked out. I never thought I'd pass in university, let alone make it so far as to land a job here!"

"You should be proud of yourself," Mydei says quietly, realising his voice has gone impossibly gentle. It's so easy to let himself be sucked back into Phainon's orbit when he talks like this, offering up information about his past that Mydei soaks up like a sponge. He wants to know everything that Phainon has to offer—the good, the bad, the ugly—and every detail and thing that's happened to him.

Phainon spins around on the ball of his feet and flops back against the wall next to the boards, the action causing a puff of air to lift the post-it notes up slightly before they float back down flat. He tilts his head back, letting it thunk against the wall.

"I couldn't have done it without my parents and Cyrene, they're my biggest supporters. And also Theron and Dorian—they're actually the ones who told me about the teaching job here."

"That doesn't mean that you didn't do most of it with your own strength," Mydei says, watching as Phainon's bangs get caught between his eyelashes.

"I know," Phainon beams, and Mydei's hands tremble from where they're by his side, the dire need to touch him becoming too much. "But their strength is my strength, yeah?"

He can't stop himself. Phainon is so honest, so earnest, so open with him that his hand lifts up, brushing away the soft locks out of his eye to the side. He freezes when he realises what he's done, and Phainon looks shocked from the touch. They watch each other for a few moments until it's too much, and Mydei clears his throat and quickly removes his hand, clenching it into a fist by his side instead.

Phainon blinks a few times, as if coming out of a daze. His cheeks are slightly flushed, he blushes so easily, and Mydei hates that he knows how that'd feel against the skin of his hands. He hates how warm Phainon is, how beautiful he is, how funny and charming he is, he hates it. He can't stand how much he wants him, wants to tell him how much he likes him, how much he cares for him, how much he needs him now. He hates, he hates, he hates. But he wants, and wants, and wants.

"You still haven't answered my question, by the way," Phainon reminds him.

Mydei can't bear to look at him any longer—he's too bright, too stunning, too much, and Mydei feels too exposed indulging in things he shouldn't be doing or thinking about. Never mind that they're co-workers, or the fact that there's a 13 year age difference between them, and never mind that Phainon definitely regrets their kiss—Phainon has made it clear that they're just friends. No matter what either of them say or do, no matter how many things that makes Mydei wonder if there's anything more, there just isn't.

"Class is going to be starting up again soon," Mydei says instead of replying. He adjusts his glasses despite them not having slid down his nose at all, but the gesture soothes him nonetheless.

"Mydei…" Phainon begins, clearly noticing the beginnings of the shift between them. The way he says his name is pleading, but Mydei isn't sure what he's asking for. He doesn't know what Phainon wants from him.

Mydei turns away, walking back over to his desk and leaves Phainon on his own. He shuffles a few papers around to keep him from going back and carrying on their conversation, or spilling his guts up with all his thoughts and feelings he's been keeping deep inside his heart.

"Is that all, Mr Khaslana?" He asks, the title feeling like acid on his tongue. He hates it—hates putting up these barriers between them, but he needs to remind himself that this is their situation: teachers at the same school, friends, and certainly nothing more. He can do this—he can treat Phainon like a co-worker, and like a friend when the time calls for it.

He hears Phainon sigh in frustration, and he looks up in time to see the younger teacher scrubbing a frustrated hand through his hair. "Why are you acting this way? If I'd known kissing you would've made us like this, then —"

"Like what?" Mydei snaps, cutting him off.

"Like you don't wanna be around me anymore! You're acting all weird, like… Like whenever you see me, you're in pain."

Mydei feels anger erupt inside of him, and it's so consuming and scorching hot that he raises his voice slightly: "You couldn't even look at me after the mere suggestion of us being together, acting as if it was the most revolting thing you'd ever heard. I think you're the one who doesn't want to be around me anymore!"

"That's because I was embarrassed!" Phainon shouts back, his eyebrows furrowing as he places a hand over his chest.

"I see," Mydei says, and every ounce of fight leaves him. It feels like someone else is controlling his body, speaking the words in his mind and making sure his ribcage expands and contracts to ensure he keeps breathing. He already knew deep down that's how Phainon feels now, but having it confirmed directly to him doesn't ease the hurt.

Phainon's embarrassed of Mydei.

Maybe it was due to the way they shared something on Saturday night that he couldn't stand, and then he was reminded of it when someone pointed out that they might've had something more than friendship going on between them. "I guess we shouldn't be around each other since it's embarrassing for you."

"Wait, no! Stop twisting my words, that's not what I—" Phainon takes a few stumbling steps forward, his expression so pained and open that it makes something in Mydei's chest crack.

Mydei grits his teeth so hard that his jaw aches. "If you're quite done, you should get back to your department. Wouldn't want to delay anyone's classes again."

It's a low blow and they both know it. It doesn't even mean anything either —a dig at something that happened months ago and was a one off, but he'd seen Phainon at his lowest with it—the fear, the way it'd shaken him up and made him think he wasn't worthy of continuing his career. So to use it against him… Well, Mydei never said he couldn't be cruel sometimes, even towards the person he likes. He regrets it as soon as it leaves his mouth though, and he wishes he could rewind time and take it back, but the impact of his words has clearly already landed in the way Phainon recoils like he's been physically hit.

"Fuck you, Mydeimos," Phainon spits out and storms away, slamming the door behind him so hard that the walls of his classroom tremble, just like what his hands are doing as he grips onto the stack of papers like a lifeline.

Mydei's chest heaves as he tries to calm down his breathing, his body shaking with repressed anger, frustration, and worst of all—shame. Because for the first time, Phainon had said his name right, and it was all for this.

He's messed up already, so soon after he now realises that Phainon had been the braver one and offered him an olive branch to carry on whatever normality they had left. It's like he can't stop the things he wants from crashing and burning right in front of him: his mother, his father, and now Phainon.

Mydei wants to catch up with him, to pull him into a hug and never let him go. He wants to whisper apologies and pepper kisses all over his face in hopes that Phainon will forgive him for lashing out—but the thought of being rejected again instils such a bone-deep fear in him that he can't move an inch from his spot.

Phainon just wants to be friends. But Mydei wants more. And no matter how much he wants that to be different, how much he wishes he was satisfied with being friends with the younger teacher, he can't find it in him to truly believe that. From their lingering gazes to the way they fall into each other so effortlessly, how can Mydei ignore all of that? Phainon makes him feel so alive, a whole decade younger, and he wishes it could change, but it won't.

Mydei isn't sure how he can fix things this time.

Mydeimos [12:03 pm]

Come to the staffroom.

Cipher [12:05 pm]

i'm going to kill u.

Mydei sips absentmindedly at his tea, which is a touch too cold now to taste nice but he doesn't care. It's been over two weeks since he's last seen Phainon after what happened in his classroom, and it's clear that he's finished with him. Mydei isn't surprised. He hasn't texted Phainon, and the other hasn't reached out either—why would he, when Mydei gloriously threw everything back in his face?

He spent the first week after the fight in a daze, not able to ground himself as time passed. Mydei purposely came into work even earlier than usual to avoid him, and he hasn't worn his scarf since—the memories attached to it now are too much for him to deal with. Even his students noticed, their questions of 'Mr Kremnos, are you alright?' still ring in his head as they looked between themselves in confusion and worry as he slipped up again during his lectures. He heard a few of them whispering between themselves, saying that Mr Khaslana has been acting weird too, but he didn't bother telling them off for not listening.

The second week was a lot harder; where everything had set in and he realised that he wasn't sure if he'd see or hear from Phainon ever again unless it was an accidental run-in, but it's clear that they're both staying away from each other. Mydei combs through their texts every night religiously, reading every single exchange again and again until he has them practically memorised. He can barely look at the contact photo of him as he reads over their messages, the tiny circular image of Phainon sunbathing on the beach while looking calm and serene only makes him remember how Phainon had looked the last time he'd seen him—distraught, as if his heart had been scooped out of him and he was standing there watching Mydei crush it in his hands right in front of him. The softness of the photo is too much, too soon, and it makes him feel like he isn't allowed to enjoy it anymore after how he'd hurt him so deeply.

The slamming of a tupperware box jolts him out of his thoughts. He watches as both Cipher and Castorice slide into the chairs opposite him, their faces sour and eyes narrowed. Even Castorice doesn't look pleased.

"What did you do?" Cipher hisses, voice low enough to not let anyone else in the room hear.

"Hello, you two," Mydei says plainly.

"Hello, Mydeimos. What did you do?" Castorice replies, and her voice is the flattest he's ever heard it as she echoes Cipher's question.

"I don't know what you mean," Mydei says, sniffing haughtily.

Cipher rolls her eyes and unpacks her lunch box, setting her food out in front of her. "We're grown-ups now, so just answer the bloody question. You've not shown up here in weeks, ignored all my texts, and then finally you say to meet us here and you're acting like this! We've given you space, but you better explain yourself. Now."

Mydei is tempted to remain silent out of spite, and just to see if he can outlast the cold war going on between him and Cipher now what with them glaring at each other, but with it all laid out in front of him he realises what a shit friend he's been. It's obvious they're both angry, but he's also upset with how everything went down. He can talk about it though, he doesn't need to keep it bottled up inside—these two are his best friends (his words now, not just theirs), and he wants to know what they think, even if it hurts.

"…I think Phainon hates me," Mydei replies eventually, immediately wanting to kick himself with how pathetic he sounds.

"You think or did Phainon actually tell you this?" Cipher asks, picking a grape off the vine and popping it in her mouth.

"His last words to me were fuck you, Mydeimos, before storming out of my classroom. I think it's safe to say he hates me," Mydei says forlornly.

Castorice sighs, her shoulders remaining tense. "He's not angry, Mydeimos. He's sad."

Mydei's heart stops at that—he doesn't want to imagine Phainon sad in general, he can barely even fathom it, but let alone knowing that he was the cause of it all. Having Phainon hate him would've made this a lot easier.

Cipher eyes him knowingly and sighs too. "I don't know exactly what happened, he didn't tell me, but all I got was that you both upset each other. So take yourself down a few pegs and go talk it out."

"What if it's better this way? For the both of us?"

Cipher growls at him and chucks the grape in her hand at Mydei, hitting him square in the forehead. "Don't you ever say that again. I'm not here to attend your self-fulfilling misery session, Mydeimos. You love him, so why can't you just admit that to yourself and go fucking do something about it already?"

"I don't love him!" Mydei says too loudly in the quiet of the room. He feels people turn towards him, their chairs creaking and their eyes burning into the back of his head. Castorice peers around him to glare at them all so they go back to their business. She's scary when she's serious, Mydei thinks.

"Fine," Cipher snaps, leaning over the table so she can whisper: "You like him. You like like him. Phainon and Mydei kissing in a tree, K-I-S-S-I-N-G!"

"Don't ever say that again," Mydei cringes, but the childish nursery rhyme makes him feel slightly shy about his feelings which are, despite everything, still very strong and real.

"That was the only issue?" Cipher replies incredulously. "Not the fact that I said you like like him? Or that you wanna kiss him?"

"We wouldn't be here if any of those things weren't true, would we?" Mydei replies, forcing a lightning fast sarcastic smile on his face, and Cipher mirrors it back at him before clicking her tongue in annoyance.

"I'm saying that you're mature enough to know better, and if you really want something then you actually have to put the work in. Phainon is human too — plus, he's moping all over East Block and it's killing the vibe. Go sort it out."

"So you're just mad that he's ruining the atmosphere in your block?" Mydei asks, raising an eyebrow as he sits back in his chair, crossing his arms over his chest.

"He's our friend too," Castorice pipes up, her voice a lot gentler now. "Neither of us want to see the both of you in pain because of a misunderstanding."

"Exactly," Cipher clicks her fingers. "And all I'm seeing is both of you being miserable bastards, day in, day out, and it pisses me off that this is happening when it doesn't need to."

Mydei holds Castorice's pleading gaze for a few moments before it becomes too much, and he stares down at his unfinished cup of tea instead. It's stone cold by now, but he still takes a shaky sip of it to wet his lips. "Would he even want to see me?" Mydei asks carefully.

"I'm going to pretend you're genuinely not stupid enough to ask that, and instead I'm going to insist you go and see him right now and talk."

"I don't know if I can, guys," Mydei admits.

"Sure you can, it's easy! Take your fancy designer shoes on a walk to the P.E office, fall to your knees and clasp your hands together and beg for another chance. There, done," Cipher waves her hand with a flourish, her grapes forgotten. "Actually, maybe don't drop to your knees. Phainon would like that too much, and I'm not sure your bones could take it."

"No, I mean…" Mydei trails off and adjusts his glasses in frustration, ignoring the last two crude comments out of Cipher's mouth. "I don't just want to be friends with him anymore. I can't do that."

"Okay…?" Both Cipher and Castorice say at the same time, their tone sceptical.

Mydei's irritation from that response skyrockets, "How is that okay? He's not interested and I clearly am, so it's not going to work!"

They're both so silent that Mydei chances looking back up at them to see what they're doing. They're both gaping at him in what can only be described as horror.

"Why the hells do you think that?" Cipher asks.

Mydei furrows his eyebrows, "Because he made it very clear."

"I wasn't going to say anything," Castorice begins, and she straightens up in her chair and leans over the table, grasping Mydei's hands in hers. "But I can't let this go on any longer."

"What do you mean?" Mydei asks.

"Mydeimos," Castorice says slowly, enunciating each syllable of his name. "Phainon is very much interested."

"What?" Mydei snaps, too brusque, but he's shocked. "No, he's not."

"Did he tell you he wasn't interested? That he didn't like you back?"

"No, but—"

"Then listen," Castorice says. "Phainon is an openly bisexual man. Which means he likes men, but more specifically, likes you. He's made that extremely clear to us, trust me," She pats his hand and pulls back.

"Don't act like you know everything when you haven't been subject to one of his insane rants about how beautiful you are," Cipher adds on, shuddering.

"He's bi?" Mydei squints at them. "Why didn't I know that?"

"Because he doesn't have to spell it out for everyone to just know, Mydeimos. He's not exactly been hiding his attraction towards you, right?"

Mydei sighs and pushes his glasses up again from where they've slid down slightly. He doesn't really know what to do with that—he can't play entirely obtuse and say that Phainon didn't give him subtle hints since they've known each other, but they weren't enough to fully signal to him any intent. But if he's friends with Cipher and Castorice, and they all hang out without him, then… Then maybe what they're saying is true, and he's opened up to them about his feelings for Mydei beforehand.

"Are you both being entirely truthful right now? You're not just trying to set us up?" Mydei questions, needing to know.

"Cross my heart and hope to die, if I have to hear another word about your conspicuous body, I think I might go insane," Cipher says, shuddering.

"But—" He starts, and then stops. He tries again: "But he said that he wouldn't have kissed me if he'd known it would 'make us like this', and that he was embarrassed! I know I'm not always… the best person to be around, but I—"

"He was scared," Castorice says. "He wasn't ready for his feelings, and he was worried you didn't like him back."

"What?" Mydei says in disbelief. "Did he tell you that too?"

"Sure did," Cipher says.

"Aren't you spilling too much of his private thoughts right now?" Mydei asks, suddenly feeling protective and defensive over Phainon.

"He has feelings for you, you dolt! That's no secret! Just… Go and speak to him so we don't need to keep 'spilling too much' about him," Cipher says, using air quotes.

Mydei knows that his and Phainon's… Whatever this is now, is hanging on by a thread, and he has the potential to either strengthen it or cut it off completely, but he's scared. He wishes it was as easy as they're making it out to be to just waltz over to East Block, do some grovelling and have Phainon immediately forgive him and sweep him up into a kiss to seal the deal.

"Do you trust us?" Castorice asks suddenly.

"Of course I do," Mydei replies without hesitation. He may not always believe them, per se, but if he's being asked to trust them, then that's something he'll never question.

"Then go and see Phainon and talk with him. Tell him everything, and I promise you, it will be fine," Castorice says, her voice warm and sincere.

Mydei nods, the words settling in as they give him courage and strength. He leaves the staffroom in silence after that. He can't just run over to East Block like he wants to, he still has two more classes left to teach before he can even think about it. But that's only two more hours, and then he'll be able to speak to Phainon, and maybe that will be it, their final conversation as Phainon tells Mydei he hates him and wants nothing to do with him anymore, or maybe—

Mydei doesn't let himself think about the other, more hopeful ending to that thought just yet.

chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Phainon grumbles, jutting his bottom lip out into a pout. "Gods, why do I even love a guy like you?"
